<a id="t19"></a>

# T19 — Higher-level abstractions implemented in C

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 56 | C |

**Prerequisites:** [T18](#t18), [T06](#t06).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 25 | 13 | 6 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Build higher-level abstractions from explicit state, operations and lifetime protocols. C does not require one object pattern; plain structures, opaque objects, tables, tags and cursors are choices with measurable costs. The module makes those costs and contracts visible rather than treating dynamic dispatch as an automatic improvement.

## Entry check and remediation

Complete T18 contract/ownership gates and T06 typed interface reasoning. If an abstraction hides who owns context or how a partial operation reports progress, expose those facts before adding another layer. T14 container implementation may proceed in parallel after its selected prerequisites.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t19-01"></a>

### T19.01 — Objects as state and operations

An object is state plus operations constrained by invariants; no hidden language runtime is required. Construction, active operations and destruction have separate responsibilities. Plain structs expose representation while opaque interfaces centralize invariant enforcement, so choose based on caller needs.

Investigation: Implement the same small counter/session as a plain struct and an opaque interface with explicit lifecycle.

Misconception to resolve: A function naming convention alone does not enforce object invariants.

Observable evidence: State transitions and an interface comparison showing where validation occurs. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-01-a"></a>


- **T19.01.a** Represent object state explicitly and define valid transitions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-01-b"></a>


- **T19.01.b** Separate construction, operation, and destruction responsibilities. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-01-c"></a>


- **T19.01.c** Compare plain structs with opaque object interfaces. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-02"></a>

### T19.02 — Function-table interfaces

An operation table pairs exact signatures with a context pointer. Immutable shared tables can be reused across instances while mutable state remains per instance. Optional operations require presence/version/size rules; calling a null slot is not an optional-feature policy.

Investigation: Implement two backends with one versioned operation table and a deliberately absent optional operation.

Misconception to resolve: A table entry cast cannot repair a signature mismatch.

Observable evidence: Backend conformance tests, shared-table/per-instance diagram and optional-slot checks. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-02-a"></a>


- **T19.02.a** Define operation tables with consistent signatures and context ownership. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-02-b"></a>


- **T19.02.b** Separate shared immutable tables from per-instance state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-02-c"></a>


- **T19.02.c** Version interfaces and handle optional operations deliberately. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-03"></a>

### T19.03 — Closures and callbacks

A closure-like callback pairs function and explicit context. Registration creates a lifetime relationship; removal must specify whether a callback can still be in flight. Reentry and callbacks during cancellation/destruction require a protocol, often deferred removal or generation validation.

Investigation: Build a bounded callback registry with self-removal and a destruction-time policy.

Misconception to resolve: Removing a registration does not automatically reclaim a context still used by an active callback.

Observable evidence: Registration/in-flight traces and exact context reclamation rules. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-03-a"></a>


- **T19.03.a** Pair function pointers with explicit context pointers. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-03-b"></a>


- **T19.03.b** Specify callback registration, lifetime, reentrancy, and removal. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-03-c"></a>


- **T19.03.c** Handle callbacks occurring during destruction or cancellation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01).


<a id="t19-04"></a>

### T19.04 — Generic components

Generic components move type checks and costs differently: void-pointer interfaces need runtime size/alignment/copy/destruction contracts; generated macros specialize source; _Generic selects compatible typed operations. None can ignore ownership or element lifecycle.

Investigation: Compare one fixed-capacity component in typed, void-pointer and generated forms.

Misconception to resolve: Element byte size alone is not a complete generic element contract.

Observable evidence: Diagnostics, alignment/lifecycle checks and code-size/indirection comparisons. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-04-a"></a>


- **T19.04.a** Compare void-pointer, macro-generated, and _Generic interfaces. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


<a id="t19-04-b"></a>


- **T19.04.b** Maintain element size, alignment, copy, and destruction contracts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


<a id="t19-04-c"></a>


- **T19.04.c** Evaluate compile-time diagnostics and runtime indirection costs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


<a id="t19-05"></a>

### T19.05 — Tagged unions and variants

A tagged union couples a discriminant to a permitted payload. Operations must validate that relationship and handle every alternative. Conversion should produce a new valid variant or an error variant, not reinterpret unrelated bytes through a guessed tag.

Investigation: Implement integer/text/error variants with exhaustive handling and bounded borrowed-text lifetime.

Misconception to resolve: A union’s current bytes do not identify the active logical alternative without a contract.

Observable evidence: Tag/payload checks, exhaustive dispatch and invalid-tag rejection. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-05-a"></a>


- **T19.05.a** Represent alternatives with an explicit discriminant. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


<a id="t19-05-b"></a>


- **T19.05.b** Validate tag/payload consistency and exhaustive handling. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


<a id="t19-05-c"></a>


- **T19.05.c** Implement conversion and error variants without unsafe reinterpretation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02).


<a id="t19-06"></a>

### T19.06 — State and strategy patterns

State and strategy patterns separate transition decisions from effects or configurable operations. Switches, tables and function dispatch have different visibility, extensibility and code costs. Use dynamic strategy only when variation at runtime justifies it.

Investigation: Implement one transition model with a pure core and compare switch/table dispatch plus one injected strategy.

Misconception to resolve: Adding function pointers does not inherently improve architecture or performance.

Observable evidence: Equivalent transition outputs, effect boundaries and a reasoned dispatch choice. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-06-a"></a>


- **T19.06.a** Separate transition logic from effectful operations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


<a id="t19-06-b"></a>


- **T19.06.b** Compare tables, switches, and function-based dispatch. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


<a id="t19-06-c"></a>


- **T19.06.c** Justify dynamic dispatch against simpler static alternatives. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


<a id="t19-07"></a>

### T19.07 — Iterators and ranges

An iterator specifies order, end state and mutation invalidation. Pull cursors let callers control progress; push callbacks invert that control and introduce callback lifetime/reentry obligations. Both can use bounded storage, but early stop and mutation policies must be explicit.

Investigation: Implement cursor and callback traversal over a fixed-capacity collection with epoch invalidation.

Misconception to resolve: An index within capacity is not valid after arbitrary mutation if the traversal contract forbids it.

Observable evidence: Order/early-stop cases, stale-iterator checks and bounded temporary storage. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-07-a"></a>


- **T19.07.a** Specify traversal order, mutation, and invalidation behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


<a id="t19-07-b"></a>


- **T19.07.b** Implement cursor-based and callback-based traversal. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


<a id="t19-07-c"></a>


- **T19.07.c** Compare pull and push iteration under bounded-storage requirements. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03).


<a id="t19-08"></a>

### T19.08 — Streams and composable I/O

A stream operation can report partial progress separately from terminal error or backpressure. Composing framing, checksumming and transport must preserve those distinctions and retain only explicitly owned bytes. Buffering adds capacity and flush policies, not an excuse to assume one call consumes all data.

Investigation: Compose a bounded frame/checksum writer with a short-write transport adapter.

Misconception to resolve: A successful write need not consume the entire request.

Observable evidence: Progress traces, exact reconstructed bytes and backpressure/ownership checks. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-08-a"></a>


- **T19.08.a** Define read/write contracts including partial progress and errors. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-08-b"></a>


- **T19.08.b** Compose buffering, framing, checksumming, and transport adapters. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-08-c"></a>


- **T19.08.c** Preserve backpressure and ownership across abstraction boundaries. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-09"></a>

### T19.09 — Reference and handle abstractions

Reference counts keep objects alive under a release protocol but do not prevent cycles or concurrent data races. Generation handles reject stale identities until generation exhaustion, which needs an explicit policy. Select reclamation and overflow behavior before copying references or reusing slots.

Investigation: Implement generation-counted fixed slots and analyze a reference-counted cycle as an alternative.

Misconception to resolve: Shared ownership is not concurrent access synchronization.

Observable evidence: Stale/overflow/reuse tests and separate lifetime versus access-safety claims. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-09-a"></a>


- **T19.09.a** Implement reference counting or generation-counted handles with explicit limits. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-09-b"></a>


- **T19.09.b** Analyze cycles, overflow, stale access, and reclamation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-09-c"></a>


- **T19.09.c** Separate shared ownership from concurrent access safety. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-10"></a>

### T19.10 — Abstraction cost analysis

An abstraction’s cost includes instance bytes, table bytes, indirect calls, branches, copies, allocations and cache behavior. Inspect generated code under recorded optimization, then measure relevant paths against a simpler baseline. Remove a layer only if evidence and maintainability support the change.

Investigation: Compare direct and table-dispatched versions with identical contracts and workloads.

Misconception to resolve: A microbenchmark does not justify deleting an abstraction across unrelated workloads.

Observable evidence: Size/code/resource ledger, repeated measurements and a bounded decision record. Evidence is developed in [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t19-10-a"></a>


- **T19.10.a** Inspect generated code for each dispatch and representation strategy. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-10-b"></a>


- **T19.10.b** Measure size, allocations, branches, and cache access where relevant. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).


<a id="t19-10-c"></a>


- **T19.10.c** Remove abstraction only when evidence and maintainability justify the change. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04).

## Reading guidance

- **R-hanson-cii**, **3.1 Interface** (1 h): Compare object/opaque interface responsibility.

- **R-hanson-cii**, **3.2 Implementation** (2 h): Relate the interface to a concrete representation and its costs.

- **R-kernighan-ritchie-2**, **5.11 Pointers to Functions** (1 h): Critique callback casts and retain exact modern signatures.

Read only these inspected locators as the essential spine. Additional reading time covers comparison, notes and retrieval, not an unstated whole-book assignment. Historical examples require the modern contract review stated here; draft and live-document limits remain in [guide-reading](#guide-reading).

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T19-01](#pr-t19-01) — Stateful object with operation table and callbacks (10 h, profile C, core).

- [PR-T19-02](#pr-t19-02) — Generic storage and tagged result variants (8 h, profile C, core).

- [PR-T19-03](#pr-t19-03) — Pure state strategies and two traversal styles (8 h, profile C, core).

- [PR-T19-04](#pr-t19-04) — Composable short-write stream and stable handles (12 h, profile C, core).

The project-hour total is 38 h and is already included in implementation plus verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are separate. Follow [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for conditional diagnostic and elective accounting.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Implement the abstraction without hidden ownership or progress assumptions. Demonstrate stale callback/iterator/handle rejection, partial writes and valid tagged alternatives. Defend the chosen generic/dispatch design with both diagnostics and cost evidence.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

Change backend, element type or transport chunk size after a delay. Reuse conformance tests to show semantic equivalence and revise resource bounds before optimizing.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

<a id="t20"></a>

# T20 — Modular and system architecture

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 50 | C |

**Prerequisites:** [T18](#t18), [T19](#t19).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 21 | 11 | 6 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Choose architecture by hidden decisions, ownership and observable requirements. A portable deterministic core, explicit adapters and an execution model let the same behavior move between Linux and firmware without pretending the platforms are equivalent. Architecture decisions remain hypotheses tested under changing workloads and faults.

## Entry check and remediation

Use T18 contracts and T19 state/stream/dispatch mechanisms. Draw current dependencies before adding layers. For hardware-specific execution, complete the relevant embedded laboratory prerequisites before the physical adapter run; the architecture laboratory can implement and test the core/adapter protocol with a declared synthetic backend first.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t20-01"></a>

### T20.01 — Module boundaries

A module groups cohesive responsibility and owns a decision, representation or resource. Public interfaces should reveal required behavior while hiding unstable platform details. Dependency cycles make changes and tests harder because neither side can be understood independently.

Investigation: Draw a dependency graph for a record-processing service and reorganize it around format, storage and transport decisions.

Misconception to resolve: Processing stages alone do not necessarily make good module boundaries.

Observable evidence: An acyclic interface graph and a change-impact comparison with the original decomposition. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-01-a"></a>


- **T20.01.a** Group responsibilities by cohesion and ownership. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-01-b"></a>


- **T20.01.b** Separate public interfaces from implementation and platform detail. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-01-c"></a>


- **T20.01.c** Identify cycles and unstable dependency directions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-02"></a>

### T20.02 — Mechanism and policy

Mechanism supplies a capability; policy selects how or when it is used. A queue is mechanism, drop-oldest versus reject is policy. Allocation, clock, transport and scheduling choices should be explicit parameters or configuration, with their lifetime/effect contracts preserved.

Investigation: Inject clock/transport/overload policies and compare compile-time and runtime selection.

Misconception to resolve: Hard-coded deployment decisions inside a reusable algorithm are not free simplifications when variation is required.

Observable evidence: Policy alternatives sharing mechanism tests, plus dependency and cost comparisons. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-02-a"></a>


- **T20.02.a** Distinguish reusable capability from deployment-specific choice. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-02-b"></a>


- **T20.02.b** Inject allocation, timing, transport, and scheduling policies explicitly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-02-c"></a>


- **T20.02.c** Compare compile-time and runtime policy selection. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-03"></a>

### T20.03 — Functional core and effects

A functional core maps explicit state/input to state/output; effects sit at identifiable boundaries. This enables deterministic tests without pretending a fake device is a complete emulator. The returned effect request still needs a policy for ordering, failure and ownership.

Investigation: Implement a pure record/state transform that returns output/effect requests and drive it with recorded inputs.

Misconception to resolve: Pure decision logic does not eliminate the need to handle failed effects.

Observable evidence: Deterministic replay and separate adapter-failure tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-03-a"></a>


- **T20.03.a** Move deterministic transformations behind explicit inputs and outputs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-03-b"></a>


- **T20.03.b** Keep hardware and OS effects at identifiable boundaries. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-03-c"></a>


- **T20.03.c** Design tests that exercise core logic without platform emulation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-04"></a>

### T20.04 — Ports and adapters

A port specifies semantics such as time units, partial progress, ownership and errors; adapters implement those semantics for a platform. Linux, board and test adapters can share signatures yet disagree on monotonicity, blocking or buffer retention. Conformance tests must expose those differences.

Investigation: Implement a hosted file adapter, a board-input adapter around the selected peripheral boundary and a synthetic test adapter; apply one conformance suite.

Misconception to resolve: Matching function pointer types is weaker than matching behavior.

Observable evidence: Adapter conformance records, declared environment limits and semantic equivalence at the core boundary. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-04-a"></a>


- **T20.04.a** Define contracts for files, clocks, storage, and devices. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-04-b"></a>


- **T20.04.b** Implement Linux, hardware, and test adapters independently. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-04-c"></a>


- **T20.04.c** Preserve semantics across adapters rather than only matching signatures. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-01](#pr-t20-01).


<a id="t20-05"></a>

### T20.05 — HAL, BSP, driver, and service layers

Register access belongs near a driver, board pin/clock wiring near BSP, and application meanings near a service. A vendor HAL can own substantial device mechanics, while a minimal layer owns only selected requirements. Keep register addresses, polarities and vendor types out of portable decisions.

Investigation: Map a sensor/indicator path through register, driver, board and service responsibilities, then compare vendor and minimal layer choices.

Misconception to resolve: A generic name on a register wrapper does not automatically create a useful HAL.

Observable evidence: A responsibility table, dependency direction and a portable-service header free of board layout. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-02](#pr-t20-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-05-a"></a>


- **T20.05.a** Allocate responsibility for registers, board wiring, devices, and application services. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-02](#pr-t20-02).


<a id="t20-05-b"></a>


- **T20.05.b** Compare vendor HAL use with a purpose-built minimal layer. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-02](#pr-t20-02).


<a id="t20-05-c"></a>


- **T20.05.c** Avoid leaking register assumptions into portable logic. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-02](#pr-t20-02).


<a id="t20-06"></a>

### T20.06 — Execution architecture

Superloops, event loops, tasks and thread pools differ in scheduling, queueing, ownership and latency. Choose against arrival/service assumptions and resource ceilings. A queue changes where overload occurs; it does not remove overload. Separate analytical bounds from measured latency.

Investigation: Compare a bounded event loop with a polling superloop and a task/thread-pool design for the same arrival trace.

Misconception to resolve: More threads do not inherently provide lower latency or bounded work.

Observable evidence: Queue/ownership models, overload results and a justified execution choice. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-06-a"></a>


- **T20.06.a** Compare superloops, event loops, tasks, and thread pools. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


<a id="t20-06-b"></a>


- **T20.06.b** Model queues, ownership transfer, latency, and overload. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


<a id="t20-06-c"></a>


- **T20.06.c** Choose a design against actual timing and resource constraints. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


<a id="t20-07"></a>

### T20.07 — State-machine composition

Cooperating state machines need an event-order contract, not reliance on incidental callback order. Deferred events and cancellation require identity and retention limits. Hierarchy helps when shared transitions are real, but can obscure behavior if used only to reduce switch size.

Investigation: Compose acquisition and transport machines with explicit event ordering and stale-event rejection.

Misconception to resolve: Two locally correct machines can compose incorrectly when their event/lifetime assumptions disagree.

Observable evidence: Product/cooperation traces, cancellation cases and order-perturbation tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-07-a"></a>


- **T20.07.a** Define hierarchical or cooperating machines where justified. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


<a id="t20-07-b"></a>


- **T20.07.b** Specify event ordering, deferred events, and cancellation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


<a id="t20-07-c"></a>


- **T20.07.c** Prevent accidental dependence on callback or scheduler ordering. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-03](#pr-t20-03).


<a id="t20-08"></a>

### T20.08 — Configuration architecture

Build-time features alter binaries and possibly ABI; runtime parameters alter active policy within a supported configuration. Validate both, give the configuration an identity and trace it to tests/artifacts. Avoid parallel sources of truth between generated headers and handwritten defaults.

Investigation: Generate a build identity and validate runtime capacity/time limits with versioned schemas.

Misconception to resolve: A config file being parseable does not mean its combination is supported.

Observable evidence: Invalid-combination tests and artifact-to-configuration traceability. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-08-a"></a>


- **T20.08.a** Separate build-time features from runtime parameters. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-08-b"></a>


- **T20.08.b** Validate combinations and generate documented configuration identities. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-08-c"></a>


- **T20.08.c** Keep configuration changes traceable to tests and binary artifacts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-09"></a>

### T20.09 — Fault containment

Logical modules share memory and privilege unless a real boundary says otherwise. A bad adapter can corrupt a process despite clean interfaces. Specify failure propagation, degradation and restart, then distinguish contract-checking from memory isolation. Supervision needs its own failure/resource policy.

Investigation: Inject adapter errors and malformed results, define containment within the logical model and document what requires process/MPU isolation.

Misconception to resolve: An interface boundary is not a memory-protection boundary.

Observable evidence: Fault/degradation traces and a precise isolation limit. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-09-a"></a>


- **T20.09.a** Distinguish logical boundaries from memory and privilege boundaries. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-09-b"></a>


- **T20.09.b** Specify failure propagation, degradation, restart, and supervision. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-09-c"></a>


- **T20.09.c** Test adapters that violate contracts without overstating isolation guarantees. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-10"></a>

### T20.10 — Architecture evaluation

Architecture evaluation records alternatives, assumptions and decision criteria against requirements. Trace latency, capacity, portability and recovery to concrete boundaries. Revisit the choice when workload or target changes instead of defending a diagram detached from evidence.

Investigation: Write a decision record comparing two decompositions/execution models and perturb one assumption.

Misconception to resolve: A visually tidy layering diagram does not establish fitness for the workload.

Observable evidence: Requirement-to-boundary/test mapping and a revised decision supported by the perturbation. Evidence is developed in [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t20-10-a"></a>


- **T20.10.a** Record alternatives, assumptions, and decision criteria. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-10-b"></a>


- **T20.10.b** Trace requirements to boundaries and observable behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).


<a id="t20-10-c"></a>


- **T20.10.c** Revisit decisions when workload, hardware, or safety assumptions change. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T20-04](#pr-t20-04).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Defend the dependency graph, policy injection and execution model against a changed transport, overloaded arrival stream and failed adapter. Show identical portable-core semantics across adapters with honest physical/emulated/synthetic limits. Distinguish logical containment from protection.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, replace one backend and alter the arrival rate. Update the decision record and resource ceilings, then repeat conformance and fault tests.

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

<a id="t21"></a>

# T21 — Error handling, resource management, and observability

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 53 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T18](#t18), [T20](#t20).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | 24 | 12 | 6 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Make failure behavior part of correctness. Errors carry causes, acquisition can stop partway, mutation has a guarantee, cancellation has an in-flight owner, and diagnostics consume resources. The projects connect resource rollback to bounded observability and distinguish crash evidence from validated recovery.

## Entry check and remediation

Use T18 output/lifetime contracts and T20 effect boundaries. Before coding an error path, name acquired resources and externally visible state. If cleanup is duplicated in several branches, draw the acquisition stack and verify exactly-once release before choosing a control-flow style.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t21-01"></a>

### T21.01 — Error taxonomy

Invalid external input, internal contract violation, resource exhaustion and hardware fault need different policies. Recoverable, retryable, terminal and degraded describe application outcomes, not merely numeric codes. Preserve the original operation/resource context so diagnosis can distinguish symptom from cause.

Investigation: Define an error table for parser, allocator and transport failures with recovery class and context.

Misconception to resolve: Every nonzero result should not trigger the same retry or panic policy.

Observable evidence: Error/class/action matrix and tests for at least one outcome in each category. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-01-a"></a>


- **T21.01.a** Separate invalid input, contract violations, resource failures, and hardware faults. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-01-b"></a>


- **T21.01.b** Define recoverable, retryable, terminal, and degraded outcomes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-01-c"></a>


- **T21.01.c** Preserve enough context to identify the original cause. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-02"></a>

### T21.02 — Propagation and translation

Translation maps unstable backend errors into a stable public taxonomy while retaining causal context. A component can expose a portable timeout status and store a backend detail for diagnostics. Success must not be ambiguous with partial failure, and overwriting the first cause can destroy useful evidence.

Investigation: Implement a bounded error record and backend-to-public mapping with an explicit unknown-error policy.

Misconception to resolve: Abstraction does not require discarding all cause information.

Observable evidence: Mapping tests, stable public codes and original-cause preservation across propagation. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-02-a"></a>


- **T21.02.a** Map backend errors into stable component-level results. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-02-b"></a>


- **T21.02.b** Retain causal context without exposing unstable implementation details. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-02-c"></a>


- **T21.02.c** Avoid silent information loss and ambiguous success codes. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-03"></a>

### T21.03 — Partial initialization

Partial initialization acquires a prefix of resources. Track completed stages and roll back in reverse dependency order. Repeated init/cleanup requires a state policy; a failed object may permit cleanup without permitting active operations.

Investigation: Inject failure after each of three acquisitions and check remaining ownership after rollback.

Misconception to resolve: A final “initialized” flag is insufficient to describe every intermediate owner.

Observable evidence: Acquisition/rollback traces and repeated-init/cleanup tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-03-a"></a>


- **T21.03.a** Track resource acquisition order and completed initialization stages. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-03-b"></a>


- **T21.03.b** Roll back safely after every possible failure point. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-03-c"></a>


- **T21.03.c** Test repeated initialization and cleanup under injected failures. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-04"></a>

### T21.04 — Cleanup control flow

Early returns, nested cleanup and narrowly scoped cleanup labels are tools for proving release exactly once. Choose the structure that makes resource state visible and minimizes duplicated obligations. A forward jump to cleanup can be clearer than deeply nested success paths; it is not arbitrary control flow.

Investigation: Implement the same small acquisition sequence with two cleanup structures and compare reviewability.

Misconception to resolve: A blanket goto ban or blanket goto preference does not establish correctness.

Observable evidence: Exactly-once release proof, failure-point tests and a justified style choice. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-04-a"></a>


- **T21.04.a** Compare early returns, nested cleanup, and narrowly scoped cleanup labels. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-04-b"></a>


- **T21.04.b** Establish exactly-once release for each acquired resource. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-04-c"></a>


- **T21.04.c** Choose structure by correctness and readability rather than blanket style rules. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-01](#pr-t21-01).


<a id="t21-05"></a>

### T21.05 — Transactional mutation

The strong guarantee leaves observable state unchanged on failure; the basic guarantee keeps invariants while allowing changes. Stage allocations/copies before commit where strong behavior is required. Retry is idempotent only if repeated requests cannot duplicate externally visible effects.

Investigation: Implement a staged configuration update and compare strong/basic failure contracts.

Misconception to resolve: Returning an error does not imply rollback happened.

Observable evidence: Before/after snapshots, commit-point proof and repeated-request checks. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-05-a"></a>


- **T21.05.a** Define strong, basic, and explicitly weaker failure guarantees. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-05-b"></a>


- **T21.05.b** Stage changes before committing externally visible state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-05-c"></a>


- **T21.05.c** Verify rollback and idempotent retries where promised. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-06"></a>

### T21.06 — Cancellation and timeouts

Timeout says a deadline expired; cancellation completion says the operation will no longer use retained resources. An in-flight callback can arrive after a timeout, so identify requests and define one completion owner. Context cannot be reclaimed merely because the caller stopped waiting.

Investigation: Model timeout, cancel request, late callback and cancel acknowledgment, rejecting stale/duplicate completion.

Misconception to resolve: Timeout and successful cancellation are not interchangeable.

Observable evidence: Ownership/timing traces, exactly-once completion and no stale-context access. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-06-a"></a>


- **T21.06.a** Distinguish timeout expiry from successful cancellation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-06-b"></a>


- **T21.06.b** Specify ownership of operations still in flight. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-06-c"></a>


- **T21.06.c** Prevent stale callbacks and duplicate completion reporting. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-02](#pr-t21-02).


<a id="t21-07"></a>

### T21.07 — Assertions and fault policy

Assertions check developer invariants under a fault policy; required validation must remain when assertions disappear. Decide whether a fault returns, panics, enters safe state or resets, with target-specific implications. Expressions inside removable checks must not carry required side effects.

Investigation: Build assertions on/off and inject an invalid input plus an internal invariant defect under distinct policies.

Misconception to resolve: An assert is not a durable external-input validator.

Observable evidence: Equivalent required validation, explicit fault behavior and disabled-side-effect audit. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-07-a"></a>


- **T21.07.a** Separate development assertions from required runtime validation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-07-b"></a>


- **T21.07.b** Define panic, safe-state, reset, or error-return policies explicitly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-07-c"></a>


- **T21.07.c** Audit behavior when assertion code is absent. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-08"></a>

### T21.08 — Logging and trace design

Logging uses storage, time and transport. Bounded records need severity, timestamp units, operation identity and an overflow/backpressure policy. Error reporting must not recursively allocate or fail through the same broken backend without a bounded fallback.

Investigation: Implement a fixed ring of event records with a stated drop policy and rate limit.

Misconception to resolve: More logs do not automatically improve diagnosis if they can destroy timing or recurse on failure.

Observable evidence: Exact overflow/rate traces, resource bounds and reporter-failure tests. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-08-a"></a>


- **T21.08.a** Use bounded records with severity, timestamps, and context. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-08-b"></a>


- **T21.08.b** Specify overflow, rate limiting, and transport backpressure. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-08-c"></a>


- **T21.08.c** Avoid recursive failures inside error-reporting code. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-09"></a>

### T21.09 — Developer and integrator diagnostics

White-box developer instrumentation and stable integrator diagnostics serve different audiences. Give them independent switches and supported contracts. Disabled instrumentation that promises no evaluation/storage cost needs preprocessor/code/binary evidence; a runtime if may preserve argument evaluation.

Investigation: Build four switch combinations and inspect expression counts, symbols and record storage.

Misconception to resolve: A disabled sink does not necessarily mean disabled call arguments or static buffers.

Observable evidence: Independent toggle matrix, no-evaluation checks and stable black-box output contract. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-09-a"></a>


- **T21.09.a** Separate white-box introspection from stable black-box diagnostics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-09-b"></a>


- **T21.09.b** Define independently togglable interfaces and supported contracts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-09-c"></a>


- **T21.09.c** Verify disabled instrumentation removes promised evaluation and storage costs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-03](#pr-t21-03).


<a id="t21-10"></a>

### T21.10 — Crash evidence and recovery

Crash evidence needs minimal bounded context and a build identity that resolves against matching symbols. Persistence has its own atomicity/reset/lifetime assumptions. A captured symptom supports diagnosis; recovery requires restoring validated state and testing the resumed behavior under the fault model.

Investigation: Encode/decode a small checksummed fault record and test corrupt/stale-build rejection plus a separate recovery policy.

Misconception to resolve: A readable crash record is not proof that continuing execution is safe.

Observable evidence: Corruption/build-correlation tests and recovery evidence explicitly separated from collection. Evidence is developed in [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t21-10-a"></a>


- **T21.10.a** Preserve minimal fault context in suitable storage. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).


<a id="t21-10-b"></a>


- **T21.10.b** Correlate records with build identifiers and symbol files. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).


<a id="t21-10-c"></a>


- **T21.10.c** Distinguish symptom collection from validated fault recovery. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T21-04](#pr-t21-04).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Inject every acquisition failure, one mutation failure and a timeout/late-callback sequence. Prove release and completion exactly once. Demonstrate bounded diagnostics with instrumentation disabled and distinguish recorded fault context from actual recovered correctness.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, add a resource and reduce diagnostic capacity. Re-derive rollback/overflow policies and show the original cause survives the new failure paths.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.

<a id="t22"></a>

# T22 — Production-quality libraries and repositories

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shared | core | 58 | A |

**Prerequisites:** [T18](#t18), [T21](#t21).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 26 | 14 | 6 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Turn a working component into a reviewable, consumable library. Organize source and contracts, trace requirements, test installation and FFI boundaries, pin dependencies, and release with reproducible evidence. Packaging and documentation are correctness work when they define what an independent consumer can safely assume.

## Entry check and remediation

Use T18 API contracts and T21 error/diagnostic evidence. Start from a small component already built in earlier modules, not an unrelated large repository. If an independent consumer cannot identify the public header, minimal build and ownership rules, repair those before adding release automation.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t22-01"></a>

### T22.01 — Repository organization

Separate public headers, private source, tests, examples, tools and target backends by their consumption role. A minimal supported build should not accidentally depend on the developer’s source tree or optional examples. Layout is useful when it makes boundaries obvious, not when it adds empty directories.

Investigation: Organize an earlier component and rebuild its smallest supported configuration from a clean checkout.

Misconception to resolve: A neat directory tree alone does not establish a usable library boundary.

Observable evidence: Clean-build instructions, public/private inventory and target-backend separation. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t22-01-a"></a>


- **T22.01.a** Separate public headers, private code, tests, examples, and tools. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-01-b"></a>


- **T22.01.b** Keep target-specific backends identifiable. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-01-c"></a>


- **T22.01.c** Make the minimal supported build easy to reproduce. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-02"></a>

### T22.02 — Naming and readability

Names can encode units, roles and ownership, while small explicit control flow reduces hidden state. Complexity metrics highlight review candidates rather than dictate automatic rewrites. Prefer a name that explains a domain constraint over a short ambiguous name that needs repeated comments.

Investigation: Review one interface and one failure-heavy function, rename unclear units/ownership and simplify only with preserved contracts.

Misconception to resolve: A lower branch count is not automatically clearer or safer code.

Observable evidence: Before/after review examples and behavior-preserving regression evidence. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t22-02-a"></a>


- **T22.02.a** Encode role, units, ownership, and domain meaning in names. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-02-b"></a>


- **T22.02.b** Reduce unnecessary branching and hidden state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-02-c"></a>


- **T22.02.c** Use complexity metrics to investigate code rather than replace judgment. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-03"></a>

### T22.03 — Documentation

Doxygen comments document preconditions, postconditions and resource/lifetime rules; usage examples test the public story. Rationale comments explain nonobvious invariants. Generated API references show interface details, while architecture narratives explain why boundaries and policies exist.

Investigation: Document an API, compile its usage example and write a short architecture note.

Misconception to resolve: Generated documentation does not enforce a contract or replace design rationale.

Observable evidence: Rendered references, executable examples and a consumer-readable ownership/failure narrative. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t22-03-a"></a>


- **T22.03.a** Write Doxygen-compatible contracts and usage examples. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-03-b"></a>


- **T22.03.b** Explain rationale and non-obvious invariants in comments. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-03-c"></a>


- **T22.03.c** Keep generated API references distinct from architecture narratives. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01).


<a id="t22-04"></a>

### T22.04 — Requirements and traceability

Stable requirement and test IDs connect behavior to evidence. Trace through API contracts, implementation decisions and tests, detecting requirements with no test and tests with no stated purpose. Coverage of IDs is a navigation aid; test quality still needs independent review.

Investigation: Build a bidirectional traceability table and deliberately insert one orphan requirement and one orphan test.

Misconception to resolve: A complete spreadsheet can still point to weak tests that cannot expose a defect.

Observable evidence: Orphan detection and an example test strengthened to challenge its requirement. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-02](#pr-t22-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t22-04-a"></a>


- **T22.04.a** Give requirements and tests stable identifiers. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-02](#pr-t22-02).


<a id="t22-04-b"></a>


- **T22.04.b** Link API behavior, implementation decisions, and verification evidence. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-02](#pr-t22-02).


<a id="t22-04-c"></a>


- **T22.04.c** Detect requirements without tests and tests without stated purpose. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T22-02](#pr-t22-02).


<a id="t22-05"></a>

### T22.05 — Library packaging

Packaging installs public headers and artifacts with consumable build targets or explicit commands. Static/shared choices affect dependency closure, symbol visibility and runtime lookup. Test consumption outside both source and build trees, including a clean installation prefix.

Investigation: Package the small library and compile an independent consumer against installed artifacts only.

Misconception to resolve: A successful in-tree example does not test the package interface.

Observable evidence: Install manifest, exported-target/command evidence and clean-prefix consumer execution. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-02](#pr-t22-02).

<a id="t22-06"></a>

### T22.06 — Compatibility and FFI

FFI crosses calling convention, layout, string/buffer and ownership boundaries. Define length units, encoding, allocator/release pairing and version-skew behavior. A foreign runtime cannot safely guess private structure layout or release memory with a different allocator.

Investigation: Expose a minimal C ABI and call it from a small independent Python ctypes consumer with explicit signatures.

Misconception to resolve: A function name being visible does not make arbitrary foreign signatures compatible.

Observable evidence: Layout/calling-contract evidence, buffer ownership tests and version-skew rejection. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-03](#pr-t22-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t22-06-b"></a>

<a id="t22-06-c"></a>

A dependency inventory pins direct/transitive sources, versions and applicable licenses. Source reuse carries obligations distinct from an independent educational implementation informed by concepts. Record uncertainty and actual license text identity; popularity or repository labels do not decide compatibility.

Investigation: Produce a dependency/provenance ledger and separate reused code from original mechanisms and external test oracles.

Misconception to resolve: A permissive-looking top-level license does not necessarily cover every bundled component.

Observable evidence: Pinned inventory, license notices and unresolved-obligation records tied to actual artifacts. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-03](#pr-t22-03).

<a id="t22-08"></a>

### T22.08 — Code review and source reading

Review follows invariants, ownership, failure and generated code, using call/data flow to navigate unfamiliar source. Form a hypothesis before modifying a legacy path and test it against evidence. Review findings should name a contract and reproducer rather than only style preference.

Investigation: Read one selected unfamiliar implementation, map its key flow and review your component with an invariant/failure checklist.

Misconception to resolve: Reading functions in file order is not always the fastest route to understanding behavior.

Observable evidence: Call/data-flow notes, a hypothesis/reproducer and actionable findings with dispositions. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-04](#pr-t22-04).

<a id="t22-09"></a>

### T22.09 — Refactoring and regression analysis

Characterization tests preserve current behavior before a structural change, while intentionally changed contracts need new expectations. Bisection narrows a regression to a change; minimized inputs reveal its mechanism. Refactoring is successful when improved structure and preserved behavior are both demonstrated.

Investigation: Refactor one failure path after characterization, insert a regression and locate/minimize it through version history.

Misconception to resolve: Passing only new tests cannot demonstrate old consumers retained their behavior.

Observable evidence: Before/after consumer checks, bisection evidence and a retained minimized regression. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-04](#pr-t22-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t22-10"></a>

### T22.10 — Release engineering

A release includes versioned binaries, matching symbols, build/configuration provenance, changes and known limits. Reproducibility can mean identical bytes under controlled inputs or explainable differences under declared toolchains; state the claim. Clean installation and rollback/replacement tests establish deployment behavior.

Investigation: Create two small releases, install each into isolated prefixes and test replacement plus migration.

Misconception to resolve: An archive filename and successful local build are not a release evidence chain.

Observable evidence: Artifact hashes, matching debug identifiers, clean-consumer runs and rollback/migration results. Evidence is developed in [PR-T22-04](#pr-t22-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

## Reading guidance

- **R-doxygen-contract-docs**, **Documenting the code** (1 h): Produce API references while retaining separate architecture rationale.

- **R-doxygen-contract-docs**, **\pre { description of the precondition }** (1 h): Write caller obligations explicitly; documentation does not enforce them.

- **R-modern-c-3**, **10.1 Interface documentation** (1 h): Review the public contract from a consumer perspective.

- **R-hanson-cii**, **3.2 Implementation** (1 h): Practice unfamiliar-source navigation and representation/invariant review.

Read only these inspected locators as the essential spine. Additional reading time covers comparison, notes and retrieval, not an unstated whole-book assignment. Historical examples require the modern contract review stated here; draft and live-document limits remain in [guide-reading](#guide-reading).

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T22-01](#pr-t22-01) — Readable repository and executable API documentation (8 h, profile A, core).

- [PR-T22-02](#pr-t22-02) — Traceable package consumed outside the tree (10 h, profile A, core).

- [PR-T22-03](#pr-t22-03) — Foreign consumer and dependency provenance (10 h, profile A, core).

- [PR-T22-04](#pr-t22-04) — Review, minimized regression and two reproducible releases (12 h, profile A, core).

The project-hour total is 40 h and is already included in implementation plus verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation are separate. Follow [guide-workload](#guide-workload) for conditional diagnostic and elective accounting.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Consume the installed library from an independent project and foreign-language harness, then review/refactor/release it without losing contracts. Detect traceability gaps and explain all dependency/license provenance. The release dossier must make a known limitation visible rather than quietly burying it in source.

For independent study, make predictions before execution, compare an independent oracle, inspect one counterexample and defend the result aloud or in a short recorded review. Link each original objective to a specific artifact; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to score it. A failed gate requires a minimized cause, a corrected model and a fresh regression, not repeated nominal runs.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, rebuild from a clean clone with pinned inputs, replace one dependency or package mode and repeat the independent-consumer and migration tests.

## Environment and limits

Use the recorded hosted laboratory in [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) and the per-project boundary in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). C17 is the baseline; edition/extension experiments are isolated and capability checked. Supplied fixture oracles validate mathematical or declared synthetic expectations. They do not execute the learner’s C, prove all language behavior or certify target hardware. Record actual commands, versions, observations and unresolved limits separately.
