<a id="t33"></a>

# T33 — Formal reasoning and verification

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 63 | B, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T04](#t04), [T14](#t14), [T18](#t18), [T32](#t32).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 26 | 14 | 8 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

State properties precisely and connect them to concrete C semantics, bounded environments and reported verifier obligations. A proof artifact must make its assumptions and skipped/unproved goals visible.

## Entry check and remediation

Derive a prefix-sum invariant, trace one bounded pointer extent and distinguish mathematical versus unsigned/signed C arithmetic. Repair T03/T04/T14 reasoning selectively. Review T32 independent-oracle and reproducibility work before installing the selected CBMC/Frama-C/solver environment.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t33-01"></a>

### T33.01 — Specifications and invariants

A specification relates concrete state to mathematical meaning. For a bounded prefix sum, require a valid extent, define the accepted integer range and state which bytes may change. Safety, functional result and eventual termination are separate properties. Write pre/postconditions and an abstraction mapping for the fixture before choosing a verifier. The misconception is that a precise English return-value sentence also specifies lifetime, ownership and side effects.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-01-a"></a>


- **T33.01.a** Express preconditions, postconditions, and representation invariants precisely. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-01-b"></a>


- **T33.01.b** Separate safety, functional correctness, and liveness properties. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-01-c"></a>


- **T33.01.c** Match mathematical state to concrete C representations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-02"></a>

### T33.02 — Loop reasoning

A useful loop invariant carries what is already processed and what remains valid. For summing n elements, i<=n and accumulator=sum of elements before i support the exit result; an overflow bound must also be preserved. Prove initialization, one iteration and exit, then give n-i as the termination variant. Testing all small n is not an inductive proof for arbitrary n. Evidence is a proof outline plus a broken-invariant counterexample.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-02-a"></a>


- **T33.02.a** Derive invariants strong enough to establish postconditions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-02-b"></a>


- **T33.02.b** Prove initialization, preservation, and exit consequences. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-02-c"></a>


- **T33.02.c** State termination variants and resource bounds. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-01](#pr-t33-01).


<a id="t33-03"></a>

### T33.03 — Arithmetic and memory models

Mathematical integers do not wrap, while unsigned C arithmetic is modular and signed overflow is not a valid arithmetic step. Pointer validity also needs extent, lifetime and aliasing assumptions. Compare the fixture's unbounded result with an explicitly eight-bit modular result, then write the stronger precondition needed for equality. Evidence includes the promoted intermediate type and every memory bound; silently replacing C expressions with ideal arithmetic proves a different program.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-03-a"></a>


- **T33.03.a** Account for machine integers, pointer validity, and aliasing. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-03-b"></a>


- **T33.03.b** Distinguish mathematical abstractions from executable C semantics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-03-c"></a>


- **T33.03.c** Prevent proofs from silently assuming away implementation defects. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-04"></a>

### T33.04 — Contracts and annotations

Annotations belong to the API: requires describe caller obligations, ensures describe results and assigns describe the frame. ACSL's logical integers need explicit connections to machine values. Annotate a caller-storage prefix-sum or maximum routine and test that its documented failure behavior matches the contract. An omitted frame condition can leave a functional proof compatible with unwanted writes. Evidence includes a side-effect counterexample and repaired frame.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-04-a"></a>


- **T33.04.a** Write selected ACSL or tool-specific contracts. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-04-b"></a>


- **T33.04.b** Specify frame conditions and allowed side effects. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-04-c"></a>


- **T33.04.c** Keep annotations consistent with public API documentation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-02](#pr-t33-02).


<a id="t33-05"></a>

### T33.05 — Bounded model checking

A bounded model checker explores a finite encoding of input, loops and environment. Build a CBMC harness with nondeterministic n/data under the public contract, assert the result/bounds, and require unwinding assertions. The loop guard may need one more unwinding evaluation than body iterations. A too-small bound can hide a reachable defect. Preserve successful obligations, failed counterexamples, tool defaults and an intentionally insufficient-bound run.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-05-a"></a>


- **T33.05.a** Construct harnesses with nondeterministic but valid inputs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


<a id="t33-05-b"></a>


- **T33.05.b** Bound loops and environment behavior explicitly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


<a id="t33-05-c"></a>


- **T33.05.c** Interpret unwinding checks and counterexamples correctly. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


<a id="t33-06"></a>

### T33.06 — Deductive verification

Deductive proof generates obligations under contracts and models. With WP, inspect initialization/preservation/postcondition and runtime-error goals separately, including selected arithmetic and memory models. Start with a small integer routine whose range fits; do not use the Real model to claim C floating-point correctness. Evidence lists proved, assumed, unproved and unsupported obligations. 'No reported failures' is inadequate if goals were skipped or a precondition excluded every call.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-04](#pr-t33-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-06-a"></a>


- **T33.06.a** Generate and discharge proof obligations for selected routines. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-04](#pr-t33-04).


<a id="t33-06-b"></a>


- **T33.06.b** Separate axioms, assumptions, and proved lemmas. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-04](#pr-t33-04).


<a id="t33-06-c"></a>


- **T33.06.c** Investigate unproved goals instead of reporting blanket success. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-04](#pr-t33-04).


<a id="t33-07"></a>

### T33.07 — Abstract interpretation

Abstract interpretation computes an over-approximation of reachable values. An interval containing zero can warn about division even if a richer relation would rule zero out. Inspect an Eva alarm, justify an invariant or partition, and rerun without suppressing actual behavior. Evidence separates a real defect from an imprecision alarm and records soundness/context assumptions. Sequential Eva does not directly establish asynchronous interrupt correctness.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-07-a"></a>


- **T33.07.a** Interpret over-approximations and alarm explanations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


<a id="t33-07-b"></a>


- **T33.07.b** Tune precision with justified invariants and partitioning. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


<a id="t33-07-c"></a>


- **T33.07.c** Distinguish soundness assumptions from false-positive reduction. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


<a id="t33-08"></a>

### T33.08 — Environment models

An environment model determines what the proof can see. If an adapter always returns full success, the harness cannot prove cleanup after partial progress, invalid counts or allocation failure. Make nondeterministic outcomes range over the real documented contract, with explicit exclusion of unsupported asynchronous hardware. Evidence includes one counterexample admitted only after repairing an overly helpful stub. More assumptions can make a proof easier while making its claim weaker.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-08-a"></a>


- **T33.08.a** Model allocators, I/O, hardware registers, and callbacks at appropriate fidelity. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


<a id="t33-08-b"></a>


- **T33.08.b** Document behavior excluded by stubs and assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


<a id="t33-08-c"></a>


- **T33.08.c** Check that the environment model is not easier than the real contract. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-03](#pr-t33-03).


<a id="t33-09"></a>

### T33.09 — Concurrency reasoning

**Elective extension.** The elective finite queue model can test abstract linearization and FIFO histories under a declared sequentially consistent event model. Enumerate interleavings while preserving each participant's order and identify publication/removal points. This is not proof that a C acquire/release implementation realizes the abstract history, nor that an interrupt/compiler extension has ISO-thread semantics. Evidence includes accepted/rejected histories and a separate memory-order argument with its unsupported cases disclosed.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-06](#pr-t33-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-09-a"></a>


- **T33.09.a** Model a small publication or queue protocol. **Disposition:** elective. **Activity:** [PR-T33-06](#pr-t33-06).


<a id="t33-09-b"></a>


- **T33.09.b** Distinguish linearizability properties from memory-order validity. **Disposition:** elective. **Activity:** [PR-T33-06](#pr-t33-06).


<a id="t33-09-c"></a>


- **T33.09.c** Use model-specific tools without generalizing beyond supported semantics. **Disposition:** elective. **Activity:** [PR-T33-06](#pr-t33-06).


<a id="t33-10"></a>

### T33.10 — Evidence composition

Compose evidence by property: a proof may establish bounds under preconditions, instrumentation may find exercised lifetime defects, tests may establish vectors, and a scope may measure a physical pulse. Maintain a claim/assumption/artifact table with trusted compiler, runtime, solver and hardware entries. Do not add coverage percentages to proof percentages. The final argument states which properties are unproved and which counterexamples would invalidate the environment model.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t33-10-a"></a>


- **T33.10.a** Combine proofs, static analysis, tests, and measurements by property. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


<a id="t33-10-b"></a>


- **T33.10.b** Track trusted compiler, library, hardware, and tool assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).


<a id="t33-10-c"></a>


- **T33.10.c** State precisely what remains unproved or outside the model. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T33-05](#pr-t33-05).

## Reading guidance

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. Spend the remaining reading budget on original teaching, worked traces and target documentation comparisons, not whole uninspected chapters.

**An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming — 3.1. Axiom of Assignment (1 h):** Connect state transformations to contracts.

**CBMC training: What is loop unwinding? — Loop unwinding assertions (1 h):** Expose bounded completeness.

**ANSI/ISO C Specification Language — 2.2.4 Integer arithmetic and machine integers (1 h):** Connect logical and C arithmetic.

**WP Plug-in Manual — 1.2 Tutorial (1 h):** Generate selected obligations.

**WP Plug-in Manual — 1.6 Limitations & Roadmap (1 h):** Report unsupported cases.

**The Eva plug-in — 2.1 Introduction (1 h):** Interpret value approximation.

**The Eva plug-in — 5.4.5 Applications relying on software interrupts (1 h):** Keep interrupt scope honest.

**Shared scope limit — An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming:** A small illustrative language and historical formalism, not modern C semantics. Signed overflow, aliasing, memory safety and termination need current C/tool evidence. Remaining paper pages were not visually inspected.

**Shared scope limit — CBMC training: What is loop unwinding?:** Training examples do not select a release or prove a hardware environment. Pin tool version, check defaults and report assumptions, reachability and every unwinding result. The old CPROVER manual routes returned navigation only.

**Shared scope limit — ANSI/ISO C Specification Language:** Logical arithmetic has no machine overflow by default. Language expressiveness does not imply every clause is supported by each plug-in; WP limitations must accompany assignments.

**Shared scope limit — WP Plug-in Manual:** Proof is conditional on contracts, runtime-error obligations and models. Tutorial reports skipped unaligned-pointer/function-pointer guards. The Real Model explicitly does not establish C/IEEE floating-point correctness. Selected passages only; no solver execution.

**Shared scope limit — The Eva plug-in:** False alarms can result from approximation. Soundness is relative to the specified context and supported semantics. Current manual states asynchronous interrupts are not directly modeled; do not claim full firmware proof from sequential analysis.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

## Implementation projects

- [PR-T33-01 — Prefix invariant and termination](#pr-t33-01), 6 h, core, profile C. Specify and implement a bounded prefix sum for at most 4valuesin[0,10], caller-provided extent and unchanged output on invalid input.

- [PR-T33-02 — Machine arithmetic and ACSL frame](#pr-t33-02), 6 h, core, profile C. Annotate one small caller-storage routine with pre/post/frame conditions and explicit logical-to-machine arithmetic.

- [PR-T33-03 — CBMC harness and demanding environment](#pr-t33-03), 8 h, core, profile C. Build a CBMC harness for the bounded prefix routine and an adapter with partial/zero/error/invalid progress outcomes.

- [PR-T33-04 — WP obligations and explicit assumptions](#pr-t33-04), 8 h, core, profile C. Use Frama-C WP on a small integer routine with a finite admitted range, explicit memory/frame contracts and runtime-error obligations.

- [PR-T33-05 — Eva precision and composed claims](#pr-t33-05), 6 h, core, profile C. Analyze a bounded routine with Eva, classify real versus imprecision alarms and compose property-specific proof/test/measurement evidence.

- [PR-T33-06 — Elective finite publication model](#pr-t33-06), 6 h, elective, profile C. Enumerate a two-event producer/two-event consumer under a declared sequentially consistent event model.

Present one successful small CBMC claim with complete unwinding checks and one WP/Eva analysis with explicit runtime/model assumptions. Preserve a real counterexample and an unproved/imprecise obligation. If success required an unjustified assumption, repair the harness rather than announcing verification.

For every linked objective, retain a separately labeled explanation, implementation/analysis artifact and check. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the rubric; one passing fixture does not establish all three objectives of a topic.

## Consolidation and transfer

Revisit the routine with changed bounds, aliasing or partial-I/O behavior. Predict which obligations/models must change and retain one failing case that exposes an overly helpful environment stub.

# T34 — Optimization, vectorization, and measurement

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 71 | A, B, C, E |

**Prerequisites:** [T08](#t08), [T17](#t17), [T32](#t32).

**Required selected foundations:** [T25.02.a](#t25-02-a), [T25.06.a](#t25-06-a), [T25.06.b](#t25-06-b), [T25.06.c](#t25-06-c), [T25.07.b](#t25-07-b). Complete those leaves before the dependent project; the rest of the referenced domain need not be finished.

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | 30 | 16 | 8 | 5 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Optimize one verified kernel by forming cost hypotheses, inspecting generated code and measuring representative work. Preserve exact/approximate semantic contracts while changing layout, vectorization and build strategy.

## Entry check and remediation

Pass T17's independent-reference/error checks and T32's reproducible test habit. Draw nonoverlapping array extents and a publication/race argument using the selected T25 leaves; the full pthread route is unnecessary for the scalar/SIMD kernel. Repair only ratio/units, stride arithmetic or sampling/distribution vocabulary before measurements.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t34-01"></a>

### T34.01 — Optimization specification

Optimization starts with a contract: representative sizes/data, allowed numeric error, latency/throughput targets and memory/energy limits. Reuse the scalar correctness oracle before changing code. A faster result on one favorable input can fail the deployed workload or its error allowance. Define pass/fail gates independently of timing and include both tiny and large cases. Evidence is a workload ledger whose correctness gates cannot be relaxed to rescue a speed claim.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-01-a"></a>


- **T34.01.a** Define workload, latency, throughput, memory, and energy objectives. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-01-b"></a>


- **T34.01.b** Preserve correctness and numerical constraints as acceptance gates. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-01-c"></a>


- **T34.01.c** Select representative inputs rather than only favorable microbenchmarks. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-02"></a>

### T34.02 — Cost models

Work, instruction count and memory traffic are different cost models. A vector add has about one arithmetic operation per element but reads two arrays and writes one; define the measured boundary before calculating bytes or intensity. Use a simple roofline-style ceiling to form a bottleneck hypothesis, then revise it using actual evidence. A theoretical ceiling is not a measured rate or a Cortex-M WCET bound. Preserve the model and its counterexample.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-02-a"></a>


- **T34.02.a** Separate asymptotic work from instructions and memory traffic. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-02-b"></a>


- **T34.02.b** Identify compute-bound, bandwidth-bound, and latency-bound regions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-02-c"></a>


- **T34.02.c** Use measurements to revise initial bottleneck hypotheses. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-01](#pr-t34-01).


<a id="t34-03"></a>

### T34.03 — Memory hierarchy

Stride and working set determine which memory hierarchy is stressed. A blocked traversal can reuse a tile, while a transposed or hot/cold layout changes touched bytes without changing the algorithmic result. Implement variants of the T17 matrix/data kernel and calculate a declared synthetic cache-line footprint. Real TLB/cache observations require actual host counters and sizes. Alignment alone does not guarantee a gain; evidence includes semantic equality and generated access patterns.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-03-a"></a>


- **T34.03.a** Analyze cache locality, working set, TLB effects, and access stride. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-03-b"></a>


- **T34.03.b** Compare data layout, blocking, and hot/cold field separation. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-03-c"></a>


- **T34.03.c** Account for alignment without assuming alignment alone improves speed. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-04"></a>

### T34.04 — Control and instruction effects

Branches, dependencies and code size trade against one another. A branchless selection may execute extra work or extend a dependence chain, while an unrolled loop may increase instruction-cache pressure and spills. Compare branchy and branchless bounded clamp/count kernels under predictable and mixed inputs. 'Fewer branches' is not an acceptance criterion. Evidence links measured distributions to disassembly, including spills/code bytes and a workload where the anticipated gain disappears.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-04-a"></a>


- **T34.04.a** Examine branches, prediction, dependencies, and instruction-level parallelism. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-04-b"></a>


- **T34.04.b** Compare branchless and branch-based implementations empirically. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-04-c"></a>


- **T34.04.c** Inspect spills, code size, and instruction-cache effects. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-02](#pr-t34-02).


<a id="t34-05"></a>

### T34.05 — Compiler optimization evidence

Compiler reports are explanations to check against final code. Compile the scalar loop at fixed settings, retain vectorization diagnostics, inspect intermediate/final instructions and identify one justified missed optimization. If aliasing prevents transformation, inspect the interface before adding restrict. A report that says vectorized does not establish correctness or actual speed. Evidence preserves flags, object identity, report text and the corresponding machine-code loop.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-05-a"></a>


- **T34.05.a** Read vectorization and optimization reports. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


<a id="t34-05-b"></a>


- **T34.05.b** Compare source, intermediate representation, and final machine code. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


<a id="t34-05-c"></a>


- **T34.05.c** Distinguish missed optimization from invalid programmer assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


<a id="t34-06"></a>

### T34.06 — Auto-vectorization

Auto-vectorization can change iteration order, reduction grouping and alias assumptions. Permit restrict only for demonstrably nonoverlapping extents; a forbidden overlap must be rejected by the API or excluded explicitly, not accidentally benchmarked. Use unsigned elementwise arithmetic for the initial kernel to avoid floating-reduction ambiguity, then revisit a sum under its numeric tolerance. Evidence includes alias/tail cases, scalar comparison and a valid contract supporting each hint.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-06-a"></a>


- **T34.06.a** Identify dependence, aliasing, reduction, and control-flow barriers. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


<a id="t34-06-b"></a>


- **T34.06.b** Use restrict and alignment information only when contracts justify them. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


<a id="t34-06-c"></a>


- **T34.06.c** Test whether transformed loops preserve required numerical semantics. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-03](#pr-t34-03).


<a id="t34-07"></a>

### T34.07 — Explicit SIMD

Explicit SIMD works on lanes with an extent contract. The core x86 teaching kernel uses SSE2 four-lane uint32 addition modulo 2^32, unaligned full-vector loads/stores, and a scalar tail. For nine elements, process two groups of four and one tail; an unaligned load still needs sixteen valid bytes. Implement a scalar fallback and forbid partial overlap. Evidence includes wrap values, lengths 0–9, offset alignments and final instructions on a verified supported host.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-07-a"></a>


- **T34.07.a** Implement one target-appropriate intrinsic kernel. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


<a id="t34-07-b"></a>


- **T34.07.b** Handle lane operations, masks, alignment, and partial tails. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


<a id="t34-07-c"></a>


- **T34.07.c** Preserve a portable scalar fallback and reference tests. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


<a id="t34-08"></a>

### T34.08 — ISA dispatch

Dispatch must not execute specialized instructions while checking whether they are supported. Put the baseline selector and SSE2 implementation in separate translation units with recorded flags; use the documented positive/zero feature result and a force-scalar test option. On the selected x86-64 Linux environment also record applicable OS/ABI support. AVX dispatch is an unassigned extension requiring OS-state checks. Evidence is selector tests, baseline disassembly and a specialized path that is unreachable under the unsupported-feature fixture.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-08-a"></a>


- **T34.08.a** Detect required CPU and operating-system support before dispatch. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


<a id="t34-08-b"></a>


- **T34.08.b** Isolate specialized code from baseline execution paths. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


<a id="t34-08-c"></a>


- **T34.08.c** Verify build and linker behavior for multiversioned functions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-04](#pr-t34-04).


<a id="t34-09"></a>

### T34.09 — Benchmark construction

A benchmark must retain its result, exclude unrelated setup and state how warmup/cache state/affinity/clock changes are handled. Record repeated samples and report median plus spread; preserve raw samples rather than a single rounded speedup. The supplied times are synthetic oracle data, not measurements. Implement a harness with a consumed checksum and paired baseline/variant runs. Evidence includes empty-loop overhead and one source of uncertainty the setup cannot eliminate.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-09-a"></a>


- **T34.09.a** Prevent dead-code elimination and unrelated setup contamination. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


<a id="t34-09-b"></a>


- **T34.09.b** Control warmup, cache state, affinity, and clock variation where possible. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


<a id="t34-09-c"></a>


- **T34.09.c** Report distributions, uncertainty, and environmental conditions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


<a id="t34-10"></a>

### T34.10 — Profiling and counters

Sampling and counters estimate where cost occurs under their own limits. Correlate hot addresses with matching code; record counter availability, multiplexing scale and permission failures. A scaled event count is not exact when workloads change during multiplexing. Use sampling plus one supported counter when available, otherwise report the missing evidence and rely on a narrower timing claim. Evidence includes raw enabled/running times, scaling arithmetic and a revised bottleneck hypothesis.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-10-a"></a>


- **T34.10.a** Use sampling and counters to locate actual hot paths. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


<a id="t34-10-b"></a>


- **T34.10.b** Interpret counter multiplexing and measurement limitations. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


<a id="t34-10-c"></a>


- **T34.10.c** Correlate observations with generated code and memory access. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-05](#pr-t34-05).


<a id="t34-11"></a>

### T34.11 — Whole-program optimization

LTO and PGO alter whole-program decisions and introduce build/profile assumptions. Compare plain, LTO and representative-profile builds, inspect code/dependencies and retest the correctness gate. A training workload biased toward one branch may regress a different input distribution. Evidence includes build cost, executable size, profile identity/mismatch diagnostics and a held-out workload. A flag alone does not prove the linker performed the intended transformation.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-11-a"></a>


- **T34.11.a** Evaluate LTO, PGO, inlining, and section layout experimentally. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).


<a id="t34-11-b"></a>


- **T34.11.b** Account for build cost, code growth, and profile representativeness. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).


<a id="t34-11-c"></a>


- **T34.11.c** Recheck runtime dependencies and diagnostics after optimization. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).


<a id="t34-12"></a>

### T34.12 — Embedded optimization

Embedded optimization trades latency, Flash, RAM/stack and energy; the fastest version can be unacceptable in another budget. Deploy two semantically equivalent variants only after the target startup/dependency audit, measure actual execution and optionally current with recorded equipment, and keep error limits fixed. Emulator cycle counts do not establish F439 physical energy or WCET. Evidence distinguishes measured speed/size/stack from inferred models and retains regression thresholds with configuration.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t34-12-a"></a>


- **T34.12.a** Compare speed, size, stack, and energy trade-offs. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).


<a id="t34-12-b"></a>


- **T34.12.b** Measure on real target hardware for physical performance claims. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).


<a id="t34-12-c"></a>


- **T34.12.c** Retain correctness, timing assumptions, and regression thresholds together. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T34-06](#pr-t34-06).

## Reading guidance

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. Spend the remaining reading budget on original teaching, worked traces and target documentation comparisons, not whole uninspected chapters.

**Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures — Roofline Model (1 h):** State the memory/compute boundary.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -O2 (1 h):** Compare fixed optimization settings.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -fstrict-aliasing (1 h):** Audit optimization preconditions.

**Clang SSE2 intrinsic header, selected definitions — _mm_add_epi32 (1 h):** Select modulo lane semantics.

**Clang SSE2 intrinsic header, selected definitions — _mm_loadu_si128 (1 h):** Respect full-vector extent.

**GCC x86 built-in CPU detection contract — __builtin_cpu_supports (1 h):** Build positive/zero feature dispatch.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -flto (1 h):** Inspect whole-program compile/link behavior.

**GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts — -fprofile-generate (1 h):** Collect a representative training profile.

**Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization — -fprofile-use (1 h):** Reject mismatched profiles.

**Shared scope limit — Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures:** Original examples are multicore floating-point kernels with DRAM traffic. It is a reasoning model, not a universal prediction or proof of Cortex-M4 latency, WCET or energy. State the measured memory boundary and ceilings.

**Shared scope limit — Using the GNU Compiler Collection: Options That Control Optimization:** The reference version is deliberately fixed; installed compiler identity and target-dependent behavior require separate evidence. Enabling fast-math changes admissible numeric semantics and needs a documented error/exception contract.

**Shared scope limit — Clang SSE2 intrinsic header, selected definitions:** These functions specify four-lane modulo integer addition and full 16-byte unaligned access; unaligned access still requires the complete valid extent. Intrinsic header/source version is fixed, installed compiler is not verified. No other intrinsic or ISA dispatch mechanism was inspected.

**Shared scope limit — GCC x86 built-in CPU detection contract:** Does not verify installed GCC internals or OS support for arbitrary AVX state. Teaching core specialization uses SSE2 on an identified supported x86 host; AVX/ifunc expansion requires additional OS-state and loader research.

**Shared scope limit — GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts:** Selected options only, not every instrumentation feature. Flag availability and effective dependencies vary with installed compiler/target. GNU/Linux hardening aggregate is not a bare-metal recipe; instrumentation changes resource/timing behavior.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

# T35 — Secure and resilient C

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |

| cross-track | core | 66 | A, B, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T18](#t18), [T21](#t21), [T23](#t23), [T32](#t32).

## Purpose and outcomes

Build a bounded command service and defend its trust, memory, process, resource and artifact boundaries. Security claims must name a deployment/threat model and actual enforcement evidence.

## Entry check and remediation

Review caller-storage bounds/lifetimes, checked integer arithmetic, Linux descriptor/process ownership and T32 failure/instrumentation work. Repair only the failed leaf before the dependent project. Identify a private nonprivileged sandbox and synthetic tokens; no personal files, production keys or elevated service is required.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) for the diagnostic policy and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for route order. Only the stated prelude leaves must precede a dependent project.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t35-01"></a>

### T35.01 — Threat and failure models

A threat model names assets, controlled inputs, trust boundaries and permitted effects; a failure model also includes accidental corruption and unavailable services. For the teaching command service, untrusted bytes may request only bounded operations and authorization is separate from syntax. Write abuse and accident cases before coding. The misconception is that every valid packet is authorized. Evidence identifies the consequence prevented, residual risks and the exact isolated test environment.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

- **T35.01.a** Identify assets, trust boundaries, attacker-controlled input, and environmental faults. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


<a id="t35-01-b"></a>

<a id="t35-02"></a>

### T35.02 — Memory safety

Length arithmetic can turn a representation defect into an invalid access. Track capacity, used extent, lifetime and ownership together; validate count before multiplication and bounds before publishing a view. Implement a bounded caller-storage command representation rather than carrying unrelated pointer/length guesses. A return-code check cannot repair an already performed out-of-bounds write. Evidence uses sentinels, rejected extreme counts and a lifetime/ownership ledger.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t35-02-a"></a>


- **T35.02.a** Trace bounds, lifetime, initialization, and ownership defects. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


<a id="t35-02-b"></a>


- **T35.02.b** Analyze how small arithmetic mistakes become invalid memory access. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


<a id="t35-02-c"></a>


- **T35.02.c** Prefer representations that make dangerous states difficult to construct. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


<a id="t35-03"></a>

### T35.03 — Input validation

Validation checks syntax, cross-field consistency and policy in that order before effects. The fixture's packet has an opcode, count and fixed-width elements; trailing bytes, mismatched count and unauthorized operation are rejected without modifying caller output. Set maximum work and nesting even for syntactically valid inputs. Evidence includes malformed and valid-but-denied cases. Sanitizing a string without validating its structured meaning is not this contract.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t35-03-a"></a>

<a id="t35-03-b"></a>


- **T35.03.b** Separate syntactic validity from semantic authorization. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


<a id="t35-03-c"></a>

<a id="t35-04"></a>

### T35.04 — Integer and format vulnerabilities

Checked size calculations must use a bound before count*width can overflow; signed/unsigned conversions and narrowing need separate range checks. A format string is trusted program data, not an input packet. Implement the fixture's capped count parser with exact decimal syntax and fixed formatting specification. Evidence includes negative, leading-sign, oversized and boundary inputs plus correctly typed output. Accepting a compiler warning-free call does not establish semantic authorization.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t35-04-a"></a>

<a id="t35-04-b"></a>


- **T35.04.b** Use checked size calculations and trusted formatting specifications. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-01](#pr-t35-01).

<a id="t35-05"></a>

### T35.05 — Filesystem and process boundaries

Filesystem names can change between check and use; descriptors name already-open objects. In the controlled Linux worker, use exclusive creation, atomic close-on-exec semantics and explicit argument vectors, then inspect which descriptors the child inherits. Pass a read-only log descriptor, read its bytes and attempt a write: record the actual EBADF failure and unchanged bytes. Keep reopening the path as a separate residual-authority test. Evidence also includes a competing-name case and partial-failure cleanup.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-02](#pr-t35-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t35-05-a"></a>


- **T35.05.a** Avoid race-prone check-then-use assumptions. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-02](#pr-t35-02).


<a id="t35-05-b"></a>


- **T35.05.b** Handle descriptor inheritance, temporary files, and process execution safely. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-02](#pr-t35-02).


<a id="t35-05-c"></a>


- **T35.05.c** Prefer explicit argument vectors over untrusted shell-string construction. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-02](#pr-t35-02).


<a id="t35-06"></a>

### T35.06 — Resource-exhaustion resistance

Resistance to exhaustion requires bounded admission, queues, allocation/work, retries and nesting. A syntactically valid request can still be too expensive. Implement per-request and total quotas with a fail-before-effect policy and a finite retry/recovery budget. Evidence includes a burst, pathological valid input and recovery under continued overload. Retrying faster cannot create capacity; state which requests are dropped, coalesced or rejected and how callers learn that outcome.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-03](#pr-t35-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t35-06-a"></a>

<a id="t35-06-b"></a>


- **T35.06.b** Define overload and admission-control behavior. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T35-03](#pr-t35-03).


<a id="t35-06-c"></a>

<a id="t35-07"></a>

### T35.07 — Binary hardening

Hardening changes generated code and runtime expectations. Audit ASLR policy and repeated process mappings, ELF PIE type, GNU_RELRO plus eager binding, stack-protector code/runtime symbol, fortification at supported optimization and non-executable stack/load segments. Compare a plain and a hardened hosted build; inspect actual bytes/headers rather than the command alone. Evidence also lists libc/compiler-helper dependencies and overhead. These Linux facilities are not portable replacements for bare-metal bounds or ownership.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-04](#pr-t35-04).

<a id="t35-08"></a>

### T35.08 — Privilege and isolation

Privilege and isolation require an OS or hardware mechanism with a stated scope. The nonprivileged worker uses an inherited read-only log descriptor: the OS enforces that writes through this descriptor fail, while application policy denies write-config before effects. A private directory and CLOEXEC control names and inheritance but do not remove ordinary user filesystem or network authority. Compare the child’s separate address space and this narrow descriptor restriction with a logical module and an MPU design at awareness depth. Evidence includes the denied write and a residual-authority table; do not claim a complete sandbox.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-02](#pr-t35-02).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t35-09"></a>

### T35.09 — Sensitive data and timing

Secrets can persist in copies, logs and compiler-eliminated clearing. Use synthetic test tokens only, enumerate copies/lifetime and inspect generated code for a deliberate clearing policy supported by the selected environment. Compare early-exit and fixed-work toy comparisons, observing input-dependent work before any physical timing claim. Fixed source-loop length is not proof of constant-time machine execution. Evidence states compiler/ISA and excludes production cryptography or a claim that Bernstein's old host mechanism exists on F439.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-05](#pr-t35-05).

<a id="t35-10"></a>

### T35.10 — Concurrency and resilience

Validation can become stale if another context changes the validated state. Use an immutable accepted request/ownership transfer and finite fail-safe state transitions; inject an update between validation and effect and require rejection or coherent generation checking. Recovery must preserve invariants under repeated failure, not loop forever. Evidence includes adversarial logical schedules, one terminal outcome per request and a bounded recovery trace. A lock protecting a flag alone may leave the actual invariant exposed.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-03](#pr-t35-03).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t35-11"></a>

### T35.11 — Supply chain and artifact integrity

Artifact identity is a hash comparison, while authenticity requires a trusted signing/verification chain and rollback policy. Compute fixture hashes and reject incompatible versions or uncommitted update slots, then record the source/tool/dependency release identities for your real image. An attacker able to replace both bytes and checksum defeats checksum-only authenticity. Evidence distinguishes consistency, signer trust, freshness and reproducibility; no homemade signature algorithm is part of this project.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-06](#pr-t35-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t35-12"></a>

### T35.12 — Security review and limits

A security review needs a concrete checklist derived from the component's actual boundaries: lengths, arithmetic, lifetimes, effects, quotas, privileges, sensitive data and artifact trust. Map each property to a regression, static/proof argument or explicit gap. Review a deliberately flawed design ledger and revise one implementation accordingly. Evidence retains residual risks and unsupported attacker/fault assumptions. A passing fuzz campaign and a collection of hardening flags do not establish complete security.

Apply this mechanism in [PR-T35-06](#pr-t35-06).

## Reading guidance

Read the bounded selections before the corresponding project, then annotate one contract or assumption you will test. The assigned reading table is generated from the exact inspected locators. Spend the remaining reading budget on original teaching, worked traces and target documentation comparisons, not whole uninspected chapters.

**GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts — -fhardened (1 h):** Inspect supported hosted hardening aggregation.

**GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts — -fstack-protector-strong (1 h):** Inspect generated guard/dependency behavior.

**GNU ld option contracts for stack execution, eager binding and RELRO — relro (1 h):** Check protected relocation segment.

**GNU ld option contracts for stack execution, eager binding and RELRO — now (1 h):** Distinguish eager from lazy relocation.

**GNU ld option contracts for stack execution, eager binding and RELRO — noexecstack (1 h):** Audit executable-memory policy.

**Linux proc_sys_kernel(5), ASLR policy subsection — /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space (1 h):** Read policy and observe repeated mappings.

**Cache-timing attacks on AES — 3 Summary of the attack (1 h):** Bound a historical timing threat model.

**CBMC training: What is loop unwinding? — Loop unwinding assertions (1 h):** Keep bounded security claims complete.

**Shared scope limit — GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts:** Selected options only, not every instrumentation feature. Flag availability and effective dependencies vary with installed compiler/target. GNU/Linux hardening aggregate is not a bare-metal recipe; instrumentation changes resource/timing behavior.

**Shared scope limit — GNU ld option contracts for stack execution, eager binding and RELRO:** Moving manual snapshot, not an installed-linker identity. A requested property is not proof of final image/runtime enforcement; no linker execution.

**Shared scope limit — Linux proc_sys_kernel(5), ASLR policy subsection:** Linux-specific, architectural/kernel support and actual configuration still require observation. Read-only policy audit is assigned; no system-wide ASLR modification.

**Shared scope limit — Cache-timing attacks on AES:** Historical Pentium III/OpenSSL experiment; it neither proves a Cortex-M4 leakage mechanism nor supplies production cryptography. The paper itself labels this a preliminary version. Use only a controlled educational threat model.

**Shared scope limit — CBMC training: What is loop unwinding?:** Training examples do not select a release or prove a hardware environment. Pin tool version, check defaults and report assumptions, reachability and every unwinding result. The old CPROVER manual routes returned navigation only.

See [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for access/provenance and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the language baseline.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Reject malformed/unauthorized/overbudget requests before effects, audit actual hardening and descriptor/privilege boundaries, and preserve finite recovery/integrity policies. Review the service against a concrete checklist with residual risks. Flags, fuzz volume and checksum agreement alone do not establish security.

For every linked objective, retain a separately labeled explanation, implementation/analysis artifact and check. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the rubric; one passing fixture does not establish all three objectives of a topic.

## Consolidation and transfer

Change one trust boundary, count limit or update rollback policy and predict which prior evidence becomes insufficient. Replay a race/failure regression and re-audit a compiler-changed image, keeping toy timing experiments separate from production cryptography.

## Environment and limits

Use [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) to declare the dependency boundary, [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory) for installed tools and hardware, and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for image/call-graph evidence. Fixtures are original deterministic mathematical or synthetic-protocol data. Run `python tools/verify_embedded_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to recompute their expectations. This oracle checks fixtures, not learner code.

Record host/tool/ISA identities and all mathematical/environment assumptions. Instrumented timings are not production timings; numerical references have stated domains; proof results hold only for reported obligations/models.

Use [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) to find supplied data and [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) for later cross-module work.

## Purpose and outcomes

Carry a mathematical state relation through original assembly into a protected C interface. This domain extends the completed T14/T15/T18 portfolio: full containers, sorting, matching and graph algorithms are reused. New work consists of narrow kernels, certificates and adapters, not a second complete implementation. Eight milestones total 60 hours of implementation and verification; reading, assessment and consolidation make 84 hours overall.

## Entry check and remediation

Replay an existing T14 heap/AVL and T15 lower-bound/string/graph test; explain one T18 ownership/failure contract and an unsigned midpoint calculation. If an original implementation is missing, complete its prior project first; do not charge its whole rebuild to this extension. Diagnose a failed invariant with a two-element trace before attempting assembly. Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) and [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) to distinguish component and harness dependencies.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t36-01"></a>

### T36.01 — Specifications, invariants and resource bounds

A specification relates initial and final observations; an invariant relates every intermediate state to that specification. A decreasing measure supplies a separate termination argument. In the original Euclid trace `(1071,462) → (462,147) → (147,21) → (21,0)`, replacing `(a,b)` by `(b,a mod b)` preserves common divisors because `a=q*b+r`. The positive second operand decreases; the last nonzero first operand is 21. Three remainder operations is an exact count for this trace, not a bound for every input.

Choose the counted primitive before giving a complexity claim. A RAM comparison count ignores instruction encoding and caches; an expected hash cost requires a distribution; amortized cost covers an entire operation sequence. In a reused doubling vector starting at capacity 1, eight appends write eight new values and copy 1+2+4 old values: fifteen payload writes total, even though the capacity 4→8 append alone costs five. That sequence bound is not a promise that each append is constant-time. Charge queue failure checks as well as successful operations in [PR-T36-01](#pr-t36-01). For a capacity-three queue, a fourth insertion changes neither payload nor count. A sorted prefix alone is too weak: the transformation `[2,1] → [1,1]` is sorted but loses a value. Strengthen it with a multiset relation. Submit the first invalid transition of that mutation, a Euclid preservation/progress derivation and the queue cost ledger. Passing the final-output test alone does not establish an invariant.

<a id="t36-02"></a>

### T36.02 — Arrays, links and frontier representations

An index is a representation choice, not an address. With three actual eight-byte records, payload offsets are 0, 8 and 16; addressability still requires that the corresponding objects and lifetime exist. A node-slot queue carries next links and a free-list invariant in addition to logical FIFO order. Its live payload can equal a circular array's while metadata and traversal costs differ. The operations put 11, put 22, take, put 33, put 44, failed put 55, take leave `[33,44]` in either representation. A contiguous ring may wrap physically even though its logical sequence remains consecutive.

Replay that sequence through the completed T14 implementations. Annotate head/tail/count, occupied node slots, ownership and failed-operation state. Reuse T18 contracts: a typed pool is an actual array of the right element type; a portable byte arena supports byte operations/copy in-out; genuine allocated storage has a different effective-type rule. Merely aligning `unsigned char[]` does not authorize an arbitrary record lvalue. A storage-policy change preserves logical order only if no stale pointer or iterator escapes it. [PR-T36-08](#pr-t36-08) then makes two wrappers expose the same observations with deliberately different ownership. Evidence consists of both state traces, separately counted traversal/storage, and an invalidation experiment performed through a defined API rather than dereferencing a dangling pointer.

<a id="t36-03"></a>

### T36.03 — Callable hand-written x86-64 and Thumb kernels

Assembly exposes the proof boundary one register and memory access at a time. Build two original scalar lower-bound kernels over sorted `uint32_t` arrays: SysV x86-64 and AAPCS32 Thumb for Cortex-M4. Use bounded 32-bit lengths/indices and a checked C wrapper; length zero performs no load and may use a null pointer. A nonempty array must be a live typed array of at least the declared length. Neither kernel may call `bsearch` or any equivalent routine. Compiler output can explain differences, but it is not the hand-written artifact.

Write a liveness table before choosing registers. On SysV, RBX/RBP/R12–R15 are preserved and entry `(RSP+8) mod16=0`; a caller aligns before a nested call. The 128-byte user red zone is not a Cortex-M or Linux-kernel rule. AAPCS has r0–r3/r12 scratch, a preserved set including r4–r8/r10/r11 and platform-specific r9; SP is word-aligned always and eight-byte-aligned at a public interface. BL changes LR, so a nested caller must preserve its return path. In [PR-T36-02](#pr-t36-02), use a leaf kernel plus a separate nested-call probe that poisons allowed scratch registers. Require sentinel, preserved-register and stack-alignment evidence alongside outputs. Successful output with a corrupted saved register is an ABI failure.

<a id="t36-04"></a>

### T36.04 — Ordering, searching and partition boundaries

For half-open lower bound, maintain `0≤lo≤hi≤n`, every earlier element `<key`, and every element at or after `hi` `≥key`. Midpoint `lo+(hi-lo)/2` lies inside a nonempty interval. If `a[mid]<key`, the new lower bound is `mid+1`; otherwise the new upper bound is `mid`. Each step shortens `hi-lo`. On `[0,7,7,2147483648,4294967295]` with key 7, intervals `[0,5) → [0,2) → [0,1) → [1,1)` return the first duplicate at 1. For key 8 the path is `[0,5) → [3,5) → [3,4) → [3,3)`.

The contract orders unsigned 32-bit keys. An x86 signed less branch or Thumb signed LT is a different predicate around `0x80000000`; keep flag provenance visible. Element offset is four times an index, so the wrapper bounds length before target-width multiplication and pointer formation. An absent high key may return n without reading element n. [PR-T36-02](#pr-t36-02) compares operation certificates and reused C results, including a signedness mutation and a one-element off-by-one mutation. State exactly which load establishes each partition update. A correct middle value is insufficient evidence for a first-occurrence search.

<a id="t36-05"></a>

### T36.05 — Sorting, permutation and stability

Insertion preserves a sorted prefix by keeping one pending record while moving greater predecessors right. Equal keys must stop the shift if the policy is stable. For original tags `(3,A),(1,B),(3,C),(2,D),(1,E)`, the stable output is B, E, D, A, C by key. There are six strict inversions and hence six shift writes; the selected insertion convention makes nine key comparisons and four final placements. Changing `>` to `≥` reverses equal-tag order without violating sortedness or the multiset.

A merge transition needs the same tie policy: with left `(1,B),(3,A)` and right `(1,E),(2,D),(3,C)`, take B before E and A before C. Derive the remaining-input and output-prefix relation, rather than assuming stability follows from sorted inputs. In [PR-T36-03](#pr-t36-03), write only a bounded tagged insertion kernel in one assembly ISA, at most 32 records; retain the already completed T15 merge and heap sorts as differential subjects. Heap sort need not be stable and must not be graded against the stable-tag policy. Sorted/reverse five-key inputs give four/ten insertion comparisons under the declared convention. Submit prefix snapshots, tagged permutation checks and counted work; a shorter measured duration does not prove a lower asymptotic bound.

<a id="t36-06"></a>

### T36.06 — Heap invariants and priority policies

Sift-down begins with both child subtrees already heaps and one possible violation at p. Choose the larger child (left on an equal tie); if it exceeds the parent, exchange them. The parent's old value becomes the only possible violation at the chosen child. In `[5,7,8,3,6,2]`, root children 7 and 8 select index 2, yielding `[8,7,5,3,6,2]`; at index 2 the only child 2 stops the walk. Count one sibling comparison and two parent/child comparisons: three key comparisons, one swap. For `[1,8,7,6,5,4,3]`, the moving path 0→1→3 yields `[8,6,7,1,5,4,3]`.

Translate only this kernel into original assembly in [PR-T36-04](#pr-t36-04), preserving the T14 heap API, max-order and duplicate policy. Check `p<n` before child arithmetic; for n>1 the integer predicate `p<n/2` identifies every node with a left child, including the final single-child parent when n is even. Thus n=6, p=2 has left child 5 and no right child 6; compare the right child only after proving its index<n. The milestone's declared n≤1024 bound, or suitably widened checked arithmetic, protects `2*p+1`. Height bounds the visited levels because p descends; building the entire heap has a different cost argument. The oracle checks supplied transitions and local invariants rather than shipping the target sift code. Acceptance includes no-child, one-child, equal-child and root-replacement cases, multiplicity preservation after every swap and a resource ledger. A final heap with a silently dropped duplicate is still wrong.

<a id="t36-07"></a>

### T36.07 — Trees, rotations and representation-preserving change

A rotation changes links while preserving the inorder relation among whole subtrees. For 30 with left 10 and 10's right 20, the LR repair first rotates 10 left, making 20 the left child of 30 with 10 below it, then rotates 30 right. Final root 20 has children 10 and 30, all leaf heights 1, root height 2. Height updates must follow changed child links; updating only the new root leaves stale metadata. Parent links, unique reachability and a null-height convention are independent obligations.

Deletion can propagate a height change beyond one repaired node. In the original tree root 2, left 1, right 4 with children 3 and 5, deleting 1 leaves root 2 balance−2. A left rotation yields root 4, left 2 with right 3, right 5; inorder becomes 2, 3, 4, 5 and height remains 3. This trace uses a single repair but the reused T14 implementation must still traverse the complete recorded ancestor path. [PR-T36-05](#pr-t36-05) adds certificates to that implementation, including LR/RL cases, duplicate rejection and a multiple-ancestor deletion selected by the learner. It does not rebuild the full AVL tree. Compare searching key 3 in balanced keys 1, 2, 3 (two comparisons) with a right chain (three). Equal answers do not imply equal worst-case depth. Submit recomputed heights/parents and the first stale-metadata counterexample, not just an inorder printout.

<a id="t36-08"></a>

### T36.08 — Hash probes and bounded string matching

An empty slot proves the probe chain ended; a deleted slot only records a past occupant. In the original capacity-eight table, key 22 hashes to 6 and visits 6, 7, 0, 1, 2, 3. Slot 1 is deleted, so stopping there would make later occupants unreachable. Slot 3 is empty, so the answer is absent after six probes. A full table has no empty sentinel: cap the walk at eight probes even for an absent key. Capacity, step rule and hash reduction are representation contracts; low load in one trace does not establish a general expected bound.

Byte spans carry lengths, so embedded zero has no special termination role. Text `[0,97,0,97,0]` contains pattern `[97,0]` at 1 and 3, including overlaps for other patterns. Define empty pattern as all n+1 boundaries and require output capacity before mutation. [PR-T36-06](#pr-t36-06) adds an original assembly bounded lookup over the prior hash representation and a small original C naive span kernel for this exact output API. Reuse the earlier T15 prefix matcher as a comparison implementation; do not rebuild its full preprocessing. Count first-mismatch comparisons and probe visits independently. Evidence must include wrap, tombstone, full table, empty pattern and embedded zero; tests over NUL-terminated printable strings do not exercise this contract.

<a id="t36-09"></a>

### T36.09 — Graph frontiers, shortest paths and historical refinement

BFS settles hop layers because every edge contributes one unit. Weighted paths need tentative distances and selection of the smallest unsettled label. In the original graph A→B 4, A→C1, C→B 1, B→D 1, C→D 5, with E isolated, BFS reports hops 0, 1, 1, 2, unreachable. Weighted settlement A, C, B, D gives distances 0, 1, 2, 3 in that order: B improves from 4 to 2 through C and D from 6 to 3 through B. The predecessor equations reconstruct each finite path; an unreachable vertex has no predecessor or numeric distance.

Adapt the prior T15 solver and T14 queue/heap in [PR-T36-07](#pr-t36-07); add frontier certificates, checked finite-distance addition and an explicit tiny-graph API rather than implementing them again. With a maximum finite value 65534, candidate 65530+10 is a range error, not a wrapped short path. Reject negative weights before mutation. As a reasoning counterexample, A→B 1, A→C2, C→B−3 makes early B settlement wrong: a later route gives−1. The historical Dijkstra paper supplies the tentative/settled mechanism, not the modern C storage contract or a blanket origin for all graph ideas. An independent simple-path enumerator is intentionally exponential and restricted to at most eight vertices. Submit label/settle/predecessor evidence separately from hop results and timing.

<a id="t36-10"></a>

### T36.10 — Higher C abstractions over invariant-preserving kernels

An abstraction exposes operations while hiding enough representation to protect an invariant. A typed value wrapper can store real `Record` objects and copy values into them. An opaque pointer collection instead stores borrowed addresses; freeing the collection does not free its elements unless that is an explicit ownership policy. The two may expose the same ordered `(id,rank)` sequence while requiring different client lifetimes. Comparator context belongs to the ordering contract: rank then id forms a deterministic total order; mutating a borrowed record's rank while it is stored can invalidate the structure even though the pointer stays live.

In [PR-T36-08](#pr-t36-08), adapt one completed container and a new assembly kernel through a typed interface and a context/callback interface. Bound capacity to three for the fixture. A full insertion and duplicate-id insertion preserve the previous state, with duplicate checking taking precedence. Record whether callbacks retain, allocate or reenter; forbid those effects in this component's Profile C boundary. Invalidate handles through a defined generation/status check rather than demonstrating UB. Reuse the T18 ownership ledger and audit undefined symbols/transitive helpers. Acceptance requires equal valid observations from both adapters plus different copy/borrow lifetime explanations, comparator counterexamples and unchanged failure snapshots. Header-level genericity alone does not establish representation independence or portable object access.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

## Reading guidance

Read by milestone, not cover to cover. Start with the short Knuth/Hoare arithmetic-and-invariant spine. Select the CLRS mechanism passages when revisiting the prior implementation; read the historical shortest-path paper beside the original graph trace. ABI and instruction passages are working specifications during hand assembly. Hanson supplies interface/client obligations, while Morin is a C++ conceptual comparison. No source code is a solved C submission. The old SysV ABI draft is explicitly pinned; if a platform uses a different ABI, declare it and adapt outside the fixture assumptions.

The assigned passage hours fit the reading budget; the remainder is for hand derivations, source notes and reconciling observations. Use [guide-reading](#guide-reading) for passage access and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for the C17 baseline.

Project hours already include verification and reconcile exactly with the module's implementation plus verification budget. Do not add them again to route totals.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Assess all 30 objectives through the linked project evidence items. In a 90-minute live gate, derive a previously unseen half-open trace, repair an ABI/liveness bug without changing the C contract, recompute a heap or AVL certificate, and justify one callback/lifetime boundary. Review saved probes/graphs separately. Six assessment hours include preparation and targeted retry. A wrong flag predicate triggers signedness remediation; a stale tree height triggers bottom-up certificate work; a lifetime failure returns to T18. Passing outputs does not waive structural, cost or dependency evidence.

## Consolidation and transfer

After one week, spend two of the six consolidation hours reconstructing a kernel invariant without notes, two reconciling representation/ownership changes, and two replaying a graph/tree mutation with a peer. Keep prior project artifacts linked instead of duplicated. Transfer to a different ABI or storage policy only after restating its contract; use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for feedback and [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) for larger assembly/interface combinations.

## Environment and limits

Profile C applies to the component, with a separately declared Profile A harness. Target educational algorithms cannot delegate to libc or equivalent compiler/runtime helpers without an explicit support allowlist; inspect object/final symbols and disassembly. Typed pools, byte-copy APIs and real allocator callbacks have different C17 storage contracts. Linux x86 execution must use SysV, not assume Windows x64 conventions. Thumb assembly must actually assemble and run under a declared Cortex-M4 ISA environment; a physical board is optional for ISA evidence. Emulator execution is not physical timing, DMA or interrupt-latency evidence.
