<a id="t40-04"></a>

### T40.04 — Network addressing, routing and hop limits

Node IDs A=17, R=34 and B=51 persist across both segments. Link addresses are local: A=1/R.left=2, R.right=1/B=2. Ports 7 and 8 select endpoint services and never choose a route. A datagram for B starts with node source 17, destination 51, hop limit 4 and next protocol 4. R accepts the left frame, copies the packet, decreases hop limit to 3, and creates a right frame from link 1 to link 2. B consumes a positive-hop packet addressed to 51. It does not decrement the packet merely to deliver it.

The six-octet network header contains version, source, destination, hop limit, next protocol and payload length. The only routes are the four versioned entries in the contract. At R, hop limit at most one, unknown destination, an own-origin loop, invalid protocol or a length mismatch produces a counted drop. This is a fixed educational routing rule, not a dynamic discovery protocol.

A router's copy must outlive the input callback, particularly while waiting for its other segment's grant. Poison a released input span and verify the queued output remains correct. The common mistake is to store a pointer into a reusable receive buffer or to carry left link address 2 unchanged onto the right link. [PR-T40-04](#pr-t40-04) requires exact preserved and changed fields, a rebuilt CRC and a private-buffer ownership trace.

<a id="t40-05"></a>

### T40.05 — Reliable bounded transport and flow state

L4 turns unreliable datagrams into complete bounded messages, not a TCP-like byte stream. Its eight-octet header carries DATA/ACK/PROBE, two ports, a transfer ID, fragment index/count and credit. DATA contains 1–24 octets; all non-final fragments contain exactly 24. A message of 25 octets becomes two fragments of 24 and 1, while 120 becomes five of 24. One outstanding fragment and one reassembly tuple per direction keep both memory and protocol state inspectable.

An ACK matches nodes, ports, transfer ID and index before advancing the sender. The receiver remembers an accepted fragment and re-ACKs a duplicate without appending it again. Only the complete message is published. Retain one last completed receipt and a highest-completed ID; ACK an identical repeated last fragment, drop earlier IDs, and replace the receipt only on the next completion. IDs strictly increase within a session and never wrap. A completed SDU awaiting upper consumption holds credit zero. An index/count mismatch fails the candidate instead of stitching bytes from different transfers.

Start the 100-ms retransmission clock after the lower layer actually accepts the fragment for transmission, not while it is still BUSY waiting for a grant. At most three retransmissions use identical bytes and index. Credit zero pauses new DATA; a 100-ms PROBE asks for credit, and an independent 500-ms blocked deadline frees state with a failure event. Duplicate ACKs and probes cannot postpone that deadline indefinitely. ID wrap forces session reopen. In [PR-T40-05](#pr-t40-05), show a dropped ACK, duplicate fragment, credit pause and timeout with no partial publication. A plausible retry count without an exact buffer/state trace is insufficient.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t40-06"></a>

### T40.06 — Session dialogue and resynchronization

L5 adds schema/unit negotiation, dialogue ownership and checkpoints; these are distinct from transport delivery. OPEN and OPEN_ACK agree on nonzero session/epoch, schema 1, unit 1 and initial token A. Their checkpoint is zero, as are TOKEN/CLOSE/ERROR control records. DATA carries the next positive checkpoint for its direction. A cannot send another application DATA while B holds the token, even though transport buffers may be available.

Transferring the token is itself uncertain until transport completion. The sender enters TOKEN_PENDING and sends no new DATA. The receiver changes holder when the complete TOKEN arrives. If its ACK is lost, the former holder remains blocked and a repeated TOKEN changes nothing again. This may pause progress, but never gives both endpoints permission. After A's request and token transfer, B sends the reply and returns the token.

Retained RAM remembers the last committed per-direction checkpoint and payload/response. Same checkpoint plus identical bytes causes no new effect; same checkpoint plus changed bytes is an error. A transport reset can use RESUME only when both peers retain matching session/epoch/checkpoint state. A rebooted peer with no state refuses. Checkpoint wrap requires close/reopen. This is neither authenticated identity nor durable exactly-once processing. [PR-T40-06](#pr-t40-06) asks for a state diagram and effect count that distinguish lost ACK, stale epoch, incompatible negotiation, retained resume and reboot refusal.

<a id="t40-07"></a>

### T40.07 — Presentation syntax and typed representation

L6 begins with schema 1 and ascending unique TLVs. Tags encode verb, request ID, signed value, unit and optional UTF-8 label. Two octets `f0 60` mean signed -4000 in the declared two's-complement 16-bit representation; they do not depend on the host's native byte order or struct padding. Decode through unsigned arithmetic, then convert within a representable signed range. A 16-byte label limit counts UTF-8 octets, not displayed characters.

Stage a decoded record until all TLV syntax, lengths, required fields, units and canonical UTF-8 have passed. Reject duplicate/out-of-order tags, truncated values, overlong encodings, surrogates and unknown schema. A label is display data, never a format string. Presentation validation proves that a typed record can be represented; only L7 decides whether a SET value is allowed for this application.

Implement encode/decode without copying a native struct. Compare a boundary SET, reordered tags and a UTF-8 label split inside a multibyte code point. [PR-T40-07](#pr-t40-07) requires unchanged output sentinels on failure and a round trip with a separately derived wire record. A decoder that silently replaces malformed UTF-8 would violate this canonical contract.

<a id="t40-08"></a>

### T40.08 — Application exchange and seven-layer acceptance

GET returns a declared fixture plant value. SET changes the fixture setpoint only within -4000 through 12500 centidegrees Celsius; ERROR leaves it unchanged. Unit 1 is mandatory for SET and REPLY, and every response correlates the request ID. These are explicit original application semantics; no physical sensor is implied. An otherwise valid session cannot make an out-of-range setpoint acceptable.

Trace SET from A to B through representation, session checkpoint, transport fragments, routed packets and two link frames, then the reply in the reverse direction. Correlate address scopes without expecting identical wire bytes at R. Apply the effect once before replying and keep the recorded response for a valid duplicate checkpoint. The invalid-SET ERROR includes the retained setpoint and a state witness demonstrates unchanged state independently of the error text. GET still returns the separate fixture plant value, not the setpoint.

[PR-T40-08](#pr-t40-08) integrates all eight milestones. Its host fixture deliberately lacks physical evidence, so a correct protocol transcript still reports an open physical gate. Actual acceptance adds two-segment relay captures, corrupt/noisy/truncated frames, dropped ACKs, blocked credit, dialogue violation, retained resume, reboot refusal and cable interruption. Each fault is attributed to the responsible boundary, rather than described vaguely as a network failure.

## Reading guidance

The JSON reading list supplies exact inspected locator strings. X.200 assigns responsibilities; Peterson/Davie explains encapsulation; the TI documents constrain the actual declared wiring and driver enables. Read them against the boundary ledger, not as an implementation recipe. The whole wire format, retry policy and fixture application are original EDU7-v1 decisions. No textbook C solution is supplied. The TI application note is guidance, not complete TIA conformance evidence; component specifications also do not verify an adapter PCB or bench installation.

Allocate the remaining reading hour to the original contract and your layer/API ledger. For current edition, access and inspection limits use [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory). Advanced OSI service definitions outside these selected passages are further study, not required uninspected reading.

## Implementation projects

Complete [boundary ledger](#pr-t40-01) (4 h), [physical adapter and grant scheduler](#pr-t40-02) (8 h), [framer](#pr-t40-03) (6 h), [router](#pr-t40-04) (6 h), [message transport](#pr-t40-05) (10 h), [session](#pr-t40-06) (8 h), [presentation](#pr-t40-07) (8 h), and [whole-stack exchange](#pr-t40-08) (8 h). Keep a host adapter for injected faults and clocks while replacing the physical adapter with target UART/DE operations.

Run `python tools/verify_networking_fixtures.py` in the declared host Python environment to check supplied expected values. It checks finite independent calculations/traces, not your C implementation. Your own tests exercise every listed transition, capacity and publication contract and compare against these oracles. Retain a fixture-to-evidence index using [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit).

## Mastery gate and feedback

For each topic submit the three project evidence items and explain one changed condition without running code. Reconstruct the 87-octet message budget; redraw the lost-token-ACK trace; predict the next-hop rewrite; decode a negative value; and identify which observations establish TC and physical driver release. The reviewer selects at least one unseen split, corruption, route and session reset, then checks unchanged state or exact accepted bytes.

Feedback names the failed boundary and observable invariant. Repair framing by a minimal noise/resynchronization trace, transport by a matching tuple/index ledger, session by effect/token state, and hardware timing by a measured waveform. Repeat the failed gate and one adjacent interaction only. A host-only route can close portable protocol objectives while marking physical objectives pending; it cannot receive a whole-family completion claim.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least several days, rebuild one frame and one lost-ACK/session-resume trace from the versioned contract. Replace the UTF-8 label with a longer legal multibyte label and explain why the byte budget changes while routing does not. Add an optional second application verb by first changing L7/L6 contracts and tests, not by making R interpret it. A second session or dynamic routing is a new design with fresh ownership/state bounds.

Use [guide-workload](#guide-workload), [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) to record the family hours and scope. The extension teaches mechanisms deeply while preserving the original curriculum's foundational ownership and verification work.

## Environment and limits

Profile C executes deterministic host octet/event tests. Profile E uses the three declared boards and two bounded bench segments, with actual MCU clocks/pins and adapter schematics recorded. Firmware evidence must include original layer/state work; supplied solved stack code cannot fulfill it. Wire captures, voltage and termination measurements retain uncertainty and equipment settings. No host model, emulator, replayed capture or synthetic register log establishes electrical safety, timing or a connected physical sensor. There is no encrypted/authenticated session, durable recovery, automatic route discovery or ISO protocol-suite conformance claim.

<a id="t42"></a>

# T42 — From-scratch HTTP server over OS sockets

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP application and Linux systems | core | 96 | A, C |

**Prerequisites:** [T15](#t15), [T18](#t18), [T23](#t23), [T24](#t24), [T32](#t32).

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 | 46 | 18 | 6 | 6 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Build an original bounded HTTP/1.1 origin server in C. It owns incremental octet parsing, framing, routes, serialization, descriptor/buffer lifetime, bounded queues and deadlines. It listens on loopback 127.0.0.1:8080. The OS supplies TCP/IP and lower layers. This is the third communication family; the first is the original seven-layer protocol and the second supplies its own Ethernet-to-TCP implementation. The portable HTTP core developed here is reused by the second family.

## Entry check and remediation

Demonstrate span bounds and retained-pointer lifetimes; predict short read/write/EINTR/EAGAIN behavior; trace an event-loop resource acquisition and cleanup; derive checked integer accumulation. Reuse T15/T18 parsing/ownership and T23/T24 Linux adapters. A failed prediction returns to those exact mechanisms before implementing a larger server. Inspect the shared contract and distinguish octets, TCP stream, HTTP message and application representation. Do not assume that one read contains a request.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t42-01"></a>

### T42.01 — Socket lifecycle and layer ownership

A socket delivers an ordered stream whose chunk boundaries belong to the current call, not to HTTP. OS TCP performs sequence/retransmission work. The application owns descriptor lifecycle, byte retention and message interpretation. Reuse the earlier Linux accept/event adapter, then attach four explicitly owned connection records. Accept readiness is only a hint: another action can consume the pending connection, so EAGAIN returns to the event loop. On Linux an accepted descriptor does not inherit the listener's nonblocking status; set and verify flags explicitly. A failed initialization must close the descriptor exactly once before publishing a record.

Trace accepted descriptors 11,12,13,14 into four slots. Descriptor 15 cannot acquire a slot and is closed. Releasing 12 allows 16 to enter; no reference to 12 may survive in a queued event. Add a generation number to distinguish a recycled descriptor number from the old connection. Record this invariant: every live descriptor has one owner and every published record has a valid descriptor. A readable listener does not guarantee a successful accept, and an open socket does not establish an HTTP session. Evidence includes flag inspection, an accept-race trace, injected exhaustion, resource counters and an explicit layer-ownership map.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t42-01-a"></a>


- **T42.01.a** Create a loopback listener and bounded accepted-connection table with explicit descriptor flags and cleanup. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-01](#pr-t42-01).


<a id="t42-01-b"></a>


- **T42.01.b** Separate application/parser ownership from OS TCP/IP and physical responsibilities. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-01](#pr-t42-01).


<a id="t42-01-c"></a>


- **T42.01.c** Handle accept/readiness races and descriptor-limit failures without blocking the event loop or leaking state. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-01](#pr-t42-01).


<a id="t42-02"></a>

### T42.02 — Incremental request grammar and target authority

Treat input as bounded octets. A recv call may stop between CR and LF, between a field name and colon, or inside a request target. Save state and the precise consumed offset; never append a NUL then assume all octets are text. The strict project grammar uses one SP between request-line elements and CRLF delimiters. Field names use the HTTP token alphabet and case-insensitive matching; whitespace before the colon, folding, NUL and invalid controls cause rejection before publication. Strict recipient policy is allowed here but is not a claim that the RFC has no tolerant parsing provisions.

For a GET header ending at offset 46, feed prefixes of lengths 0 through 46. Every proper prefix reports NEED_MORE with no complete request; the final LF completes the header once. Feeding two headers in one span completes only the first and returns its consumed length, leaving the second unchanged. Absolute-form http://localhost:8080/health selects authority localhost:8080, even if the syntactically valid single Host says other.example. Origin-form uses the single Host. Validate bounded configured host/port authorities; do not implement filesystem normalization. Missing/duplicate/malformed HTTP/1.1 Host returns 400 and close. A complete header is not yet a complete body. Retain split/coalescing, target-authority and smallest malformed-octet evidence.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.


<a id="t42-02-a"></a>

<a id="t42-02-b"></a>


- **T42.02.b** Validate the declared origin-form and bounded absolute-form targets and the single HTTP1.1 Host contract. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-02](#pr-t42-02).


<a id="t42-02-c"></a>


- **T42.02.c** Reject ambiguous whitespace, control bytes and obsolete folding before publishing a request. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-02](#pr-t42-02).


<a id="t42-03"></a>

### T42.03 — Header normalization and unambiguous message framing

After headers, select exactly one body mode. The method name does not define the wire boundary: a GET can carry framed content, while a POST without length fields has zero request-body length. This project consumes a framed body before routing even when a route later rejects it. NONE means zero body; LENGTH requires exact unsigned decimal syntax; CHUNKED means the decoder owns termination. Header lookup must retain duplicate occurrence counts rather than overwriting one field with another.

Derive a checked decimal accumulation condition before each multiply/add using the declared maximum 4294967295. Then apply the 1024-byte body cap. An overflowing numeral is 400; a representable declared body above the cap is 413. Identical duplicate Content-Length is conservatively400+close. TE+CL is always400+close, rather than choosing whichever parser seems convenient. Check syntax and framing before unsupported decoding: a request whose final coding is not chunked is 400+close. Thus gzip alone and chunked,gzip are 400. Repeated chunked, malformed token lists and chunked parameters are 400. A valid gzip,chunked list is framed but requires an unsupported decoder, so it is 501+close. The declared strict profile rejects other parameterized coding lists with 400; this is a syntax-subset policy. For LENGTH 5 and input abcdeGET..., consume exactly five body octets; GET belongs to the next message. Premature EOF after four bytes is incomplete and cannot dispatch a successful echo. Produce the framing-decision table, byte-conservation ledger and overflow counterexamples.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t42-03-b"></a>


- **T42.03.b** Reject duplicate lengths, TE+CL, overflow and unsupported coding with the exact error/close policy. **Disposition:** core. **Activity:** [PR-T42-03](#pr-t42-03).

<a id="t42-04"></a>

### T42.04 — Chunked decoding, extensions and trailers

Chunked transfer encoding is a framing grammar. Maintain SIZE_LINE, DATA, DATA_CRLF, TRAILERS and COMPLETE states with independent counters. Hex accumulation and aggregate size are checked before accepting bytes. A valid bounded unknown extension is syntactically parsed and ignored; rejecting every unknown extension would evade the receiver contract. Trailer fields are validated in separate bounded storage and discarded. They never replace Host, Content-Length or routing decisions.

Trace 3;x=y CRLF abc CRLF 2 CRLF de CRLF 0 CRLF X-Debug: ignored CRLF CRLF. The representation is the five octets abcde. The zero-size chunk ends data but does not finish the message until the trailer section's final empty line. A CR split across reads is still pending state, not an optional delimiter. The supplied invalid trace puts X where the data-ending CR belongs and returns 400+close; the incomplete trace has no terminal empty line and publishes no body. Check every byte split, extension/trailer capacities and EOF in every state. Keep decoded content separate from wire byte counts; the wire overhead is not echoed.

<a id="t42-05"></a>

### T42.05 — HTTP semantics, routing and response serialization

Routing begins only after a complete admissible request, except that header-determined errors and 100-continue need early handling. GET and HEAD /health select the representation hex `6f6b0a`: three octets, including LF. HEAD sends its GET-equivalent Content-Length: 3 with no representation body. POST /echo returns identical bounded octets, including NUL and non-UTF8 values. Unknown route returns 404. A recognized method disallowed on the selected route returns 405 and route-specific Allow; an unknown method returns 501. Declare bounded supported methods GET, HEAD, POST and distinguish recognition from permission.

Every HEAD response suppresses content, including error responses. HEAD /unknown therefore reports the selected ten-octet error representation length and sends zero body octets. HEAD /echo reports 405 with Allow: POST and the selected nineteen-octet error length, again with no body. Preserve representation metadata separately from actual serialized content.

For an admissible POST with Expect: 100-continue and body not yet received, enqueue the interim 100 immediately, then wait for the framed body. If headers already establish an error, enqueue that final error instead. Waiting for the body before 100 can deadlock a cooperative client. Emit Date using a reasonable UTC clock; fixture epoch 1672531200 yields Sun, 01 Jan 2023 00:00:00 GMT in the required fixed-date format. Use a separate monotonic clock for deadlines. Length is an octet count, not Unicode character count. User data never becomes unchecked header syntax or a format string. Evidence includes exact serialization, binary echo, HEAD boundary, Allow and expectation traces.

<a id="t42-06"></a>

### T42.06 — Partial output, persistence and pipelining

Keep immutable response storage until every queued byte is locally accepted or the connection aborts. A send of four bytes advances the offset by four; EINTR and EAGAIN advance it by zero. Sending again from offset 0 duplicates output. POLLOUT interest is needed only while pending bytes remain; a permanent writable interest can spin an otherwise idle event loop. Local send success is not evidence that the peer application consumed the response.

For nine output octets and results 4, EINTR, 2, EAGAIN, 3, the retained offsets are 4, 4, 6, 6, 9. A two-entry request queue holds requests 1, 2 and pauses parsing 3. Persistent responses remain FIFO even if their computation costs differ. The default maximum is four requests per connection; the fourth response announces close. If request 2 requests Connection:close, 3 is never dispatched. Drain the final response, shutdown the write direction, then receive/discard remaining bytes only until EOF or the 1000 ms drain deadline, and close. The discarded bytes are not new requests. Record read backpressure, output retention, FIFO and close-state transitions with tiny-send and coalesced-input tests.

Interim responses preserve association too. If a pipelined second request expects 100-continue, queue its interim response after the first request's final response and before its own final response. Decide on 100 as soon as the admissible headers are complete; that decision cannot preempt an earlier response's bytes. Apply bounded output backpressure while the client waits for the ordered interim response.

<a id="t42-07"></a>

### T42.07 — Deadlines, resource limits and transport failure

Resource limits are part of the state machine. Idle activity and total elapsed request time are independent. A byte every four seconds can keep a five-second idle timer fresh while violating a fifteen-second total request deadline. Do not renew the total deadline on every byte. Bound headers at 8192 octets, 32 fields, target 1024 octets, body 1024 octets, extension 128 octets per chunk and trailer 1024 octets/eight fields; apply limits before storing. Track four connections, two complete queued requests and four requests per connection. Derive actual memory from chosen representations, including retained spans, output, queues and error paths.

With request start 0, progress at 4000, 8000, 12000, 14900 ms and now 15000 ms, idle has not expired but the total deadline has. A request timeout returns bounded 408+close where output remains usable; output timeout aborts and makes no completed-response claim. POLLHUP may arrive with readable buffered bytes: consume those before treating recv 0 as EOF. A half-close after a complete request can still allow its response; one inside a declared body remains incomplete. EPIPE/reset aborts output and releases ownership. Retain monotonic-clock traces, failure-state distinctions and allocator/descriptor high-water evidence rather than calling every close successful.

### T42.08 — Parsing security and independent interoperability

A parser boundary is a security boundary because two participants can disagree on where a request ends. Compare your exact framing decisions with an independent raw client and the current RFC contract. A mature client is an oracle peer, not permission to import an HTTP parser/server library. Reject unsupported CONNECT or Upgrade with a final error and close; optimistic following bytes never become another dispatched request. RFC 9931's inspected CONNECT proxy requirements are background authority, while this origin-server rejection policy is an original declared policy.

Run curl for GET, HEAD, binary POST and expected 100-continue behavior, and a separate raw-octet peer for duplicate lengths, TE+CL, invalid controls, chunks, pipelines and half-close. Packet segmentation, socket read chunks and HTTP messages are three different units. Save normalized status/header/body results and exact byte traces where framing matters. Test that the same request under all partitions produces one result and that a close/error prevents any second application effect. Publish component/source/dependency ownership, unresolved deviations and limits. Plain loopback HTTP has no TLS, proxy or production deployment claim. Static fixture checks cannot replace executing and inspecting the learner's original C.

## Reading guidance

Read UNP for the short-I/O mechanism, then extract the current Linux return/error and readiness rules. Its blocking helpers are explanation rather than event-loop code to copy. Read RFC 9112 in the order grammar → framing → chunking → persistence/teardown, constructing a decision table for the project instead of reading the entire protocol at once. RFC 9110 supplies method/expectation/Date semantics; it cannot replace wire-framing rules. RFC 9931 updates HTTP/1.1 transition security with explicitly scoped CONNECT proxy requirements.

The assigned table contains exact inspected passages. Adjacent RFC sections may be consulted as reference; assigning new obligatory passages requires inspection and registry extension. Distinguish the RFC obligation, a stricter original resource/syntax policy and an excluded capability in the evidence ledger. Current primary contracts take precedence over old textbook behavior.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Every topic needs separate a,b,c evidence. Defend one successful path and one minimized failure without reading the implementation. Publish a byte-conservation ledger and demonstrate identical semantic results under every selected partition/coalescing of the input. Show one output backpressure trace, one deadline that survives slow progress, and one close/error followed by apparent request bytes with no second dispatch. The complete gate includes actual original C execution with independent curl/raw peers, current source contracts, memory/descriptor limits, symbol/dependency inspection and delayed reconstruction.

A fixture verifier checks static oracles only. Parser bugs, send success, coverage percentages and cooperative-client success do not establish every HTTP receiver requirement. Minimize disagreement before changing the contract. A body/framing defect returns to the portable parser; an event/lifetime defect returns to the adapter. Record excluded features and unresolved actual execution explicitly.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least one day reconstruct framing precedence, HEAD length and the partial-send invariant from memory. Change a split, duplicate header, EOF point or timeout boundary and predict the new result. Carry the accepted portable parser/serializer into T41 through a span/event adapter. Keep its original project IDs and hours; the new adapter must demonstrate preservation of bytes and ownership over custom TCP rather than charge for rewriting HTTP again. See the communication-family guide for the cross-domain route.

## Environment and limits

The hosted executable uses profile A; parser/router/serializer components use profile C with caller storage, allowed type headers and explicit time/config callbacks. Audit compiler helpers and callbacks separately; no external HTTP library implements the studied mechanisms. Linux-specific MSG_NOSIGNAL, descriptor flags and poll behavior are declared platform contracts. curl and raw clients are verification peers only. The server is plain loopback HTTP with bounded routes, not TLS, a proxy, a filesystem server, a tunnel or a production deployment. Hardware lower-layer closure belongs to T40/T41 and cannot be claimed from these sockets.

## Purpose and outcomes

Implement the packet and state work of a **custom minimal Ethernet-to-HTTP stack** on NUCLEO-F439ZI. The MCU provides an Ethernet MAC/DMA controller; the fitted LAN8742A, magnetics and cable provide actual physical signaling. Your original C owns the selected driver, Ethernet/ARP, IPv4/ICMP, passive TCP and HTTP adapter. Register definitions are permissible aids, while a vendor Ethernet driver, lwIP or an OS TCP/IP stack cannot perform the owned mechanism work.

This is a controlled, same-link interoperability profile, with board 192.0.2.2/24, peer 192.0.2.1/24 and server port 8080. The [original contract](research/enhancement/networking_contracts.json) excludes DHCP, DNS, routing, IP reassembly/options, general congestion growth and several TCP services. Successful exchanges with a declared cooperative client do not establish general RFC host or IEEE conformance. The Internet suite also does not map one-for-one onto OSI's seven layers: HTTP can include several upper-layer concerns, TCP supplies transport, and the PHY/MAC boundary still requires explicit physical evidence.

Eight milestones contribute **72 implementation and verification hours** once. The portable HTTP parser/serializer projects in T42 are prerequisite work reused here; their hours belong to T42 and are not added again. Physical bring-up and protocol logic remain independently reviewable.

## Entry check and remediation

Before driver work, reconstruct a T29 DMA ownership transition and show which SRAM regions are Ethernet-DMA accessible on the recorded F439 target. Before packet work, safely decode a bounded big-endian integer and prove every nested length lies within its enclosing span. Before final HTTP integration, complete T42.02–T42.05's portable grammar/framing/chunk/serializer evidence; the hosted multi-connection event-loop milestones need not precede this board's one-connection adapter.

Targeted mathematics covers unsigned modular subtraction with live intervals below 2^31, one's-complement end-around carry, powers/masks, and weighted means for SRTT/RTTVAR. If sequence wrap is unclear, first draw a 16-value ring and compare intervals shorter than eight; then apply the same reasoning to 32 bits. If checksum carry is unclear, add three 16-bit words on paper and repeatedly fold high carries before complementing. These are local repairs, not a prerequisite general mathematics course.

Pin the exact board marking, RM0090 Rev21, UM1974 Rev8, inspected LAN8742A datasheet revision, compiler/linker and host adapter settings using [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles), [guide-inventory](#guide-inventory) and [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory). Verify clock and board pin configuration from earlier T27/T28 work rather than guessing from another STM32 board.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t41-01"></a>

### T41.01 — Protocol subset, interfaces and bounded resources

Each input span has a local interpretation. Ethernet supplies an entire frame beginning with DA. IPv4 supplies a datagram whose total length excludes Ethernet padding. TCP supplies a sequence-space segment, but the HTTP consumer receives an ordered byte stream with no preserved packet boundaries. Do not cast all three into one native struct or use Ethernet receive length as an HTTP body length.

Declare immutable borrowed spans for synchronous receive; owned slots for queued transmit data; and explicit consume counts for the HTTP stream adapter. Packet validation publishes nothing on failure. A TX DMA completion permits reuse of that DMA buffer but does not acknowledge the TCP bytes: their immutable retransmission copy remains until valid ACK. A full queue returns BUSY without consuming caller bytes. Link-down invalidates the transport incarnation and reports an abort rather than pretending all queued data reached the application.

For a TCP payload of 3 octets with fixed IPv4/TCP headers, 20+20+3=43 IPv4 octets, plus 14 Ethernet octets gives 57. MAC padding brings the frame from DA through padding to 60, then FCS yields 64. Preamble/SFD and interframe gap are physical/MAC behavior outside the driver's DA-starting span. [PR-T41-01](#pr-t41-01) produces the scope/API/length ledger and a bounded memory budget. The trap is labeling all exclusions as optional standards features instead of acknowledging that a full IPv4 host must do more.

<a id="t41-02"></a>

### T41.02 — Ethernet PHY, RMII and physical readiness

The F439 Ethernet block speaks RMII to an external PHY. LAN8742A converts that digital interface to actual cable signaling through magnetics. Its 50-MHz reference and the selected board pins/bridges are functional dependencies, not observations proven by a packet fixture. Configure RMII during the documented reset/clock sequence, confirm actual reference operation, then use MDIO to read the fitted PHY's identity and status.

The inspected identity is register 2 = 0x0007 and register 3 masked by 0xfff0 = 0xc130; the low nibble records silicon revision. Reset bit 15 of control register 0 self-clears. Use a recorded finite reset/MDIO deadline rather than an infinite busy loop. Basic Status link bit 2 is latch-low: reading 0x0020 then 0x0024 means a down condition was latched and the current link is up, not that the second value erased the event. Negotiation completion also requires the selected status fields.

Register 31 has negotiation-done bit 12 and speed bits 4:2. Codes 001/101 mean 10 half/full, 010/110 mean 100 half/full. Thus 0x1018 indicates completed 100-Mbit full duplex. Only supported full-duplex results enable this profile; MAC DM/FES must match the actual outcome. [PR-T41-02](#pr-t41-02) checks numeric decoding and actual clock/link/reset/cable captures. PHY IDs do not prove a clock exists, and a TAP or mocked status register cannot close this topic's physical gate.

<a id="t41-03"></a>

### T41.03 — MAC and Ethernet DMA descriptor lifecycle

Use four RX and two TX normal, 16-byte descriptors, each paired with one 2048-byte buffer in DMA-accessible SRAM, not CCM. Disable enhanced descriptors and timestamps; DSL=0 gives contiguous descriptors. The final RX uses RER, the final TX TER; chained mode is off. Buffer 1 has the exact RX size or TX byte count, and buffer 2 is unused. This costs 6×2048+6×16=12384 bytes before higher-layer queues.

Initialize complete buffers/descriptor controls, apply the target's required ordering, then publish OWN. CPU may inspect payload/status only after DMA clears OWN. For TX, normal TDES0 holds OWN31, IC30, LS29, FS28 and TER21; DC27=0 and DP26=0 request MAC CRC/padding and CIC23:22=0 disables transmit checksum offload. DMA writeback resets transmit control fields, so reconstruct them on every reuse. The earlier generic operation paragraph's IC reference conflicts with the normal-descriptor detail; use the inspected normal description, not the generic reference.

For RX, require OWN clear, FS+LS, no error summary/descriptor error and FL in 64..1518. CSTF=APCS=0 retains FCS, so expose FL-4 bytes beginning DA. A minimum FL=64 exposes 60; do not subtract the four bytes again in Ethernet. Store-and-forward is enabled for RX/TX; bad/undersized forwarding and checksum offload are disabled. Configure list bases only while stopped. Poll status with defined W1C masks, refill a suspended ring before poll demand and stop service on fatal bus error. [PR-T41-03](#pr-t41-03) combines the finite ownership oracle with actual ring wrap and descriptor reuse. Volatile alone does not order ordinary packet stores or grant CPU ownership.

<a id="t41-04"></a>

### T41.04 — Ethernet demultiplexing and ARP neighbor state

Untagged Ethernet II carries DA, SA and a big-endian type. This profile accepts local unicast and ARP broadcast, types 0x0800/0x0806, and drops VLAN/foreign traffic. Hardware perfect filtering is an aid; the software contract still validates its inputs. The board's locally administered fixture MAC is 02:00:00:00:00:02; actual peer MAC is observed and recorded, not assumed from the fixture.

ARP does not use an IPv4 wrapper. Its 28-octet Ethernet/IPv4 payload declares hardware type 1, protocol 0x0800, lengths 6/4 and opcode 1 or 2. Check those and enclosing length before reading variable fields; require ARP sender MAC to equal Ethernet SA. Only the configured peer IP can enter the one-entry cache. Reply to requests for the local IP, expire learned state after 30 seconds, retain at most one queued datagram, and issue at most three resolution requests one second apart.

An unresolved neighbor is a bounded resolution failure rather than permission to overwrite the only queue. Learning a tuple establishes a local address association, not authentication. A poisoned source field must never silently redirect the queued TCP packet. [PR-T41-04](#pr-t41-04) checks exact ARP wire bytes, mismatch/expiry/drop outcomes and an actual request/reply capture on the isolated link.

<a id="t41-05"></a>

### T41.05 — IPv4, ICMP echo and Internet checksum

Accept version 4, IHL 5, total length 20..1500 within the received span, TTL positive, valid header checksum, local destination and configured peer source. Protocol is ICMP or TCP. Emit DF=1, MF=0, offset=0, ID=0, TTL=64. Dropping options and all fragments is an explicit restricted-profile omission: full-host reassembly requirements do not disappear merely because the lab avoids fragments.

The Internet checksum adds big-endian 16-bit words with end-around carry and then complements the folded sum. An odd final octet is the high byte of a zero-padded word. Byte `61` contributes 0x6100, not 0x0061. Bound accumulation or fold periodically so the host integer cannot overflow. TCP's checksum covers its IPv4 pseudo-header, TCP header/options and payload; IPv4 header checksum alone says nothing about transport integrity.

Echo accepts ICMP type 8, code 0 and at most 64 payload bytes with valid checksum. Reply type 0 preserves identifier, sequence and every payload octet, then recomputes the checksum. With five echoed bytes, IP length is 33; Ethernet length before padding is 47, requiring 13 zero pad bytes to reach 60. [PR-T41-05](#pr-t41-05) independently derives those checksum/length expectations and adds default 56-byte real ping. A successful ping proves neither TCP nor HTTP framing.

<a id="t41-06"></a>

### T41.06 — TCP handshake, sequence and close state

Listen passively on 8080 for one connection. Validate tuple, checksum, header/data offset and options before state mutation. Advertise MSS 256 and use min(256, peer MSS or default 536) for sending. Parse EOL/NOP/MSS and skip well-formed unknown length-coded options; malformed lengths drop. Do not negotiate scaling/SACK/timestamps/ECN. Unsupported urgent data or SYN payload has a recorded restricted-profile outcome rather than a false full-TCP claim.

Sequence numbers lie on a 2^32 ring; all live spans stay below 2^31. SYN and FIN each consume one, pure ACK consumes zero. Starting peer SYN at 0xfffffff0 gives RCV.NXT=0xfffffff1. Sixteen accepted bytes move it to 1. A repeated segment contributes zero new bytes; an overlapping segment starting at 0xfffffff9 with twelve bytes has eight old bytes and four new, moving it to 5. Ordinary unsigned less-than fails across this wrap. Use explicit modular interval predicates whose preconditions are checked.

Reject an ACK beyond SND.NXT before freeing output. Update the peer window only with the inspected SND.WL1/WL2 guards; stale ACKs cannot roll it backward. Trim to an admissible in-order span and ACK gaps without retaining an out-of-order queue. Exact-RCV.NXT RST aborts; an in-window unequal RST sends a challenge ACK and no effect, outside-window RST drops. This is not authentication.

Trace LISTEN→SYN-RECEIVED→ESTABLISHED and active/passive close, FIN-WAIT-1/2, CLOSE-WAIT, LAST-ACK, CLOSING and TIME-WAIT. A peer FIN is a half-close, not successful completion of an incomplete HTTP body. Hold active-close TIME-WAIT for 240 seconds using MSL=120; a repeated remote FIN restarts it. [PR-T41-06](#pr-t41-06) requires a transition ledger, overlap bytes and separate reset/half-close observations, including actual packet captures after host state tests.

<a id="t41-07"></a>

### T41.07 — TCP timers, flow pressure and conservative sending

Retransmission and flow state are separate. RTO begins at 1000 ms, estimates from unambiguous RTT samples and backs off after timeout; receiver window expresses storage, while cwnd expresses a sending restriction. The profile keeps at most one outstanding segment and fixed conservative cwnd of one effective MSS. This bounded policy is intentionally slower than a full Internet implementation and does not demonstrate congestion growth, fast recovery or all event obligations.

For the first 80-ms sample, SRTT=80 and RTTVAR=40. With the next sample 120, update RTTVAR first: 0.75×40+0.25×|80-120|=40; then SRTT=0.875×80+0.125×120=85. Raw RTO 85+4×40=245 becomes 1000 under the minimum. No ambiguous retransmitted sample enters this calculation. Timeout events after an initial send occur at 1000, 3000, 7000 ms with three retransmissions, then the explicit finite resource abort at 15000. Cap RTO at 60000; a SYN retransmission keeps post-handshake initial data RTO at least 3000.

Keep the unacknowledged byte copy until ACK, even after TX DMA completes. Zero peer window pauses new data; a probe on the current RTO/backoff schedule requests an update without consuming another application byte. Local advertised window follows actual retained RX capacity and reopens when the parser consumes it. [PR-T41-07](#pr-t41-07) verifies clocked samples, ignored ambiguous samples, zero-window/reopen and no duplicate delivery. It also compares the omitted general behavior explicitly rather than calling a one-segment sender a complete congestion controller.

<a id="t41-08"></a>

### T41.08 — HTTP reuse, independent interoperability and physical closure

Attach the existing T42 portable parser/serializer through a stream adapter. Its byte grammar, Content-Length/chunked rules, Host/target validation, trailer limits and error-close policy stay the same. Configure one connection, queue depth one, one request and Connection: close. GET/HEAD /health uses the three-octet representation hex 6f6b0a; POST /echo preserves bounded binary octets. The shared fixed-order response fixture is an original serializer policy, not a universal RFC field-order rule.

Set the adapter's configured authority to `192.0.2.2:8080`; the hosted profile uses its separately declared loopback authority. This changes configuration and I/O callbacks, not parser grammar or Host validation. The fixed epoch 1672531200 belongs only to deterministic fixtures. Actual cable responses use a recorded reasonable UTC callback or initialized clock for Date, separate from the monotonic TCP clock. If no reasonable UTC is available, omit Date as allowed by the inspected RFC9110 Date rule and record that response variant; do not call the fixture's historical date current.

TCP can ACK bytes retained for the parser before an HTTP request is complete. A callback passes arbitrary accepted prefixes; preserve each consume count and leftover octet. Serialize once, retain immutable response bytes while segmenting at effective MSS/window, and free them only under the declared acknowledgment/completion rules. Send FIN after all response bytes are acknowledged. Error requests close without interpreting optimistic trailing bytes as a second request.

[PR-T41-08](#pr-t41-08) correlates independent captures for ARP, echo, handshake, exact HTTP semantics, loss/retry, zero window and close. Remove/reconnect the cable and reset the board; show link down aborts the old incarnation and new requests belong to a recorded new one. A replayed pcap or hosted TAP closes finite protocol tests only. The full family closes only with actual fitted PHY/clock, cable operation, original driver/state work and independent client evidence.

## Reading guidance

The exact reading locators are in the front matter. Board/manual/PHY readings constrain the chosen physical and driver setup; RFC readings constrain packet/state mathematics. Allocate the remaining reading hour to the original contract and omitted-requirements matrix. RM0090 is the actually inspected English Rev21 and UM1974 the actually inspected English Rev8; later catalog revisions have uninspected deltas. Register scopes cover only the normal polled, untimestamped, software-checksum profile. No whole Ethernet chapter, analog PHY certification or complete TCP event/congestion algorithm is implied.

Use [guide-reading](#guide-reading) and [guide-standards](#guide-standards) for source access and version records. T42's exact HTTP readings remain attached to the reused parser work; this module does not pretend to inspect or assign an entire HTTP RFC again.

## Implementation projects

Complete [scope and API ledger](#pr-t41-01) (4 h), [physical readiness](#pr-t41-02) (8 h), [custom MAC/DMA driver](#pr-t41-03) (10 h), [Ethernet/ARP](#pr-t41-04) (8 h), [IPv4/ICMP](#pr-t41-05) (8 h), [TCP state](#pr-t41-06) (12 h), [timers and flow](#pr-t41-07) (12 h), and [HTTP/cable closure](#pr-t41-08) (10 h). Stage every 12-hour milestone into a first host checkpoint and a second integration checkpoint without adding hours.

Run `python tools/verify_networking_fixtures.py` for the supplied finite arithmetic and trace expectations. Independently execute your C against packet/event adapters and the board. Reuse T42's wire fixture without copying its hours or delegating custom TCP to the OS. Keep captures and failure attribution alongside the evidence index from [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit).

## Mastery gate and feedback

Explain an unseen retained-FCS receive length, rebuild a reused TDES0, decode two latch-low status reads, checksum an odd payload and predict a modular overlap. Then reconstruct a close and RTO trace from state, not from remembered packet pictures. A reviewer injects a malformed option, ACK beyond SND.NXT, zero window and incomplete HTTP half-close; rejected inputs must neither free unacknowledged bytes nor publish partial application requests.

Repair the smallest failed invariant: a hardware-mode ledger for negotiation, a descriptor ownership log for reuse, a nested-length/checksum witness for parsing, or a state/sequence/clock table for TCP. Retest that invariant and one adjacent layer interaction. Require the per-topic three evidence items; an HTTP 200 alone cannot replace physical, ownership or failure evidence. Host-only progress records its pending physical objectives clearly.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, recompute the wrap and second RTT example, then change one MSS and one odd payload length. Explain why packet boundaries and MAC padding change while HTTP semantics do not. Port the HTTP core to the board adapter without changing parser contracts. An optional second connection or IP fragmentation adds state/resource obligations and requires a new specification and source scope, rather than silently removing declared limits.

Use [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap), [guide-workload](#guide-workload) and [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) to schedule T42 portable leaves before this family's final adapter. Keep the 72 project hours here, the existing parser hours there, and observed integration evidence in both cross-references.

## Environment and limits

Use a dedicated isolated Ethernet adapter and short cable, with no default route, Internet bridge, DHCP or DNS. Record actual peer MAC, adapter offload settings and capture point; offloads can alter what a host capture shows, so do not label a missing displayed checksum as a wire failure without checking that environment. Plain HTTP has no TLS or authentication claim. Fixture ISNs are deterministic; physical isolated-lab incarnation policy is documented separately and is no production security guarantee.

Profile C supplies packets/register mocks and virtual clocks. Profile E supplies actual PHY/RMII/MAC/DMA/cable measurements. Neither host mocks, QEMU, TAP, replayed captures nor a loopback client establishes physical L1 completion. Exact subset interoperability and full-host conformance are separate claims; the omitted-requirements matrix remains part of acceptance even when all cooperative-client tests pass.

## Purpose and outcomes

Explain an algorithm's cost and measure a component without turning one kind of evidence into another. This module deepens accepted C containers/algorithms, paired assembly kernels and hosted/firmware adapters with explicit analysis certificates and bounded observation protocols. Fourteen topics produce forty-two separate mastery claims; twelve small projects add 102 hours of new implementation/verification. With reading 18, assessment 8 and consolidation 6, total workload is 134 hours. Prior builds remain credited to their original modules.

The target result is a reproducible decision dossier: proved model bounds, independently checked finite traces, actual runtime observations and conditional hardware evidence each carry their own scope. Profiles C, A and optional E describe different implementation/harness/firmware boundaries, not interchangeable results.

## Entry check and remediation

Bring accepted T13/T15/T18/T23/T34 artifacts and the selected assembly/cache/quantitative and counter/deadline preludes in the front card. Before projects, explain a valid span/lifetime, one accepted short transfer, one potential initial state, the units of cycles/frequency and the difference between all-thread CPU and elapsed time. Calculate 64 cycles at 16 MHz and identify why a historical memory peak cannot identify a new run.

If an answer fails, return to that exact accepted contract, write a six-row trace and repair the missing owner-domain evidence. Do not rebuild a sorting suite or file layer inside T43. The conditional firmware work has additional exact project gates; the captured/static core route remains explicitly non-silicon evidence. No T44/T45 completion is a prerequisite.

## Study sequence and teaching

Begin with cost models and prefix reasoning, then add space/traffic/component boundaries, clock protocols and tool observations. Keep a running evidence ledger. Reserve PR-T43-03's final verification for the concluding multi-measure decision rather than spending another project budget.


<a id="t43-01"></a>

### T43.01 — Cost contracts and observable work

A complexity statement needs a cost contract. The same sort can have n records, four-byte keys and a variable-size comparator payload: those are different size measures. “One comparison” is constant only in a model that fixes its cost. Declare successful and failed operations, output size and the case quantifier before counting. Then choose a work vector instead of prematurely collapsing comparisons, moves and probes into a time estimate.

For [4,2,5,2,1,4], each earlier key greater than a later key must cross it under insertion sorting. Eight inverted pairs explain eight shifts. The scan also makes stopping comparisons, giving eleven comparisons; five final placements add to thirteen destination writes. Equal keys illustrate why comparisons can occur with no shift. Trace these events on the accepted T15 kernel in [PR-T43-01](#pr-t43-01), preserving stability.

The misconception is that a profiler number supplies the omitted model. It does not: instrumented event counts, retired instructions, target cycles and a static CFG measure have different definitions. Mastery evidence names all boundaries and predicts the count vector before running C.

### T43.02 — Asymptotic bounds and finite scaling evidence

Big-O says there exist a positive constant c and threshold n₀ bounding the named function above thereafter. Big-Ω supplies a lower bound; a tight Θ statement needs both. For f(n)=3n²+5n+7 and n≥1, n≤n² and 1≤n² give 3n²≤f(n)≤15n². The constants are witnesses; deleting lower terms without the quantifier is not a proof. The worst-case function is the maximum cost over valid inputs of a given size, so a lower bound on that maximum does not assert every input costs as much.

Output matters: a traversal contract 3V+2E+Z yields O(V+E+Z) under fixed record/edge work. If output generation emits Z records, an expression that erases Z may miss the dominant cost. Use [PR-T43-01](#pr-t43-01) for the quantified proof and multi-parameter worksheet.

Measured slopes are finite evidence. A function equal to n through 128 and n² afterwards looks linear at 2,4,8,16, yet costs 16900 at 130. Construct that counterexample and explain why an upper bound is neither necessarily tight nor a universal finite-size speed ranking.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-03"></a>

### T43.03 — Aggregate, accounting and potential analysis

Amortized analysis bounds a sequence without a probability distribution. A table growth may cost Θ(m) once while total cost over many appends is linear. Aggregate analysis adds actual costs; accounting precharges operations and keeps nonnegative credit; potential records stored work in state. Each method must name its initial state and cost primitive.

Twelve appends from an empty doubling table cost 27 unit insert/copy operations, with the ninth append alone costing 9. Charging 3 per append gives 9 credits left after twelve and no negative prefix. For Φ=2·live−capacity, Φ₀=0 and Φ₁₂=8, so Σĉ=Σc+Φ₁₂−Φ₀=35. The initial append costs amortized 2; later ones cost 3. This is a deterministic expansion certificate, not an expected average over workloads.

In [PR-T43-02](#pr-t43-02), extend the accepted T14 table with prefix rows and a nonempty-initial-state variant. Preserve allocation-failure behavior separately. Unit copies exclude allocator latency, cache stalls and arbitrary destructor work. Show actual rows, the telescoping identity and the 96-byte transient old/new payload capacity before claiming mastery.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-04"></a>

### T43.04 — From work to instructions, cycles and bottlenecks

An executed instruction count depends on the selected path and generated code. A cycle model additionally depends on the target's instruction/stall assumptions; elapsed time depends on clock and observation boundary. The processor equation IC×CPI/f helps separate these terms. A linear primitive count can cross cache/branch thresholds or run under different clocks, so it need not produce a universal linear-cycle relation.

The original mix 100×1+40×2+20×4 gives 260 cycles for 160 instructions: CPI 1.625. At 100 MHz, that is 2.6 µs, not 260 ns. Under a separate affected-fraction model, improving 40% of work by a factor two bounds total speedup to 1/(0.6+0.4/2)=1.25; untouched work remains. These are model calculations, not timings for either ISA.

Reuse the T36 callable kernel and T37 quantitative artifact in [PR-T43-03](#pr-t43-03). Count an executed path, compare with identified measurements, and explain a residual. Include code bytes, branches and connected-function cyclomatic e−n+2 as distinct measures. Equal static graph complexity says nothing automatic about repeated loop work or processor cycles.

<a id="t43-05"></a>

### T43.05 — Storage boundaries and lifetime peaks

Space is also a model with boundaries. Live payload, reserved capacity, retained inactive storage and scratch may overlap in time. A shared owned object is counted once, even if two views point into it. Peaks must be calculated on simultaneous states, not by adding independently occurring maxima. Static sections and measured resident/charged memory are other categories.

At time 3 the fixture has 64 live work bytes plus 80 scratch bytes: live peak 144. At time 7 work/result capacity is 128+96=224, while their payload is only 88. At time 10 work's 128 bytes remain retained although its live interval has ended. Summing 144+224+128 would count overlapping storage repeatedly and combine different times.

For stack, a .su record describes a function frame and qualifier. A feasible main/work/leaf chain is 32+48+16=96; main/other is 112. A stipulated 24-byte nonnested interrupt allowance makes 136 only for the declared known paths. Unknown callbacks, recursion or unbounded dynamic records remain unresolved. [PR-T43-04](#pr-t43-04) pairs the original ledger with actual compiler/section evidence; a sampled watermark or .bss total cannot certify a whole-program stack maximum.

<a id="t43-06"></a>

### T43.06 — Block transfers, locality and amplification

An external-memory model counts transfers of B fixed-size items between main memory M and a larger sequence N. The bounded activity fixes one disk/processor and a stated replacement/write policy. It is useful because locality can change transfer counts while comparison counts remain similar. It does not prescribe disk service latency or every bus transaction.

With four-byte items, B=2 and M=4, reading items 0..7 needs four eight-byte blocks: 32 bytes transferred for 32 useful bytes. A mixed read/write stream transfers 48 for 28 useful bytes, amplification 12/7. Dirty eviction and the final flush both matter. No-reference input has denominator zero and an undefined amplification ratio, including 0/0.

In [PR-T43-05](#pr-t43-05), add a bounded traffic adapter to existing T37 reference reasoning. Show residents, recency and dirty status at each reference. Contrast model transfers with file/syscall/device observations: warm pages, buffering, readahead and shared writeback can change the mapping. A cache miss, syscall and physical block I/O are not interchangeable events. Mastery retains item/byte units and a named layer for every ratio.

<a id="t43-07"></a>

### T43.07 — Component runtime, overlap and completion

Component runtime needs events rather than one undifferentiated duration. A blocking return can include completion. Asynchronous submission returns acceptance, while completion and safe buffer release have separate boundaries. A fast operation can complete before its submission function returns; event semantics, not a preferred diagram shape, decide validity. POSIX AIO is the bounded concrete comparison here, with one result collection after completion and valid borrowed request/buffer storage while pending.

Submission 0, return 2 and completion 12 yield call span 2 and latency 12. Overlapping phases [0,2],[1,11],[10,12] sum to 14 but cover a union of 12. Two threads can consume 15 CPU units in that 12-unit elapsed window. Wall-minus-process-CPU then becomes −3; it is not a universal waiting estimate. Serial nested attribution can calculate exclusive time under a complete call model, but that rule cannot blindly subtract concurrent phases.

[PR-T43-06](#pr-t43-06) adds an event adapter to accepted components. Define throughput's completed-item numerator and observation window. Submit separate serial/overlap and CPU/elapsed evidence, including completion-before-return, rather than inferring hidden work from one timestamp.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t43-08"></a>

### T43.08 — Read/write performance and persistence

A request count is not an accepted-byte count. Positive read/write results advance by exactly that many bytes; interruptions or nonblocking unavailability need explicit bounded policy. A zero read means EOF, while the chosen bounded write adapter stops on zero progress. Terminal errors preserve the already accepted prefix instead of replaying it or concealing it.

Writing eight bytes through returns 3,EINTR,2,EAGAIN,3 accepts eight in five attempts. Buffered write completion at 8 followed by successful requested fsync at 13 has a five-unit synchronization phase. A separate device-byte observation can exceed the logical file size; the synthetic 4096/8 ratio is 512. The file, buffered transfer and media/accounting layers answer different questions.

Extend T23 in [PR-T43-07](#pr-t43-07). Preserve native file-byte verification, requested synchronization results and warm-state/file lifetime. Successful write alone does not establish durable storage; a delayed fsync error remains significant. Directory-entry synchronization is separate where creation/rename matters. No timing sample demonstrates survival under all crashes or power failures. Mastery reconciles these boundaries without an unbounded retry loop or a global cache flush.

Choose a clock contract before collecting numbers. CLOCK_MONOTONIC can be frequency adjusted and excludes suspend; RAW avoids that adjustment and also excludes suspend; BOOTTIME includes suspend. Process CPU counts all threads, thread CPU one thread. Resolution is a stated granularity, not accuracy or bracket overhead, and consecutive valid timestamps can be equal. Integer conversion and return errors belong in the harness contract.

For paired A/B samples, analyze each pair before summarizing. The fixture medians 102 and 98 differ by 4, while the median paired improvement is 3. Nearest-rank p95 at N=5 selects the largest sample. An empty-bracket median 11 yields a 91-unit subtraction sensitivity; it does not prove a removable constant overhead. Small signals require a changed bracket or an inconclusive conclusion.

PMU counters observe selected events under hardware, kernel, privilege and scheduling constraints. Identify target, event meaning, binary and permitted user/kernel scope. ### T43.11 — cgroup CPU, memory and I/O accounting

cgroup v2 supplies resource policy and scoped accounting. cpu.max configures temporal fair-class bandwidth; cpu.stat observes usage/throttling. memory.current is a charged-memory gauge; high/max are different control boundaries. io.stat reports keyed major:minor counters, whereas io.max configures limits. Delegation and ancestor constraints decide who can change what. A useful read-only investigation needs no new privileges.

The original snapshot adds 800 µs CPU in a 2000-µs window, fraction 0.4; a configured 500/1000 quota ratio is 0.5. They need not coincide. memory.current can decrease while historical memory.peak is 12288. Reset semantics apply to subsequent reads on the same open descriptor; without that reset no fresh-window peak is established. Per-device byte deltas and PSI totals have their own units; pressure is not exclusive component waiting.

[PR-T43-10](#pr-t43-10) parses by key and distinguishes absent controllers from zero. Core route reads permitted files or records denial plus captured analysis. A prepared delegated experiment is optional and preserves/restores authorized state. Filesystem writeback support/shared-inode attribution, descendants and counter reset remain limits. Show policy versus observation and avoid a false isolated-memory claim.

### T43.12 — Compiler-based profiling and its perturbation

Compiler instrumentation observes a changed program. -pg needs matching compile/link boundaries and a supported runtime; --coverage counts selected execution arcs, not elapsed time. Entry/exit hooks can give a bounded serial call ledger, but must exclude themselves and avoid recursion/allocation/I/O hazards. Conceptual inline calls, code growth, dropped records and nonlocal exits limit completeness.

For complete work [0,9] containing child [1,4] and [5,7], inclusive work is 9 and exclusive work 4. A truncated buffer with open frames cannot supply exact durations. gprof samples self CPU time and propagates child time using an average-per-call assumption: two cheap/expensive caller populations can invalidate it. The original 20-ms child with two A/eight B calls predicts 4/16 ms, but declared actual 16/4 gives ±12-ms error. Off-CPU I/O delay is absent from that self-time estimate.

[PR-T43-11](#pr-t43-11) uses a reused single-threaded component, matched baseline, bounded hooks and a supported/unavailable gprof comparison. Record measured perturbation and code/.su changes. Mastery separates counts, samples, inferred children and elapsed waiting boundaries rather than calling instrumentation transparent.

### T43.13 — Bare-metal cycle and timer measurement

CYCCNT is an optional 32-bit processor-clock counter. Exact Armv7-M architecture addresses/fields are the start of an access contract, not proof that every board has an available counter. DEMCR.TRCENA must make trace reads meaningful; with it clear, DWT reads are UNKNOWN. Counter presence, access, enable, clock, device errata, interrupt/debug conditions and setup ownership must be checked before a claim.

Endpoints 4294967280→48 have a modulo delta 64. Only an independent interval bound below 2³² rules out additional wraps. At 16 MHz that is 4000 ns; removing an eight-cycle empty bracket yields a sensitivity 3500 ns. Debug state stops the counter, so halt-spanning active cycles cannot simply represent wall time. An unknown/absent counter is not a zero-cycle result.

[PR-T43-12](#pr-t43-12) requires the captured/static certificate. Optional silicon execution follows its firmware-specific gates and reuses existing setup/kernel/timer work. Preserve other debug bits and users; never reset a shared counter merely for a tidy sample. Timer/GPIO alternatives name their own clock/resolution observer. Emulators support correctness evidence, not measured silicon cycles, energy or sampled-tail WCET.

<a id="t43-14"></a>

### T43.14 — Choosing useful measures and making a performance decision

Choose measures from requirements. Useful work units, cycles/time, completed-item throughput, per-item latency, peak/retained space, code size, branches/traffic and deadline jitter form a vector. A single score can conceal an unacceptable resource. Energy needs a documented observable/instrument or declared physical model; elapsed time alone is insufficient. Cyclomatic complexity is a static design/test aid, not either Big-O or runtime cycles; feasible paths and fault freedom remain separate.

Variant B is faster in the fixture's model (240 versus 260 cycles) but exceeds both code and retained-storage limits. A is the accepted candidate. Equal cyclomatic v=3 graphs have sequential 2n versus nested n² body work; that shared static number cannot settle a speed decision. A different traffic/jitter constraint could change the accepted choice again.

Complete [PR-T43-03](#pr-t43-03)'s reserved decision dossier after the observation projects. It must cite the requirement, each accepted/rejected candidate, omitted measures and revision/build/workload. Label algebraic proof, finite fixture arithmetic, actual learner runtime and optional silicon/energy separately. A rigorous inconclusive or baseline-retention decision can pass; a fast number with missing boundaries cannot.


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

## Reading guidance

Use the front-card locators as bounded assignments. CLRS supplies formal quantifiers and deterministic prefix proofs; it does not predict allocator or target time. The architecture equation is a declared model; recompute its units and exclude the known inconsistent copied numerical examples. Vitter defines fixed-item block parameters; its historical device numbers are not today's measurements. NIST supplies the connected-function static CFG convention and its feasible-path limits.

Read Linux interfaces alongside the specific observation adapter: clocks/AIO/read/write/fsync before phase logs; PMU/security before permitted counts; cgroup/PSI before interpreting keyed snapshots. GCC/gprof scopes govern matching builds, stack qualifiers and perturbation. The exact Arm scopes govern only the optional counter certificate and ownership/presence/halt boundaries. Assigned reading cards total 15 hours; use the remaining 3 reading hours to recompute formulas, compare actual tool records and annotate the accepted source scopes. Wider chapters, additional PMU tables or board-specific setup recipes require fresh inspection before becoming an assigned authority.

| [PR-T43-11](#pr-t43-11) | Bounded compiler-hook/gprof perturbation comparison | A | 7 | 3 | 10 |

| **Total new project hours** | | | **66** | **36** | **102** |

Each detailed brief links a concrete original fixture, specifies edge/failure responses and distinct a/b/c evidence. The Profile C algorithm/model adapters are original work and cannot delegate their educational mechanism to libc. Hosted harness services remain identified as Profile A; genuine allocated or actual typed storage is required for typed access, and alignment of a declared byte array alone is insufficient.

## Mastery gate and feedback

Spend the 8 assessment hours on a cold explanation plus evidence audit. For every topic, point to three separate evidence items matching its objective claims. An assessor changes one input/case/clock/scope and asks for a prediction before execution. Require all twelve finite certificates, their rejection controls, actual demanded C/tool observations and honest unavailable/conditional routes; static fixture success cannot replace a required C count adapter or native clock trial.

Explain a formal bound with constants, a nonempty-state potential correction, unequal simultaneous space peaks, zero useful-byte amplification, completion-before-return, process CPU greater than wall, historical cgroup peak, zero-running PMU estimate and ambiguous wrap. Explain why equal cyclomatic v does not imply equal work. Repair a failed claim at its mechanism: missing prefix credit needs a corrected state proof, not more timing runs; missing observation needs a correctly scoped experiment, not a stronger asymptotic label. Reassess the exact leaf with a fresh input. The final decision dossier records justified acceptance, rejection or inconclusive evidence.

## Consolidation and transfer

Use 6 delayed hours for two transfer reviews. After a week, choose an already accepted different kernel/component and rebuild its cost/event contract on paper before instrumenting; after a second interval, examine one deliberately misleading performance claim and identify missing size, clock, layer, attribution or evidence. Credit prior owner-domain work once. Keep one frozen dossier with source locator/build/raw samples and limitations so a second reader can reproduce the bounded result.

Connect the work to [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-reading](#guide-reading), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles), [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment), [guide-workload](#guide-workload) and [guide-performance-debugging](#guide-performance-debugging). Integration reuse organizes these completed artifacts; it adds no duplicated implementation hours.

## Environment and limits

Core hosted observations use permitted interfaces and disposable files. Controller/PMU/gprof access can be absent; record an actual attempt and explicit unavailable result rather than changing global policy or claiming zero work. A prepared delegated cgroup or exclusive board trace session is optional. CPU clock/event meaning, compiler/runtime, filesystem writeback, shared descendants/inodes, asynchronous phases and device/debug/interrupt state remain named limitations.

The Arm route's static/captured evidence is mandatory and its actual silicon implementation is optional, with additional firmware gates in PR-T43-12. Emulation demonstrates functional execution, not silicon timing. No project claims energy without an instrument/source, experimental crash durability, whole-program stack proof from .su alone, or WCET from sampled maxima. tools/verify_performance_fixtures.py independently verifies finite arithmetic/semantic certificates and strict owned file correspondence; it does not compile or solve the learner's C, mutate host controls or certify hardware.

<a id="t44"></a>

# T44 — Debugging from symptoms to causal evidence

| Track | Status | Hours | Dependency profiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cross-track | core | 114 | A, B |

**Prerequisites:** [T03](#t03), [T07](#t07).

**Required selected foundations:** [T21.07.a](#t21-07-a), [T21.08.a](#t21-08-a), [T32.01.b](#t32-01-b), [T32.14.a](#t32-14-a). Complete those leaves before the dependent project; the rest of the referenced domain need not be finished.

| Reading | Implementation | Verification | Assessment | Consolidation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18 | 56 | 26 | 8 | 6 |

## Purpose and outcomes

Develop a diagnosis that survives a changed input, build or environment. T44 turns symptoms into replayable evidence, locates the first violated contract, tests competing causes and verifies a causal repair. It reuses existing components and tool practices; new hours cover the intentional defect, dossier and transfer. Ten projects of 4–12 hours total 82 hours; with reading 18 hours, assessment 8 hours and consolidation 6 hours, the module totals 114 hours. The 82 hours are implementation 56+verification 26, not an additional allocation.

## Entry check and remediation

After T03/T07, explain a valid object/lifetime, compile a two-function C program and test a boundary without executing UB. Complete only the named T21 assertion/logging and T32 fixture/replay leaves for the first milestone. If a learner cannot distinguish observed output from a hypothesis, use the defined assignment/counter faults in PR-T44-01/03 and repeat one discriminating test. The first three milestones need no completed T24/T25/T27/T31/T33 or T45 module. Later briefs list their exact selected preludes and reused artifacts; prerequisite time belongs to those existing exercises. A full-program order may place T44 later, while this novice diagnostic route selects only its entry leaves.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles) and [guide-roadmap](#guide-roadmap) for entry/dependency policy. Every project keeps predicted, observed, inferred and open claims distinct. A tool absence has a supported alternate environment or a narrower model task, with the dependent runtime claim left open.

## Study sequence and teaching


<a id="t44-01"></a>

### T44.01 — Observation, contracts and replay identity

A symptom is an observation; a cause is an explanation that survives discriminating tests. Record the expected contract before the first run: input range, state/effect limits, output on failure and finite completion policy. Preserve source revision, compiler/flags, image hash, input hash, configuration, platform and timeout. A log paired with the wrong image is not the same experiment. PR-T44-01's image A / input abc record matches, whereas image B with image A symbols does not. Its digest identifies bytes, not their authenticity.

Predict two causes before editing: for an accepted out-of-range request, either validation was removed or validation changed the input. Observe the parameter immediately before/after validation to separate them. Keep expected, observed, inferred and open claims in separate fields. An isolated deterministic harness makes hypotheses cheap to test; a synthetic expected history remains a model. A build that happened to print the expected value says little about an untested boundary. Retain the first useful cause separately from secondary cleanup/logging failures and reduce one diagnostic variable at a time.

Apply in [PR-T44-01](#pr-t44-01). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.01.a`: Write an observation record that separates actual output, expected contract, inference and an untested hypothesis.
- `T44.01.b`: Reproduce a bounded failure with input, source/image/configuration/environment identities and a finite timeout.
- `T44.01.c`: Predict two competing causes and select a discriminating observation before changing the program.

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.
