<a id="t44-02"></a>

### T44.02 — Build diagnostics, assertions and bounded logs

Use an explicit dialect and a warning build such as cc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wformat=2 -g -Og on a supported GCC environment. Record the actual version and accepted options; GCC 15.2 is the inspected contract, not an installed-tool claim. -Wall enables a selected set, not every warning. The faulty admissible function in PR-T44-01 assigns n=0 in its condition, then accepts every supplied value. This is a defined logic error, so its source transition is suitable for a first novice investigation. A warning is a lead: parenthesizing the assignment may silence it while preserving the defect. Repair the intended 1..4 relation and test 0, 1, 4, 5.

External validation must survive NDEBUG. Assertions express internal promises, and their expressions must not perform a required operation. Reuse T21's three-record ring with overflow policy and an independent first-cause field: four events retain the last three while the first cause stays E_INPUT. Disable each diagnostic channel independently, then verify no diagnostic-only side effect is evaluated and required validation still runs. Bounded logs can drop events and change timing; retain those limits and compare a release build. A clean warning build or debug-only repair is not a correctness certificate.

Apply in [PR-T44-01](#pr-t44-01). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.02.a`: Interpret warnings and generate a matching debug-information build while retaining the production optimization comparison.
- `T44.02.b`: Separate internal assertions from durable external validation and make a bounded diagnostic log preserve the first useful cause.
- `T44.02.c`: Demonstrate that disabled assertions or logs do not erase required validation or evaluate diagnostic-only side effects.

<a id="t44-03"></a>

### T44.03 — Minimal reproducers and input reduction

Specify one same-failure predicate before reducing input. PASS means the selected contract holds; FAIL means the selected failure persists; UNRESOLVED means a malformed candidate, another symptom, or an unclassified replay. Treating UNRESOLVED as PASS can produce an invalid alleged minimality result. The inspected ddmin algorithm tries subsets and complements, keeps a failing smaller configuration and increases partition granularity when no reduction works. Use at most 16 chunks, bounded work/time, a stable configuration identity and cached test outcomes. Reuse the T32 replay harness; write only the new reducer and small original input grammar.

The eight-chunk fixture fails when it contains 1, 7, 8 together or 2, 3 together; a partial 1/7/8 group without either complete trigger is unresolved. The candidate 1, 7, 8 fails and all three single deletions are unresolved, so it is 1-minimal. Yet 2, 3 is a smaller failing input. Exhaustive finite enumeration is the independent fixture oracle, distinct from the learner reducer. Check every remaining single deletion and retain the actual replay classification. The reduced input localizes a trigger; inspect the first invalid code transition separately to explain the repair.

Apply in [PR-T44-02](#pr-t44-02). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.03.a`: Define PASS, same-failure FAIL and UNRESOLVED outcomes with a stable finite replay contract.
- `T44.03.b`: Implement a bounded original token reducer using subset/complement trials and preserve the failing input grammar.
- `T44.03.c`: Check every single remaining deletion to certify 1-minimality and explain why it does not prove global minimality or causal code repair.

<a id="t44-04"></a>

### T44.04 — Stepping, scopes and call stacks

Begin with initialized valid storage and a defined logic defect. A counter used represents admitted records with invariant 0<=used<=capacity. The faulty condition used>capacity admits a fifth record at capacity 4; the counter reaches 5 without requiring an invalid memory access. `break try_acquire if *used == cap` can stop before this transition when symbols permit it. Use step to enter, next to stay at the current source level, finish to return and stepi/nexti for machine instructions. State which transition each command observes; source stepping is not an instruction-by-instruction history.

Frames and scopes select different objects. In the supplied synthetic two-frame example, probe's status 7 differs from caller's status 2. Use bt full, frame 0 and frame 1, then inspect the appropriate name/argument. A selected frame's locals may be incomplete in a machine prologue or absent after optimization. Save the command transcript and exact image/symbol identities; an unavailable value is not evidence that its source variable was zero. Reuse the prior minimization/backtrace practice, add this new counter defect and explain why the final count 4 after a release hides the earlier violation 5.

Apply in [PR-T44-03](#pr-t44-03). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.04.a`: Use source and instruction stepping to stop before the first contract-violating transition in a learner-owned C program.
- `T44.04.b`: Select frames and scopes to distinguish the current local, a shadowed name and the caller’s arguments.
- `T44.04.c`: Record a backtrace with matching symbols and state what optimized-out or unavailable values prevent it from proving.

<a id="t44-05"></a>

### T44.05 — Conditional breakpoints and watchpoints

Choose a stopping mechanism from a hypothesis. A pure breakpoint condition used==capacity tests the admission boundary without calling code that changes inferior state. A watch on a live, initialized object tests a particular value change. Avoid dereferencing a guessed address or an expired local. Hardware watches typically stop at the responsible instruction, while software watches can stop at the next statement and are much slower. GDB's current manual states that software watches observe only the current thread; they do not establish another thread's writes.

The fixture requests an eight-byte watch on a four-byte-width target and three watches with only two slots. Both exceed its declared geometry; those numbers are a model, not F439 capabilities. Actual hardware availability and insertion/resume errors must be collected. Narrow the watched valid object, use a pure breakpoint, or add a bounded replay log when unsupported. This changes the claim's granularity and perturbation. A watchpoint shows a change, which may occur after the first invalid state; compare it with the contract transition and retain the earliest corroborated violation. Document object lifetime, scope expiry, thread focus, width and slot limits.

Reuse a selected ABI probe. Under the inspected historical SysV AMD64 scope, the example entry stack 4104 has the expected 16-byte relation; a changed preserved register 11 → 12 violates the chosen boundary even though the stack returns unchanged. Confirm the actual ABI/build variant before generalizing. A core or saved state needs the matching executable and symbols and can omit memory. The fixture contains registers/text but no heap; unavailable heap state stays open. A core is a stopped snapshot, not the preceding history. ### T44.07 — Memory fault diagnosis through reused invariants

Reuse object extents, allocator ownership and T32's isolated faulty/repaired memory variants. The finite model marks an offset 4 write into extent 4 invalid, a read after free invalid, an uninitialized value use invalid and an old alias after successful nonzero resize invalid. Failed resize preserves the old allocation and valid aliases under the declared contract. Even a successful in-place realloc ends the old allocation lifetime; old aliases must be re-derived from the returned pointer. Deep stack, fixed-region and asynchronous memory practice belongs in T45 rather than a duplicate allocator implementation here.

Keep the language violation distinct from its observed symptom. A tool might report a later visible use, the process might continue, and a clean run may miss the path. Run separate supported ASan/UBSan and unsanitized Memcheck tracks; use origins where available. ASan alone is not an initialization detector. Record the first invalid source/lifetime transition, each actual tool report or silence, flags and environment. Repair before the invalid transition, verify ownership/failure state, then transfer to a different extent or failure point. An oracle's invalid-event index cannot certify an actual diagnostic or prescribed UB output.

<a id="t44-08"></a>

### T44.08 — I/O, errno and descriptor failure histories

A stream cursor advances by each positive byte count, not by the requested count or the last count alone. For seven bytes and results 2, EINTR, 2, EAGAIN, 3 the retained offsets are 2, 2, 4, 4, 7. EINTR before progress and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK leave the cursor unchanged; a successful short result already accounts for progress. A positive-count stream read 0 means EOF, while a zero write requires the declared zero-progress policy and a finite bound. Reuse T24's cursors and event state rather than write another event loop. Reject impossible adapter counts before arithmetic.

Capture errno immediately after the operation indicates failure, before logging can overwrite it. ENOSPC followed by logging EIO still has original cause ENOSPC. Pthread functions return direct statuses, so that layer does not use this errno rule. EPIPE with default SIGPIPE may terminate before the return is observed; an explicitly handled/ignored signal disposition makes a different experiment. Positive write means local acceptance, not durable storage or peer consumption. On Linux, close releases the descriptor early, so retry after an error can close a reused number/generation. The inspected POSIX.1-2024 EINTR rule differs; label this exercise Linux. Use an injected/capped EMFILE ledger first; any actual exhaustion test is limited to the isolated learner process, at most eight owned records, with cleanup and no system-wide ENFILE campaign.

Apply in [PR-T44-06](#pr-t44-06). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.08.a`: Trace positive partial progress, zero/EOF, EINTR and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK without discarding or duplicating bytes.
- `T44.08.b`: Capture errno only after the relevant failure and diagnose EPIPE/SIGPIPE and bounded per-process descriptor exhaustion.
- `T44.08.c`: Repair cursor/ownership cleanup under the declared Linux close contract and explain its POSIX.1-2024 portability limit.

<a id="t44-09"></a>

### T44.09 — Concurrency, deadlock and lost events

Reproduce a schedule before drawing a timing conclusion. If A holds lock L and waits for B's lock R while B holds lock R and waits for A's lock L, the finite wait-for graph has a cycle. Whole-thread backtraces can corroborate a stopped instance; the graph and one run are not every future schedule. A non-atomic write and read to the same object on different threads, without a happens-before edge, are an unordered conflict in the fixture. Its repaired ownership/mutex argument must supply the edge; volatile and longer sleeps do not supply it. A data race has no promised final value.

The lost-wakeup fixture has consumer check false, producer set true/signal, consumer waits. Fixing only the sleep length leaves that window. Reuse T25's predicate-under-the-same-mutex protocol: the wait releases atomically, the producer changes state while holding the mutex, and the consumer rechecks after reacquisition and every wakeup. Save forced schedules, thread identities, direct API statuses and a written ordering/lifetime argument. Supported detector runs and stress add exercised evidence. Halting or logging can hide a race; a detector's silence and one deterministic history do not close all schedules or establish fairness.

Apply in [PR-T44-07](#pr-t44-07). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.09.a`: Reconstruct a forced event schedule, happens-before obligations and a wait-for graph while separating mutex correctness from timing observations.
- `T44.09.b`: Diagnose a race, deadlock or predicate/wakeup defect using reused T24/T25 programs and whole-thread observations.
- `T44.09.c`: Test a causal synchronization repair with controlled schedules and detector runs while leaving unobserved schedules open.

<a id="t44-10"></a>

### T44.10 — Bare-metal startup, faults and asynchronous state

Reuse the selected F439 startup/image and basic exception decoder. The fixture reset word 0x08000101 denotes Thumb entry 0x08000100. IRQ 3 corresponds to exception 19 and vector 0x0800004C. EXC_RETURN 0xFFFFFFFD selects the scoped basic PSP/Thread return; with aligned pre-PSP 0x20001000 and no padding, eight words start 0x20000FE0. Optional extended FP frames, padding and nested-handler details need their own supported interpretation rather than this simplified model.

CFSR 0x8200 indicates precise BusFault plus BFAR valid; HFSR 0x40000000 records forced escalation. The imprecise 0x400 case has no valid BFAR, so the stale address is not usable evidence and stacked PC is not promised to identify the responsible access. Compare bad startup, peripheral clock/pin sequencing and invalid ownership as competing hypotheses. Do not inspect arbitrary side-effecting MMIO in the debugger. The policy model's configure-before-enable violates its stage invariant; actual peripheral effects require device evidence/measurement. DMA cancellation request leaves ownership with DMA until stop acknowledgment; the third CPU write is invalid even if the core is halted. The selected F439 SRAM/DMA path has no core data-cache maintenance requirement. Static arithmetic, emulator observations and physical fault/electrical observations remain separately labelled.

### T44.11 — Sanitizer, static, fuzz and differential evidence

Choose a tool by the defect class and supported environment. Reuse T32's separate dynamic tracks, bounded fuzz seeds, independent differential reference and static review; do not build another fuzz framework. Static over-approximation can produce alarms that are not demonstrated executions. Eva's inspected scope does not directly model asynchronous interrupts. ASan, UBSan, thread instrumentation and Memcheck have distinct contracts and incompatible/unsupported combinations; record actual versions/options and instrumented versus release behavior. Unsupported capability is an open tool claim, not a clean run.

The original u8 contract is saturating addition. For 100+50, 250+10, 255+1 the mathematical reference returns 150, 255, 255 while a defined uint8_t narrowing defect returns 150, 4, 0. A differentially failing sum begins at 256; the candidate 255, 1 is one boundary example, not the unique smallest operand pair. Build a bounded original C implementation and test harness, then preserve a minimized failing pair and an independent arithmetic oracle. Each clean run covers only its executed scope; a static model/fixture does not establish a sanitizer message. Triangulate the source transition with actual supported evidence, explain disagreement and retain unsupported observations honestly.

### T44.12 — Causal repair, regression and delayed blind transfer

A causal repair prevents the first invalid transition. A symptom patch may only hide its final effect. At used 4/capacity 4, reject-before-commit keeps state valid and reports full; clamp-after-commit temporarily reaches 5 before restoring 4. The identical final count does not make the histories equivalent. Test the minimized trigger, normal/boundary/invalid neighbors, failure cleanup and matched debug/release/instrumented images. A fix whose check only exists in an assertion fails the release contract. Save raw observations and remaining scope limits instead of matching diagnostic wording.

Progress through guided investigation, symptom-only investigation, then delayed transfer. The supplied public fixture/oracle is visible, so it is guided practice, not a blind assessment. A peer/reviewer supplies a genuinely withheld new variant, or a solo learner commits to an unopened seeded variant and reveals its oracle only after submitting the predictions, first-invalid-state evidence and repair. Revisit after at least seven days. Self-authored faults retain limited independence even when delayed; state this and use an independent reviewer when possible. Remediate the mistaken inference or invariant, then retry a different withheld variant rather than rereading every module.

Apply in [PR-T44-10](#pr-t44-10). Evidence must separately address these objective checks:

- `T44.12.a`: Explain a repair in terms of the violated invariant and reject a symptom-only patch with a competing counterexample.
- `T44.12.b`: Replay the minimized trigger, adjacent boundary cases and matched debug/release/instrumented builds with explicit observation categories.
- `T44.12.c`: Diagnose a delayed unseen variant from an evidence dossier and record remaining claims instead of reusing memorized diagnostic strings.

## Reading guidance

The metadata assigns 18 bounded one-hour passages, including the original ISSTA 2000 reduction argument, GDB's captured development snapshot, GCC 15.2 and exact Linux/POSIX/Arm contracts. Read the named locator and limits rather than an entire manual. Further accepted ABI, POSIX memory, ST DMA/boot and Eva passages remain available through the reused T08/T25/T27/T29/T31/T33 lessons. A prior source acceptance supports only its inspected scope. The held Vidović book supplies a layered crash example on its own SEGGER platform; compare it with the official contract rather than importing a proprietary setup or promised C-UB trap. Grenning's host-to-target cycle explains which evidence must be recollected for each boundary.

## Implementation projects

Complete PR-T44-01..03 as the novice diagnosis spine, then PR-T44-04/05 for image/memory evidence. Enter PR-T44-06/07 only with the stated hosted I/O/concurrency leaves, and PR-T44-08 with the selected firmware artifacts. PR-T44-09 compares tool/reference evidence; PR-T44-10 assesses delayed transfer. Adapt PR-T21-03, PR-T24-04, PR-T25-05, PR-T31-01/02 and PR-T32-05/07 instead of rebuilding logs, event loops, queues, allocators or fuzzers. T45 is optional deep memory practice with no mandatory dependency in this module.

The supplied fixtures are finite model histories with independent static certificates. The learner owns original C and its fault/repaired variants. Run the static oracle separately from actual C/debugger/tool/hardware collection. Strict fixture/catalog checks reject missing, unexpected nested, duplicate, mistyped or wrongly bound artifacts. Model outcomes are not runtime observations.

## Mastery gate and feedback

For every a/b/c objective, supply its explanation, evidence and scope. A complete dossier includes expected contract; pre-run competing predictions; source/image/configuration/environment identities; finite replay/actual observation; earliest invalid transition; discriminating hypothesis test; minimized tri-state trigger; invariant repair/limits; regression matrix and changed variant. The novice gate requires one warning/validation investigation and one counter / watch investigation. The later gate requires a systems/firmware dossier with its selected preludes, a tool-disagreement explanation and a causal-repair counterexample. Missing runtime capability leaves that claim open instead of passing a different property silently.

Use guided→symptom-only→delayed assessment. Visible public fixtures/oracles are guided, not blind. A reviewer/peer withholds a new variant, or a solo learner commits to an unopened seeded variant and reveals its oracle only after the submitted dossier. Separate this from self-authored fault practice, whose independence is limited. Feedback names the faulty inference, state transition or contract; the retry uses another variant.

## Consolidation and transfer

After at least seven days, diagnose a withheld new boundary, cleanup, schedule or stale-generation variant without reopening the old answer. Predict which image/input/tool/target evidence must be recollected. Retain rejected hypotheses and an example symptom patch that final-state checks would miss. Summarize the actual remaining claims rather than treating one successful transfer as every-case correctness.

## Environment and limits

GDB's inspected 19.0.50.20261009-git manual is a current development snapshot. Installed compiler/debugger, target watch resources, permissions, core generation and tool platforms must be recorded. Watchpoints can expire or miss other threads; optimization can erase variables; logs/stops/instrumentation perturb timing. Dynamic tools observe supported executed paths, static tools require context and may alarm conservatively, and cores omit history/memory. Undefined behavior and data races have no prescribed symptom. Linux close/EINTR policy is not a portable generic POSIX rule. The F439/basic-frame/static model excludes unsupported FP/padding/board effects; the selected F439 SRAM/DMA path has no core data-cache maintenance requirement. No fixture or emulator certifies physical timing, peripheral effects or electrical behavior.

## Purpose and outcomes

Learn to diagnose and repair memory and resource failures with evidence that distinguishes object bounds, initialization, lifetime and capacity. The result is ten small original experiments and repair dossiers, built on earlier APIs and harnesses. Each gives a prediction, controlled negative observation, first-invalid-state argument, repair and new regression/transfer cases.

## Entry check and remediation

Before PR-T45-01 explain ownership after failed nonzero resize, a bounded NUL scan, a three-stage cleanup prefix and the difference between a model and actual tool evidence. Revisit selected T03/T21/T32 leaves when needed. PR-T45-04 adds T13 stack analysis and T23 checked process/limit setup; PR-T45-05 adds T27 layout/startup. PR-T45-09 adds the T29 DMA/ordering leaves. The front card records these selected imports; early hosted milestones do not require completing every firmware laboratory first.

Use [guide-entry](#guide-entry) and [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted feedback. Repair integer interval/multiplication reasoning in PR-T45-02/03, maximum path sums in 04, aligned interval placement in 05 and root reachability in 06. State the equation and one counterexample before returning to C; no unrelated mathematics restart is required.

## Study sequence and teaching

Reuse a prior implementation or write a small owned example; do not consume a supplied solved C program. Run one deliberately faulty mechanism per supervised hosted process. Preserve input, build identity and observation before repair, then repeat with identical controls. Native undefined behavior does not have a prescribed output, crash signal or address.


<a id="t45-01"></a>

### T45.01 — Controlled observation and detection contracts

An experiment starts with a claim and its detection contract. An extent monitor checks permitted addresses; an initialization monitor follows valid values; a resource ledger checks acquired and retained objects. Each can miss a different kind of defect. Name the exercised path, monitored boundary, runtime dependencies and observations before running the faulty version. An unavailable tool is an unresolved observation; a setup failure is not evidence about the target.

Worked trace: a negative control produces a report, a repaired trial produces no report, and another negative trial is silent. These results establish detection for the first exercised trial and support the repaired trial's selected checks. The silent faulty trial remains inconclusive. They do not establish a universal memory-safety property. A report also needs a matching binary and an explanation of the first invalid state; later runs after corruption can obscure that state.

Reuse the T32 harness in PR-T45-01. Record exact compile/link commands, sanitizer options, symbols, supervisor limits and tool versions for native, ASan/UBSan and separate unsanitized Memcheck builds. Predict which checked invariant should fail, then record actual output and termination without imposing a portable crash value or diagnostic string. The misconception is that a clean dynamic report proves all paths or that an unsupported invocation counts as a pass. Evidence is a coverage matrix plus a negative/repaired pair and an explicit open-claim list.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-01](#pr-t45-01).

<a id="t45-02"></a>

### T45.02 — Object extents, underflow, off-by-one and NUL boundaries

Capacity describes storage; initialized length describes valid payload; a string adds a terminating NUL within the object's extent. A signed external index must be checked before conversion or pointer formation. One-past permits a position used for a zero-length operation under this API's explicit contract, never a dereference. Check lower bounds, remaining extent and NUL space before touching the destination, so rejected input preserves sentinels and observable length.

For capacity 8, indices 0 through 7 name bytes. Index −1 is below the lower bound and index 8 with count 1 is beyond it. Index 8 with count 0 is accepted without access. Seven data octets plus one NUL fit; eight data octets plus NUL require nine bytes. A scan bounded to eight bytes can return missing-terminator without reading byte 8. Do not use strlen to discover the length of an untrusted unterminated array.

In PR-T45-02 build these checked operations and contrast them with separate faulty learner-owned copies in the hosted process. Add a legal C array access that writes the wrong logical field: it can violate an application invariant while staying inside addressable storage. The misconception is that any array-shaped or zero-filled data is a valid string, or that an addressability tool checks the application meaning of every write. Evidence includes preserved failure snapshots, explicit terminator bytes, exact-capacity success, lower/upper cases and an independent logical-field assertion.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-02](#pr-t45-02).

<a id="t45-03"></a>

### T45.03 — Checked allocation sizes and integer conversions

A correct allocation extent comes from a checked expression, not the wrapped result. Validate nonnegative external counts before converting them, constrain representable inputs, check multiplication, then check the header or terminator addition. Do not compute an overflowing intermediate and attempt to validate it afterwards. Conversion to a narrower size can lose information before the allocator is called.

The supplied model uses a maximum of 65535, header 12 and stride 7. Count 9360 gives 65520 payload bytes and 65532 total. Count 9361 has a representable product, 65527, but its total 65539 fails addition. Count 9363 has product 65541, so multiplication fails first. Count zero with header 12 still requests twelve bytes; total zero is rejected by this lab contract. These numbers model a declared width; the learner's C uses its actual SIZE_MAX and selected interface limits.

PR-T45-03 repairs a count-to-storage helper and a caller that narrows a length too early. The API returns a status and publishes the size only on success; no allocation occurs on rejection. The misconception is that defined unsigned wrapping makes the requested storage sufficient, or that UBSan's default group detects every unsigned size wrap. Evidence is the first rejected arithmetic stage, unchanged output/owner, independent wide arithmetic and native boundary tests. Remediate division inequalities and representability before adding complexity.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-03](#pr-t45-03).

<a id="t45-04"></a>

### T45.04 — Stack exhaustion, frames and nested execution

Stack-capacity exhaustion consumes the reserved stack through calls, recursion, dynamic storage and nested contexts. A buffer write outside a local object's bounds is a different failure, even if it corrupts the stack. Frames depend on actual compilation, alignment, spills and callees. A GCC dynamic entry without bounded cannot close the whole-path bound. Unknown recursive depth or indirect callees keep that claim open.

The synthetic single descending stack has frames 32 + 48 + 64 = 144 bytes. Its two permitted nested contexts contribute (32 + 48) + (32 + 40) = 152, for 296 total. A 320-byte reservation leaves 24. Replacing one 32-byte saved frame with a declared 104-byte extended frame makes 368, exceeding the reservation. Real MSP/PSP selection and floating-point/lazy-frame configuration must be recorded separately; this is not a universal frame formula.

Changed-pattern scanning measures bytes that no longer match the fill. In the fixture, 32 unchanged bytes become eight four-byte words; the recorded minimum SP reserves 48 bytes even though only 32 changed. Unwritten local space or a restored pattern can hide reservation. Reentrant logging and interrupt nesting can add paths absent from the trial. PR-T45-04 combines closed-path calculations, actual .su/object inspection, a bounded high-water experiment and child-only native exhaustion. The misconception is that the largest single frame, watermark or canary proves a maximum. Evidence separates conditional bound, tested observation, guard behavior and unresolved paths.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-04](#pr-t45-04).

<a id="t45-05"></a>

### T45.05 — Fixed RAM sections, startup and collision failures

A .bss output section occupies a fixed linked interval. Startup initializes selected zeroed storage; it does not grow .bss as the program allocates. Four failures need different evidence: fixed sections exceeding a linker region; an incorrect copy/zero range; a custom heap violating its reserved interval; and a stray runtime write into another object. Link success cannot rule out the latter three.

In the synthetic 1024-byte region, aligned data 96, bss 400 and retained storage 64 end at offset 560. The declared descending 256-byte stack begins at 768. A 160-byte heap ends at 720, leaving 48; a 32-byte guard fits. A 192-byte heap ends at 752, leaving 16, so the reservation contract fails despite all fixed sections fitting. Changing bss to 900 also aligns the retained start to 1000 and ends fixed placement at 1064, a 40-byte region overflow. Those are distinct verdicts.

PR-T45-05 reuses startup and map work from T27 and checks boundaries before initialization. A wrong zero range ending at byte 13 would touch retained byte 12; the checked adapter rejects it before mutation. In a separate defined reserved-cell experiment, change a logical value with an incorrect legal-address write and show that section size remains unchanged. The misconception is that corruption means .bss grew, or that hosted heaps necessarily collide with a descending contiguous stack. Evidence includes the exact map/allocator policy, nonoverlap, retained sentinels and separate link versus runtime observations.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-05](#pr-t45-05).

<a id="t45-06"></a>

### T45.06 — Leaks, retained storage and failure cleanup

A resource leak can come from a missing release, a lost owning handle, a failed acquisition prefix or a retained object whose lifetime is too broad. Build an ownership ledger with acquisition, transfer, borrow and exactly-once release. Report live payload, retained bytes and peak bytes separately. RSS includes effects beyond the application's live allocation count.

Three resources of 32, 48 and 16 bytes produce peak prefixes 0, 32, 80 and 96. Failure before resource 2 acquires resources 0 and 1 and releases 1 then 0. Publication occurs only after all acquisitions; cleanup errors preserve the first cause. In the finite graph, lost A retains child B, rooted C remains reachable and D has only an interior root. These are declared graph categories, not promised native Memcheck output. C's 24 reachable bytes exceed a retention budget of 16 even though reachability prevents a lost-root classification.

In PR-T45-06 reproduce forgotten free, direct owner overwrite on failed resize and cleanup failure in separate owned processes. The repair stages publication, retains owners until release, and exercises every failure prefix. Native leak tools use conservative roots and selected error policies; state those settings. The misconception is that reachable means acceptable retention, that every RSS increase is a leak or that process exit substitutes for bounded repeated-use cleanup. Evidence includes the ledger before and after every acquisition/failure, repeated cycles, separate leak observations and a resource budget.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-06](#pr-t45-06).


#### Evidence checklist

Retain a separate evidence item for each objective below. Meeting one objective does not establish the others.

<a id="t45-07"></a>

### T45.07 — Resize, invalid release and stale aliases

The resize protocol has two branches. Failed nonzero resize retains the original allocation and its owner. Successful resize ends the old allocation's lifetime and supplies a new owner; every old derived alias is invalid even if the allocator reuses the numeric address. Compute and save required lengths/contents before the call, retain the result temporarily, and publish it only under the chosen failure contract. Do not compare, dereference or release the old C pointer after success.

The finite history gives generation 1 eight initialized bytes. Refusal preserves generation 1 and size 8. Success supplies generation 2 and size 12, retains the first eight bytes and leaves four additional bytes uninitialized. Its address token can be 1000 again, yet the generation-1 alias is stale. Integer tokens are safe model data; they are not permission to examine an invalid C pointer.

PR-T45-07 repairs a resize wrapper and alias publication. It separately studies double release, interior/foreign release and use-after-free with own-program negative controls, never as expected production behavior. free(NULL) is valid and has no effect; clearing one owner does not clear another alias. Zero-size resize is excluded. The misconception is that a same-address return preserves old aliases, or that a null assignment repairs ownership everywhere. Evidence is failure preservation, success invalidation, initialized-tail handling and exactly-once release, followed by new relocation and alias tests.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-07](#pr-t45-07).

<a id="t45-08"></a>

### T45.08 — Initialization state and delayed invalid use

Addressability and initialization are independent. Storage can be accessible while a field lacks an initialized value. A field or byte-state model tracks intended writes; a publication contract requires every semantically required field. A zero-byte fill is not a universal typed-object initializer for every pointer or floating representation. Use typed initialization and explicit field assignments where the object contract requires them.

The supplied record has length and mode. Writing only length leaves mode uninitialized, so consuming mode fails and publication is denied even though the address is accessible. Writing both permits publication; making their storage inaccessible still fails. The two supplied synthetic representations differ in nonsemantic bytes while length 7 and mode 1 compare equal. They model a reason to compare fields, without defining a real C struct layout or promising initialized padding.

PR-T45-08 repairs partial initialization and adds branch/output consumption controls. Memcheck can propagate invalid-value metadata before reporting an externally significant use; that reporting policy is not permission to evaluate an indeterminate C value. ASan alone is not a general initialization-use detector. Optional MSan needs a supported OS and correctly instrumented dependencies. The misconception is that malloc supplies valid values, a silent copy is legal C, or whole-struct memcmp expresses semantic equality. Evidence is the write/consume history, field-wise regression, fill-pattern variation and a declared coverage limit.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-08](#pr-t45-08).

<a id="t45-09"></a>

### T45.09 — Asynchronous borrowing, DMA and reentrancy

An asynchronous borrower can retain a buffer or callback context after the caller stops waiting. A timeout changes waiting policy; a cancellation request changes intent. Reclamation requires confirmed quiescence under the adapter's contract. A request identity and generation prevent a late callback from accessing a new object at a reused address. Protecting allocation metadata does not establish this application lifetime.

In the fixture, request 7 times out and requests cancellation. Reclaim is busy until its completion confirms no further access. Reclaim advances generation 1 to 2; a later generation-1 completion is stale. Request 8 instead confirms cancellation, yielding exactly one cancellation completion before generation 3 reuse. Two simultaneous users of scratch buffer 1 conflict; buffers 1 and 2 do not under the declared nonoverlap contract.

PR-T45-09 reuses the T21 operation model and T29 adapter. Add reentrant callbacks, duplicate completion and expired callback borrows. Hosted atomics or TSan observations do not model independent DMA. F439 SRAM/CCM reachability, ordering, interrupts and actual device quiescence require qualified target evidence. Halting the core may leave a peripheral active. The misconception is that disabling interrupts, a mutex, timeout or debugger stop authorizes reuse. Evidence is the ownership interval, exactly-once completion, denied early reclaim and explicit physical claims left open until measured.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-09](#pr-t45-09).

<a id="t45-10"></a>

### T45.10 — Causal repair, prevention and transfer

A crash site is where a symptom becomes visible, not necessarily where the contract first failed. Work backwards using a competing-hypothesis table: extent, initialization, lifetime, resource boundary and observation setup. Use the smallest reproducing prefix to find the first invalid state, then design a distinguishing experiment rather than changing several conditions at once.

The extent history fails at event 2 but exhibits its symptom at event 5; the lifetime history fails at 1 and exhibits a symptom at 4. Reporting event 5 or 4 as the cause loses the repair boundary. A watchpoint should target a live, bounded object and be re-established when its scope or allocation changes. Hardware slot/width limits and software stepping affect observation. Arm watchpoint events are asynchronous; a recorded PC alone is not a universal offending-store proof. Fault frames and addresses must be validated before interpreting them.

PR-T45-10 requires an unseen repair dossier, semantic regression and delayed transfer. Separate prevention by a checked extent/owner protocol from mitigation by canaries, guard regions or hardening. A mitigation may reduce damage without restoring the invariant. The misconception is that the first reported symptom, a new allocation layout or disappearance under debug proves the repair. Evidence connects prediction, minimum trigger, first invalid state, mechanism, repair and remaining limits. Transfer changes capacity, failure position, nesting or completion order after a delay.

Develop and assess the evidence in [PR-T45-10](#pr-t45-10).

## Reading guidance

Use only the exact front-card locator scopes and their registry limits. The book's inspected second edition uses some C23 examples; this laboratory's portable drills retain the selected C17 contracts and exclude zero-size resize. Tool manuals pin documents, not installed executables. Record actual versions, target support, symbols and enabled options for every run. GDB's shared manual is a dated development snapshot. The ASan paper is historical mechanism evidence, with no transplanted overhead prediction.

For initialization, the inspected Memcheck valid-value/address subsections explain the model; MSan is a supplemental supported-environment comparison. For stack mitigation, the inspected GCC guard/check/probe entries show narrower contracts. For a watched Cortex-M object, use the two inspected Arm DWT pages and accepted fault/status passages; broader optional register programming requires new inspection. Read full runtime or peripheral chapters only after extending source scope through the research process.

## Mastery gate and feedback

For each topic submit a prediction, original negative control, earliest-invalid-state argument, repaired invariant, semantic regression and explicit observation limits. A quiet tool run cannot replace the repaired contract. An unavailable environment leaves its observation open; move to a supported host or keep a clearly limited static result. Apply [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) to the smallest failed criterion and rerun the relevant boundary/failure case. Explain allocation/lifetime and resource budgets even when a detector reports the symptom.

The final dossier must distinguish prevention from mitigation and survive new capacity, failure-prefix, address-token, initialization and completion-order cases. For independent unseen assessment, keep the selected variant's defect identity and semantic oracle withheld until the dossier is submitted. Self-authored delayed practice has weaker independence and does not close that criterion. Keep exact C-language and target assumptions in the report. Source declarations, finite fixtures, actual C execution and physical evidence have separate claims.

## Consolidation and transfer

After a delay, diagnose a changed mechanism with the same outward symptom, then the same mechanism with a different symptom. Vary count widths, retained roots, permitted nesting and cancellation order. Transfer to one existing container/parser/request pipeline and predict the first invalid state before enabling the tool. Compare the earlier and later evidence without editing original expected results to match a broken target.

## Environment and limits

The finite oracle verifies arithmetic and supplied identity/history contracts. It executes no learner C, sanitizer, debugger or board test. Hosted negative controls belong to disposable learner-owned processes with verified limits, bounded input and supervisor deadlines. Separate native and diagnostic builds; do not run Memcheck on an ASan binary. Disable core dumps for routine fault trials and record any evidence-retention variant explicitly.

Core hosted observation requires a supported Linux setup for the Memcheck comparison. The optional MSan experiment needs supported instrumented dependencies and is not a Windows claim. Native exhaustion uses child-only checked limits and a supervisor; it does not attempt recovery on the exhausted stack. Embedded extensions use qualified existing adapters after the named preludes. No undefined-pointer/double-free failure is required on a board. Host histories do not establish DMA, electrical or real-time behavior. F439 results do not generalize to cached Cortex-M7 targets.

Follow [guide-laboratory](#guide-laboratory), [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles), [guide-standards](#guide-standards), [guide-integrations](#guide-integrations) and [guide-audit](#guide-audit) for environment, boundary and evidence records.

# PR-T01-01 — Trace, invariant and finite-representation diagnostic

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | diagnostic | C |

**Teaching module:** [T01](#t01).

**Covered topics:** [T01.01](#t01-01), [T01.02](#t01-02).

## Contract

Implement a caller-storage prefix-sum routine for at most 16 signed values. Each input and every intermediate prefix must fit the declared result bounds. Return a range failure before any unrepresentable addition, even when cancellation would make the final mathematical sum fit. On every failure leave output storage unchanged; use a fixed local staging array before committing results. Before implementation, give an invariant and termination argument. Independently trace a recursive version on paper; implementation of recursion is optional, but its live-call and space account is required. Include conversion and flag exercises under an explicitly synthetic eight-bit representation, rather than claiming the host has eight-bit bytes.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 6 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture supplies [3, -1, 4], decimal 173, width 8 and flag mask 12. Expected prefix totals are [3, 2, 6]; the representation is binary 10101101 and hexadecimal ad. The flag table enumerates all four combinations of the two selected bits. Its signed-bound cases use a declared synthetic range -32768..32767: [32767, 1, -1] and [-32768, -1, 1] fail at zero-based index 1 although their final mathematical sums fit; [-32768, 32767, 1] succeeds with prefixes [-32768, -1, 0]. Also test the corresponding INT_MAX and INT_MIN cases for the actual C int type, using <limits.h> rather than assuming its width.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T01-01.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

First fill in prediction tables without running code. Implement the iterative component with no external C-library calls; use a hosted harness for printing. Validate the input value and test the next addition against the declared bounds before evaluating it; do not rely on a wider integer type being available. Stage at most 16 prefix results locally and publish them only after complete validation. Add empty and capacity-limit inputs, count operations, and compare a recursive state trace with the iterative trace. Check representability before accepting the synthetic width.

- **T01.01:** Trace a loop and recursive sum on [3, -1, 4]; count additions, iterations and maximum live calls, then state the invariant and decreasing measure. Reject a cancellation case whose intermediate prefix exceeds the declared bounds. Retain a state table, an induction argument, checked-prefix rejection evidence, and separate O(n) work / O(1) iterative / O(n) recursive stack claims. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.01.a (Trace loops and recursion using explicit state tables.); T01.01.b (Derive time and auxiliary-space costs for simple implementations.); T01.01.c (State loop invariants and termination conditions before coding.).

- **T01.02:** Convert decimal 173 to binary and hexadecimal, then build a truth table for two flags and compare any/all predicates. Retain conversions checked by reconstruction and a complete truth table including neither, each and both flags. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T01.02.a (Convert between binary, hexadecimal, and decimal representations.); T01.02.b (Relate Boolean expressions to masks and truth tables.); T01.02.c (Distinguish mathematical integers from finite machine representations.).

## Failure cases

Reject a list longer than capacity, an out-of-range input, or an unrepresentable intermediate prefix without changing output storage. Do not dereference an empty range. Never compute an overflowing prefix first and inspect it afterward. A representable final mathematical sum is insufficient: retain the positive and negative cancellation failures as regressions.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit traces, an initialization/preservation/exit proof including representability before every addition, the decreasing measure, complexity accounts and a dependency contract. Show unchanged output sentinels after each cancellation failure and the successful boundary trace. Account for the fixed staging capacity separately from the unbounded-recursion stack model. Each representation result must reconstruct the decimal input. Show any-bit and all-bit predicates differ on a one-bit case.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Use k as the number already processed, not the next valid index and last processed index interchangeably. Draw recursive activations until the base case; include the base activation in the stated counting convention.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Transfer challenge

Replace summation with maximum selection, defining the empty case explicitly. Explain which part of the invariant and which storage bound change.

Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

Expected categories follow explicitly declared properties. Functions have a separate call/linkage analysis and are not assigned object storage duration. Actual compiler symbol output is collected separately because optimization can remove unused symbols.

- **T02.01:** Make a catalog of pointer-to-array, array-of-pointers and function-pointer declarations; annotate declarations versus definitions and rewrite one nested declaration using two typedefs. Retain expression-based explanations, compilable examples and intermediate typedefs that preserve the original type. Retain a compatibility table and a wrapper-struct experiment that demonstrates stronger semantic separation. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.02.a (Distinguish object, function, incomplete, scalar, and aggregate types.); T02.02.b (Identify compatible types across separate declarations.); T02.02.c (Explain the limits of typedef-based semantic type separation.).

# PR-T02-02 — Typed expressions and a two-pass variadic protocol

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |

## Contract

Implement a bounded variadic formatter using a count plus explicit tags. Limit the protocol to promoted int and double arguments; support a sizing pass and a writing pass through va_copy. Separately build a typed-expression and sequencing notebook, replacing ambiguous effectful call-site expressions with explicit steps before they reach the formatter.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 8 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture supplies an abstract signed value -1 and unsigned comparison width 16. Its converted value is 65535 and its comparison against unsigned 1 is false. This is a synthetic arithmetic model, not a claim that the host unsigned int has 16 bits. Add formatter cases for zero arguments and a promoted float.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T02-02.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Document the tag/count convention, annotate promotions at every call and pair each va_list initialization/copy with va_end. Draw expression trees for arithmetic and conditional operators. Build sequencing graphs for safe and unsafe examples. Run only defined expressions and compare strict-build diagnostics for separate negative cases.

- **T02.06:** Design a tagged/count convention for a statistics formatter, perform two passes using va_copy, and audit every call-site argument after promotion. Retain a promotion ledger, empty-list case, two-pass output and explicit va_start/va_end ownership for each list. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.06.a (Apply default argument promotions at variadic call sites.); T02.06.b (Use va_start, va_arg, va_copy, and va_end correctly.); T02.06.c (Specify a reliable argument-type and argument-count convention.).

- **T02.07:** Draw the tree and type each node for arithmetic, conditional and assignment examples; add a range-checked conversion boundary. Retain a typed expression tree and a table showing both accepted conversions and rejected out-of-range values. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.07.a (Separate precedence, associativity, and evaluation order.); T02.07.b (Trace integer promotions and usual arithmetic conversions.); T02.07.c (Analyze conditional expressions, assignments, and explicit casts.).

- **T02.08:** List side effects for a nested-call example and replace a conflicting increment/read expression with explicit temporary values. Retain a sequencing graph, classification under the selected edition and a repair whose result no longer depends on argument order. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T02.08.a (Distinguish sequenced, unsequenced, and indeterminately sequenced evaluations.); T02.08.b (Classify conflicting reads and writes under the selected edition.); T02.08.c (Refactor expressions into explicit, reviewable steps.).

## Failure cases

A tag/type mismatch is a caller contract violation that cannot generally be detected by the callee; do not execute it as an ordinary malformed-input case. Insufficient output capacity must report required size and preserve the chosen termination policy.

## Acceptance and evidence

Show identical semantic output from both traversals, exact capacity boundaries and a conversion ledger. Explain an unspecified argument order that remains defined and one unsequenced conflict that does not. Retain the explicit-step repair and a new test using negative and unsigned inputs.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Keep argument extraction in one switch with the protocol types visible. Separate precedence questions from conversion questions before considering sequencing.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

# PR-T03-03 — Raw-storage slot and alias contract audit

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T03](#t03).

**Covered topics:** [T03.07](#t03-07), [T03.08](#t03-08), [T03.09](#t03-09), [T03.10](#t03-10).

## Contract

Build a single-element raw-storage abstraction with explicit allocator callbacks, type size/alignment, initialization and destruction. Exercise one concrete type through a typed wrapper. Create an aliasing/provenance audit alongside it, comparing valid representation copying, invalid cast-based access, restricted disjoint transforms and stale address reuse. The portable component makes no direct library calls.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 10 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture defines half-open ranges [0,4), [4,8), [2,6) and [8,8). Its pairwise overlap results establish that adjacent and empty ranges do not overlap, while partially intersecting ranges do. This arithmetic oracle supports contracts, not an implementation-dependent pointer-order test.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T03-03.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Write storage and callback obligations before allocation. Compare typed construction with copying a live representation. Give a permitted-lvalue table and label extensions. Implement a disjoint-range transform and a separate overlap-supporting policy. Audit a same-address-after-free story using lifetime and a separately labeled provenance model.

- **T03.07:** Specify one typed raw-storage slot and compare initialization by a typed write and copying from a live typed object. Retain an access-type timeline and a container contract naming type, alignment, initialization and release. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T03.07.a (Trace how allocated storage is initialized and accessed.); T03.07.b (Compare typed writes, character access, and copying representations.); T03.07.c (Audit reusable raw-storage containers against the selected C rules.).

- **T03.08:** Compare a byte-copy representation experiment with a cast-based pun and an explicitly labeled compiler extension; keep invalid cases out of execution tests. Retain a permitted-access table, portable byte-copy alternative and build observations distinguished from language guarantees. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T03.08.a (Identify potentially incompatible lvalue accesses.); T03.08.b (Compare union-based, byte-copy, and cast-based representation inspection.); T03.08.c (Separate ISO guarantees from compiler-specific aliasing conventions.).

- **T03.09:** Write copy/transform contracts for disjoint and overlapping ranges, and choose a non-restrict entry point when overlap is permitted. Retain range diagrams, valid/invalid association examples and optimized-code comparisons only for the valid contract. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T03.09.a (Identify the objects and executions covered by restrict associations.); T03.09.b (Construct valid and invalid overlapping-access examples.); T03.09.c (Compare optimized code only after establishing the aliasing preconditions.).

- **T03.10:** Create a claim ledger for same-address reuse after release, integer round trips and a container-recovery idiom; distinguish established rules from proposed models. Retain a labeled authority table and a handle-based alternative that avoids relying on stale address identity. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T03.10.a (Separate numeric address equality from valid object access.); T03.10.b (Compare base-standard rules, provenance specifications, and implementation models.); T03.10.c (Document assumptions behind low-level pointer reconstruction techniques.).

## Failure cases

Allocator failure leaves the slot empty; failed construction must not publish a live value. Reject insufficient alignment/capacity. Do not execute incompatible lvalue accesses or stale pointers as expected-output tests. Restrict promises must cover the accesses, not only distinct base addresses.

## Acceptance and evidence

Show a complete slot state/access timeline, release exactly once, and a reachable-callback dependency audit. Present optimized-code evidence only after proving the transform’s alias contract. Provide a handle alternative for the address-reuse scenario.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Start with one known type instead of a fully generic container. Treat allocation, initialization and publication as separate states. Compare addresses only inside the synthetic range model or under a documented target extension.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Inputs and expected results

The synthetic size fixture has prefix 16, element size 4, counts 0, 3 and 100, and limit 255. Expected sizes are 16 and 28 for the first two; the third is rejected without producing a truncated size. Actual structure prefix/alignment values come from the selected target.

## Steps

Check multiplication and addition before allocation. Initialize every member that will be read. Inject allocation failure for initial creation and resize; use a temporary pointer for resize. Record view validity on success/failure. Build a positive-bound VLA example only where supported, and a fixed/caller-storage alternative.

For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T03.12.a (Calculate checked allocation sizes for flexible array members.); T03.12.b (Track VLA lifetime, bounds evaluation, and edition-dependent availability.); T03.12.c (Compare flexible arrays with explicit pointer/length representations.).

- **T03.13:** Implement resize through a temporary owner, inject failure and compare pointer views with slot/generation handles across relocation. Retain success/failure lifetime diagrams, leak-free failure tests and a documented invalidation table. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T03.13.a (Model realloc success and failure as distinct lifetime transitions.); T03.13.b (Specify iterator, slice, and pointer validity across container mutations.); T03.13.c (Choose stable handles where direct pointers cannot remain valid.).

## Failure cases

Use count <= (limit-prefix)/element_size after checking prefix <= limit; this avoids forming the overflowing product. Separate old and proposed capacity until commit.

# PR-T04-04 — Floating contract and boundary laboratory

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T04](#t04).

**Covered topics:** [T04.09](#t04-09), [T04.10](#t04-10), [T04.11](#t04-11), [T04.12](#t04-12).

## Contract

Create a floating-point laboratory that records the chosen type characteristics, exception/rounding support and strict compiler configuration. Compare naive and compensated accumulation, fused versus separated operations where supported, and one explicitly relaxed build. The result is a numerical dossier, not a universal guarantee of IEEE behavior.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 10 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture uses exact decimal strings 10000000000000000, 1 and -10000000000000000; its mathematical sum is 1. It also supplies reference 0 and observed 0.000001 with absolute tolerance 0.000002, so the declared near-zero test accepts it. Learner floating results are measured separately under a recorded format.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T04-04.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Record FLT_RADIX, precision and exponent limits. Partition signed zero, exceptional and adjacent values conditionally on target support. Compute an independent exact/high-precision reference. Compare accumulation order and compensation, investigate contraction and supported fenv operations, then document every semantic assumption relaxed by the alternate build.

- **T04.09:** Record radix/precision/exponent limits and classify conditional exceptional values on the chosen target. Retain a format report, adjacent-value observations and clearly bounded assumptions for exceptional cases. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T04.09.a (Identify target formats and relevant implementation characteristics.); T04.09.b (Examine NaNs, infinities, signed zero, and subnormal handling.); T04.09.c (Compare floating-point representation with real-number arithmetic.).

- **T04.10:** Compare naive and compensated summation on cancellation-prone data and a fused/separate expression where supported. Retain higher-precision or exact references, error tables and a justified criterion for each workload. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T04.10.a (Quantify rounding, cancellation, and accumulation error.); T04.10.b (Compare fused operations and separated arithmetic under stated assumptions.); T04.10.c (Choose absolute, relative, and ULP-oriented test criteria.).

- **T04.11:** Build a strict and documented relaxed configuration, inspect supported environment operations and record semantic changes before timings. Retain compiler flags, environment-support probes, exception observations and a contract comparison. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T04.11.a (Inspect rounding modes and floating-point exception behavior.); T04.11.b (Analyze evaluation precision and floating-point contraction policies.); T04.11.c (Compare strict and fast-math builds without silently changing the specification.).

- **T04.12:** Generate boundary partitions and minimize one numerical disagreement without loosening tolerance first. Retain a test partition, independent references, minimized disagreement and recorded acceptance rationale. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T04.12.a (Generate exceptional, adjacent, extreme, and cancellation-prone inputs.); T04.12.b (Use higher-precision or independently derived reference results.); T04.12.c (Separate tolerance selection from unexplained test relaxation.).

## Failure cases

Do not use a relative-only comparison at zero. Treat unsupported rounding/exception facilities as explicit limits. Never increase a tolerance solely to silence a failure; minimize the disagreement and revisit the analysis. Keep performance conclusions within identical semantic requirements.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit format/environment evidence, error tables, boundary vectors and criterion derivations. Explain at least one cancellation case and one strict/relaxed disagreement. Save compiler flags, library version and reference precision so another reader can reproduce the experiment.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Begin with exact rational or decimal reference calculations, then distinguish conversion error from accumulation error. Record signed-zero behavior without assuming it survives fast-math.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

# PR-T06-01 — Preprocessor laboratory and safe wrappers

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T06](#t06).

**Covered topics:** [T06.01](#t06-01), [T06.02](#t06-02), [T06.03](#t06-03), [T06.04](#t06-04), [T06.05](#t06-05).

## Contract

Create a token-transformation notebook and a small wrapper header. Cover line splicing/comments, invocation rules, prescan/rescan, two-level stringification/pasting, empty/nonempty variadics, evaluation count and statement-macro scope. Prefer typed inline functions for value computations where possible; any retained macro has an explicit evaluation contract.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 8 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture supplies a synthetic replacement table A -> B, B -> 7 and token A. Expected rescanned result is 7. A separate spelling input VALUE with expanded value 7 expects direct stringification VALUE and two-level stringification 7. Actual compiler token formatting may differ, so compare normalized tokens.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T06-01.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Predict every expansion before -E. Keep source-phase examples minimal. Repair precedence, double-evaluation and dangling-else defects, then count effects only in defined calls. Compare baseline variadics with a capability-checked __VA_OPT__ form; label comma-swallowing extensions. Include reserved-name and caller-collision reviews.

- **T06.01:** Create line-splice/comment/literal examples and compare physical source, logical tokens and -E output. Retain a phase timeline and minimal sources that explain each surprising token result. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T06.01.a (Trace source-character handling, line splicing, tokenization, and preprocessing.); T06.01.b (Analyze comments and literals at the correct translation stage.); T06.01.c (Inspect preprocessed output to explain unexpected compilation results.).

- **T06.02:** Trace nested replacement lists and a macro name used without parentheses, then check the preprocessor output. Retain a token-stage table and actual -E observations with no semantic inference from text alone. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T06.02.a (Follow argument prescan, substitution, rescanning, and suppression rules.); T06.02.b (Distinguish object-like and function-like macro invocation.); T06.02.c (Diagnose surprising expansion caused by nested replacement lists.).

- **T06.03:** Build two-level stringify/paste helpers and one intentionally invalid token combination as a negative preprocessing case. Retain exact token/string results and a separated preprocessing-versus-semantic diagnostic ledger. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T06.03.a (Apply stringification and token pasting with controlled expansion.); T06.03.b (Generate identifiers without accidentally creating invalid tokens.); T06.03.c (Separate textual assembly from semantic type checking.).

- **T06.04:** Implement a trace wrapper with baseline and supported C23 forms, testing empty/nonempty arguments and side-effect counts. Retain expansion vectors, capability checks and observed evaluation counts for defined calls. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T06.04.a (Handle empty and nonempty variadic argument cases deliberately.); T06.04.b (Compare C23 __VA_OPT__ with documented older extensions.); T06.04.c (Design macros that preserve argument evaluation contracts.).

- **T06.05:** Repair a minimum macro and a dangling-else statement macro; compare a typed function alternative. Retain a side-effect counter test, scope/collision review and a documented remaining contract. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T06.05.a (Prevent unintended repeated evaluation and precedence changes.); T06.05.b (Analyze statement macros, dangling else, and scope interactions.); T06.05.c (Avoid reserved names and collisions with caller identifiers.).

## Failure cases

Invalid token pastes and unsupported features belong to negative tests. Do not run a duplicated unsequenced modification to obtain an evaluation count. A recursion cycle in the synthetic model is rejected by the fixture verifier rather than imitating full preprocessor suppression.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit stage tables, normalized -E output, negative diagnostics and side-effect-counter evidence. State exactly how many times each public argument can be evaluated and what types are accepted. Show a typed inline replacement for one risky macro.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Separate preprocessing token behavior from the semantics of the resulting expression. Add expansion layers one at a time for # and ##.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

# PR-T10-03 — Raw syscall transfer adapter

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | D |

**Teaching module:** [T10](#t10).

**Covered topics:** [T10.06](#t10-06), [T10.07](#t10-07).

## Contract

Implement a target-specific syscall adapter with declared register assignments/clobbers and raw-error conversion. Above it, write-all/read-bounded logic must preserve progress across partial transfers and EINTR, stop on EOF/zero progress and expose would-block policy. Hosted oracles and scripted backends remain outside the custom executable boundary.

## Inputs and expected results

Load [fixtures/systems/PR-T10-03.json](fixtures/systems/PR-T10-03.json). Its `input` and `expected` define an exact synthetic case, not an observation from a real compiler, filesystem, board or concurrent run. Run `python tools/verify_systems_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to recompute all declared fields. Keep input immutable for the reference comparison; store observed outputs separately. The fixture is one anchor, not exhaustive acceptance coverage.

## Steps

1. Write the operation/state/effects contract and predict the fixture result by hand.
2. Establish the smallest supported positive case and record environment/provenance.

- **T10.06:** Map a six-argument synthetic call and check both success and negative-error decoding.
- **T10.07:** Implement a write-all adapter and a bounded read loop over a scripted transfer backend.

3. Add boundary and deliberate-failure cases before broadening the implementation.
4. Minimize each disagreement and retain the earliest broken invariant.

## Failure cases

- Challenge the mistaken claim: C-call register assignments can be reused unchanged for syscalls. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.
- Challenge the mistaken claim: Retrying every error from the beginning is safe. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.

Exercise empty/singleton or zero-progress states where the operation admits them, exact capacity, one beyond capacity, repeated completion/cleanup and a deliberately invalid precondition. For storage-owning work, inject acquisition failures and verify unchanged old ownership. For build/binary/source studies, inject a wrong edge, symbol, width, target assumption or unsupported environment and require a visible failure verdict. Never execute malformed pointers or privileged instructions just to demonstrate a negative case. Apply these cases to the declared operation; document any inapplicable case and its reason.

## Acceptance and evidence

- **T10.06:** A register/clobber diagram and error table match the declared ABI, not an accidental successful run.
- **T10.07:** Transferred bytes occur exactly once, and zero progress terminates visibly rather than spinning.

Submit contract, implementation or awareness dossier, reference comparison, independent generated cases, failure traces, effect/resource ledger and environment manifest. The independent oracle checks the synthetic mathematical/abstract case; actual platform behavior needs the separate observations specified above. Complete the linked-objective checklist with distinct evidence items:

- [ ] `T10.06.a`: Map syscall numbers, arguments, clobbers, and results to registers. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.
- [ ] `T10.06.b`: Compare syscall ABI with ordinary C-call ABI. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.
- [ ] `T10.06.c`: Separate raw kernel error returns from libc errno conventions. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.
- [ ] `T10.07.a`: Implement partial-transfer handling and interruption policies. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.
- [ ] `T10.07.b`: Handle EOF, zero progress, and operation-specific error conditions. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.
- [ ] `T10.07.c`: Keep syscall wrappers separate from higher-level stream abstractions. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.

## Hints and recovery

Separate the raw Linux negative-error convention from the libc -1/errno convention. Keep the buffer cursor and remaining count across EINTR; do not restart from byte zero after partial progress.
