# PR-T12-01 — Header, type and bounded-format inventory

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T12](#t12).

**Covered topics:** [T12.01](#t12-01), [T12.02](#t12-02), [T12.09](#t12-09).

## Contract

Create a standard-library inventory and a bounded status formatter. Classify ISO facilities by edition and distinguish POSIX, optional annex and implementation interfaces. The formatter reports required length, written length, termination and truncation/error status, with an audited format-to-argument-type mapping.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 8 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture formats an already determined byte string abcdef into capacities 0, 1, 4 and 7. Required length is 6; written lengths are 0, 0, 3 and 6, and termination is promised only for nonzero capacity. The zero-capacity path is a sizing operation, not a generic null-pointer exemption for unrelated calls.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T12-01.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Build a limit/type/format report using actual available typedefs. Write compile-only header probes separately from link/run probes. Implement formatting around checked snprintf results, testing negativity before size conversion. Compare integer length modifiers and inttypes macros. Add negative mismatches as diagnostic tests, not executable valid calls.

- **T12.01:** Create an edition-tagged header/family matrix and classify a deliberate mix of ISO, POSIX and extension interfaces. Retain a facility/authority/dependency inventory with compile-only versus linked evidence. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.01.a (Separate the complete standard library from the single stdlib.h header.); T12.01.b (Inventory headers and function families by language edition.); T12.01.c (Distinguish ISO, POSIX, optional annex, and implementation-specific interfaces.).

- **T12.02:** Build a limit/format report and compile negative mismatched-format examples separately. Retain type/range/format mapping and compiler/header/library layer records. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.02.a (Use standard limit, type, format, and feature macros correctly.); T12.02.b (Audit fixed-width integer formatting and size-dependent conversions.); T12.02.c (Separate compiler-provided headers from external linked facilities.).

- **T12.09:** Implement bounded diagnostic formatting with a required-size result and a declared truncation policy. Retain format/type audit, zero-capacity sizing, exact-fit/truncation and encoding-error policy. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.09.a (Match variadic argument types to format specifications.); T12.09.b (Handle precision, width, length modifiers, and required output size.); T12.09.c (Design bounded formatting with explicit truncation and error reporting.).

## Failure cases

Handle encoding failure distinctly from truncation. Missing optional headers/types are explicit inventory entries. Do not assume declarations imply linked implementation. A fixed-width-looking typedef still needs its correct format type.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the facility matrix, exact format ledger and boundary outputs. Independently calculate lengths and retain an invalid-format diagnostic. Explain the difference between stdlib.h, the complete library and linked runtime support.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Start with a constant text formatter before combining numeric values. Keep required length and stored length in different fields.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

# PR-T12-02 — Byte buffers, locale boundary and chunked text

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | B |

**Teaching module:** [T12](#t12).

**Covered topics:** [T12.03](#t12-03), [T12.04](#t12-04), [T12.05](#t12-05), [T12.06](#t12-06).

## Contract

Implement a caller-storage byte-buffer component and a strict UTF-8 validation boundary. Its component storage is allocation-free; individually allowed memory/classification calls and callback effects are listed. Use a hosted comparison harness for memmove, ctype and restartable locale conversion. Do not equate the UTF-8 validator with normalization or grapheme processing.

The declared profile **B** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 12 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture contains byte sequences [65], [226,130,172], [192,175], [237,160,128] and [240,159]. Expected states are valid, valid, invalid, invalid and incomplete, with code points [65], [8364] for valid sequences. The final incomplete prefix must not be accepted as a completed string.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T12-02.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Specify byte-array/view/string invariants and append reject/truncate policy. Compare overlap-safe movement with nonoverlap copy under valid argument domains. Audit ctype inputs through unsigned char. Feed a locale multibyte character across chunks with explicit mbstate_t and recovery. Compare that state trace with the strict RFC grammar, testing embedded zero and output limits.

- **T12.03:** Write checked copy/move wrappers with explicit zero-length policy and compare overlapping ranges through a byte-array oracle. Retain range/overlap proofs, exact moved bytes and separately analyzed invalid calls. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.03.a (Specify overlap, object validity, size, and return-value contracts.); T12.03.b (Compare copying representations with constructing typed values.); T12.03.c (Test boundary cases without inventing universally valid null-pointer exceptions.).

- **T12.04:** Implement bounded append and conversion from a view to a terminated string, including embedded-zero input. Retain exact content/length/termination results for empty, exact-fit, truncated and embedded-zero cases. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.04.a (Distinguish byte arrays, terminated strings, and pointer/length views.); T12.04.b (Track capacity, logical length, termination, and truncation policies.); T12.04.c (Compare strcpy, strncpy, snprintf, and explicit-length interfaces by contract.).

- **T12.05:** Classify byte inputs under a named locale and demonstrate the safe unsigned-char boundary. Retain domain checks, locale identity and a byte-versus-code-point explanation. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.05.a (Check valid domains for ctype functions and macros.); T12.05.b (Distinguish byte classification from Unicode character properties.); T12.05.c (Identify global and per-operation locale assumptions.).

- **T12.06:** Feed a character across chunk boundaries, handle invalid bytes and bounded output, then compare with a strict UTF-8 validator. Retain state/result traces, invalid recovery and a locale/UTF-8 boundary table. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.06.a (Track conversion state and incomplete input across calls.); T12.06.b (Handle invalid sequences and output-capacity limits.); T12.06.c (Separate wchar_t representation from a portable Unicode interchange format.).

## Failure cases

Reject overlong forms, surrogate encodings and invalid continuation bytes. Preserve incomplete state only under a documented streaming policy. Do not pass negative char values to ctype or invent null-pointer exceptions for zero-length memory calls. Failure leaves the buffer invariant intact.

Supply exact byte/length/termination checks, overlap traces, locale identity and chunk-state evidence. Audit the reachable component call graph and any selected opaque functions before claiming allocation-free behavior. Show independent invalid/empty/exact-capacity cases.

# PR-T12-03 — Allocation adapter and strict conversion parser

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T12](#t12).

**Covered topics:** [T12.07](#t12-07), [T12.08](#t12-08), [T12.10](#t12-10).

## Contract

Build a small allocation adapter with injected failure and a line-oriented strict decimal parser. Use nonzero resize plus explicit release for an empty object. The parser separates tokenization, numeric conversion, trailing-data policy and application range; compare its clarity with one width-bounded scanf example.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 10 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture tokens are 0, -12, 12x, an empty token and 999 with range -128..127. Expected statuses are ok, ok, invalid, invalid and range. Valid values are 0 and -12; no partial output is published for the other tokens. The grammar intentionally uses ASCII decimal and does not import C23 binary-prefix behavior.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T12-03.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Specify ownership and alignment/zero-size policies. Inject allocation failure at creation and resize, preserving the old owner on nonzero failure. Use strto end pointers and range reporting, then validate the full token. For floating parsing, declare C locale and a rounding/error policy. Compare scanf counts, field widths, leftover bytes and EOF.

- **T12.07:** Write an allocation adapter with failure injection, nonzero resize and explicit empty release; compare aligned storage obligations. Retain allocation/lifetime ledger, checked sizes and exactly-once cleanup under each failure. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.07.a (Compare malloc, calloc, realloc, free, and aligned allocation.); T12.07.b (Analyze failure, zero-size, alignment, and lifetime rules by edition.); T12.07.c (Preserve ownership correctly when resizing operations fail.).

- **T12.08:** Build strict decimal-integer and C-locale floating parsers around explicit token boundaries. Retain no-conversion, trailing-junk, range, sign and locale tests with unchanged outputs on failure. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.08.a (Compare strto-family APIs with weaker conversion interfaces.); T12.08.b (Validate end pointers, range errors, signs, bases, and trailing data.); T12.08.c (Specify locale and rounding assumptions for numeric conversions.).

- **T12.10:** Compare a width-bounded scanf example with an explicit parser on malformed, ambiguous and leftover input. Retain destination-size audit, count/EOF distinctions and exact remaining-input observations. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.10.a (Analyze conversion counts, field widths, and destination storage.); T12.10.b (Compare scanf-family parsing with explicit tokenization and conversion.); T12.10.c (Handle ambiguous input, leftover characters, and EOF distinctly.).

## Failure cases

Distinguish no conversion, trailing data and range failure. Reject signs according to the declared unsigned-input policy rather than trusting strtoul to reject minus. Do not lose allocations on resize or assume calloc bytes establish every typed invariant.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit failure/lifetime traces, exact parser cases and a scanf-versus-explicit comparison. Audit output initialization on every status and test repeated cleanup. Record locale and conversion-family edition limits.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Keep the original owner until resize succeeds. Use endptr == start for no conversion and a separate full-token check.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

# PR-T12-04 — Stream state and execution-environment notebook

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T12](#t12).

**Covered topics:** [T12.11](#t12-11), [T12.14](#t12-14), [T12.15](#t12-15).

## Contract

Implement a small FILE-based copier and write an environment/control-flow notebook. Record orientation, buffering, indicators and cleanup, investigate an update stream with legal transitions, and contrast calendar/CPU/elapsed measurements. Analyze restricted signal handling, nonlocal jumps and selected thread/atomic capabilities without claiming the richer platform contract is ISO.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 10 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture is a synthetic read trace returning chunks ab, c, then EOF, followed by a distinct error trace. Expected copied bytes are abc; successful chunk count is 2, terminal kind eof. EOF and error are explicit backend results, not predictions from a pre-read feof check.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T12-04.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Use the read result to drive the copy loop. Capture ferror/feof after failed reads and check fclose. Exercise required update-stream positioning/flushing transitions. Copy environment data under a stated ownership policy, inventory exit handlers/system effects and compare time roles. Draw a setjmp/longjmp resource/local-state trace and a signal flag protocol; probe thread/atomic layers separately.

- **T12.11:** Build a small stream copier and update-stream experiment with explicit transitions, then contrast FILE with an OS descriptor. Retain read-result/error/EOF traces, cleanup and documented flush/position limitations. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.11.a (Model FILE ownership, orientation, buffering, and error indicators.); T12.11.b (Distinguish EOF, failure, flushing, positioning, and update-stream transitions.); T12.11.c (Relate standard streams to lower-level OS descriptors without conflating them.).

- **T12.14:** Compare time measurements, copy an environment value under a documented protocol and inventory termination/system effects. Retain measurement-role table, environment lifetime notes and a declared effects/dependency ledger. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.14.a (Distinguish calendar time, CPU time, and elapsed-time measurements.); T12.14.b (Audit environment variables, termination handlers, and system interaction.); T12.14.c (Identify implementation-dependent time representations and concurrency hazards.).

- **T12.15:** Analyze a nonlocal-jump cleanup defect, design a restricted signal flag policy and inventory selected thread/atomic contracts. Retain control/lifetime trace, allowed-handler operations and bounded thread/runtime capability evidence. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.15.a (Separate ISO signals from richer operating-system signal interfaces.); T12.15.b (Analyze setjmp/longjmp lifetime, local-state, and cleanup consequences.); T12.15.c (Locate thread and atomic contracts before applying platform assumptions.).

## Failure cases

Closing invalidates FILE use. Flushing is not a universal durability guarantee. A longjmp path must not skip promised cleanup, and modified nonvolatile locals cannot be treated as unchanged. Keep handler operations within the selected ISO or POSIX contract and label unavailable support.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit stream traces, cleanup/failure checks, update-state reasoning, environment/time ledger and nonlocal-jump analysis. Explain why descriptors and FILE, CPU and elapsed time, and ISO and POSIX signals are different contracts.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Start with a regular file and short deterministic input. Investigate one transition at a time rather than mixing orientation, buffering and platform descriptors.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Transfer challenge

Replace the stream with a nonseekable adapter and identify which update/position assumptions must be removed.

Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

# PR-T12-05 — Sorting, math and pinned implementation literacy

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T12](#t12).

**Covered topics:** [T12.12](#t12-12), [T12.13](#t12-13), [T12.16](#t12-16).

## Contract

Write a comparator/search test harness and an implementation-reading dossier comparing the selected live glibc manual with pinned glibc 2.41 and musl 1.2.5 qsort sources. Add bounded probes for scalar, complex, generic math and floating error reporting. Compare the inspected Picolibc 1.8.10 console and POSIX file-I/O configurations named below. This is a documentation/source comparison; a Picolibc build or firmware deployment is not required in this 12 h project.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 12 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture list [2147483647, -2147483648, 0, 0, 7] sorts to [-2147483648,0,0,7,2147483647]. Search queries 0 and 8 are present and absent. Equal-item positions and qsort stability are not prescribed. Actual libc allocation/stack observations are separate from this value oracle.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T12-05.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Use relational comparisons instead of subtracting operands. Test comparator antisymmetry/order consistency and bsearch’s sorted-order precondition. Follow the assigned pinned glibc/musl source entries and record algorithm/buffer choices. Compare rand reproducibility with security requirements. Map math families, probe supported domain/range reporting and apply T04 reference/tolerance reasoning. For Picolibc 1.8.10, produce two configuration rows: (A) tinystdio=true, posix-io=false, posix-console=false with application-defined console FILE objects/getc/putc and optional flush; (B) tinystdio=true, posix-io=true, posix-console=true with POSIX console and fopen/fdopen support. Map row B to malloc/free and open/close/read/write/lseek, and explain which row A obligations remain despite disabled file I/O. Use the exact inspected Stdio options, Tinystdio options, stdin/stdout/stderr and fopen, fdopen headings; this is a plan from documentation, not an executed backend.

- **T12.12:** Use a relational comparator, test duplicates/extremes, and compare pinned sorting sources plus a deterministic nonsecurity generator. Retain comparator properties, sorted/search checks and a randomness-purpose classification. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.12.a (Specify comparator consistency and avoid arithmetic-overflow comparisons.); T12.12.b (Separate mandated semantics from implementation algorithm choices.); T12.12.c (Compare reproducible pseudorandom use with security-sensitive randomness requirements.).

- **T12.13:** Map one scalar, complex and generic operation, probe a domain/range case and record observed errno/exceptions where supported. Retain facility map, supported reporting probes and justified independent reference tolerances. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.13.a (Map scalar, complex, type-generic, and environment facilities.); T12.13.b (Examine domain/range errors and target-dependent floating behavior.); T12.13.c (Compare mathematical accuracy specifications with observed numerical results.).

- **T12.16:** Navigate the specified pinned qsort entries and compare the two specified Picolibc console/file-I/O configurations, distinguishing public guarantees from internal choices. Retain pinned source/call-flow map, two-row Picolibc configuration/backend inventory and explicitly limited effect claims. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T12.16.a (Navigate pinned glibc and musl implementations of selected routines.); T12.16.b (Compare an embedded-oriented library's configuration and backend requirements.); T12.16.c (Separate public contracts, internal optimization, and application-visible extensions.).

## Failure cases

Do not infer allocation-free behavior from the musl file alone or mandate glibc’s current algorithm as the API. Random sequences are not portable across implementations or suitable for secrets. Unsupported fenv/error mechanisms remain explicit limits.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit sorted/search/property checks, versioned glibc/musl entry/call-flow maps, the two-row Picolibc configuration/backend table and numerical error probes. Separate ISO public contract, library-specific configuration, inspected internal choice and measured effects. State that the Picolibc backend rows were not built or deployed; identify what implementation/link/runtime evidence would be needed before an actual target claim.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

# PR-T13-04 — Pinned sort effects and restricted replacement

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T13](#t13).

**Covered topics:** [T13.09](#t13-09), [T13.10](#t13-10).

## Contract

Audit the same qsort API in inspected glibc 2.41 stdlib/qsort.c and musl 1.2.5 src/stdlib/qsort.c. Map allocation, temporary storage, callback and transitive-helper boundaries; distinguish glibc stack/heap selection and allocation-failure heapsort from musl smoothsort. Do not infer stable tie ordering or a complete effect bound from the API name. Locally implement a replacement restricted to at most sixteen int elements using insertion sort and caller-owned actual int storage, with visible over-capacity rejection preserving input. No qsort, external sorting or byte-library call performs the replacement. A separately hosted qsort run and mathematical sorted-multiset oracle check ordering only; comparator effects, stack, latency, size and maintenance have separately scoped evidence. Compare the two library source paths without claiming their uninspected transitive helpers are effect-free.

Worked source branch: the inspected glibc 2.41 source reserves a 1024-byte temporary stack buffer. Sorting 64 four-byte elements needs 256 temporary bytes and selects it; 300 four-byte elements need 1200 and reach the acquisition branch, which falls back to heapsort if acquisition fails. For ten 64-byte elements and eight-byte pointers, indirect storage is 2*10*8+64=224 bytes. These are source-selected temporary requirements, not total-stack bounds; helper and comparator frames/effects remain separate. The restricted local replacement accepts at most sixteen ints, so its workload and API exclusions are explicit.

The fixture is one anchor, not exhaustive acceptance coverage.

3. Add boundary and deliberate-failure cases before broadening the implementation.

# PR-T14-01 — Caller-owned arrays, views and rings

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T14](#t14).

**Covered topics:** [T14.01](#t14-01), [T14.02](#t14-02), [T14.06](#t14-06).

## Contract

Implement bounded insertion/erase, length/stride views and a count-based ring over caller storage. All access uses explicit bounds; borrowing never extends lifetime. Bulk ring transfers expose up to two spans and fail or report partial success according to a stated contract. No libc container or byte routines may implement these operations. Storage legality is part of acceptance. Under the selected C17 baseline, an aligned declared unsigned-char array is still a declared character array; alignment alone does not license arbitrary T* lvalue access. The portable byte arena uses byte APIs and explicit copying into/out of actual typed objects. A typed pool uses a real array of the selected T. A hosted harness may separately supply genuine allocated storage through a backing callback, while the studied allocator/container policy stays local. Firmware casts or mapping-backed typed objects need an explicit, inspected implementation contract and are reported under that contract, not as a blanket ISO C guarantee. Check effective type, alignment, bounds and lifetime independently.
The reusable target is Profile C: implement each studied algorithm/container/allocator/byte operation locally. A hosted test oracle may call mature libraries, but the target may not delegate its mechanism to qsort, bsearch, malloc/realloc/free, strto*, printf-style conversion, external memory primitives or equivalent library substitutes. Allocator callbacks/backing storage and compiler helpers must be explicitly scoped and audited.

# PR-T14-06 — Complete AVL family

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T14](#t14).

**Covered topics:** [T14.10](#t14-10).

## Contract

Implement AVL insertion and deletion completely, including single/double rotations and ancestor repair. Stored height equals reconstructed height and every balance magnitude is at most one. Generate small-key permutations and deletion orders against a sorted-set oracle; no library tree delegates are allowed. Keys form a set: duplicate insertion returns a distinct duplicate status and preserves the complete tree and payload ownership without replacement. Storage legality is part of acceptance. Under the selected C17 baseline, an aligned declared unsigned-char array is still a declared character array; alignment alone does not license arbitrary T* lvalue access. The portable byte arena uses byte APIs and explicit copying into/out of actual typed objects. A typed pool uses a real array of the selected T. A hosted harness may separately supply genuine allocated storage through a backing callback, while the studied allocator/container policy stays local. Firmware casts or mapping-backed typed objects need an explicit, inspected implementation contract and are reported under that contract, not as a blanket ISO C guarantee. Check effective type, alignment, bounds and lifetime independently.
The reusable target is Profile C: implement each studied algorithm/container/allocator/byte operation locally. A hosted test oracle may call mature libraries, but the target may not delegate its mechanism to qsort, bsearch, malloc/realloc/free, strto*, printf-style conversion, external memory primitives or equivalent library substitutes. Allocator callbacks/backing storage and compiler helpers must be explicitly scoped and audited.

Worked AVL repair: choose height(empty)=0 and height(leaf)=1, and balance=height(left)-height(right). Inserting 30,20,10 first makes root 30 left-heavy with balance +2. Rotate right at 30: root becomes 20 with leaf children 10 and 30; their heights are 1 and the root height is 2. Duplicate 20 is rejected with the entire structure unchanged. Deleting leaf 30 leaves root 20, left child 10, height 2 and balance +1; ancestor checks still run. More demanding deletion orders can decrease heights through several ancestors, so this anchor does not justify insertion-style early stopping.

# PR-T15-01 — Bounds and comparison-sort suite

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T15](#t15).

**Covered topics:** [T15.01](#t15-01), [T15.02](#t15-02).

## Contract

Implement linear search, lower/upper bounds, partition, insertion sort, stable merge sort and heap sort under explicit caller-workspace contracts. Reuse the binary-heap build/sift-down kernel already accepted in PR-T14-05; this milestone adds the shrinking active-region/sorted-suffix policy and its evidence rather than another heap implementation. No bsearch/qsort or external sorting/searching routines may perform the target operations. Labeled equal keys test stability; counters support, but do not replace, loop and complexity arguments.
The reusable target is Profile C: implement each studied algorithm/container/allocator/byte operation locally. A hosted test oracle may call mature libraries, but the target may not delegate its mechanism to qsort, bsearch, malloc/realloc/free, strto*, printf-style conversion, external memory primitives or equivalent library substitutes. Allocator callbacks/backing storage and compiler helpers must be explicitly scoped and audited.

Worked stable merge: sorted left [1A,3A] and right [1B,2B] have labeled equal keys. Taking the left element on equality produces [1A,1B,2B,3A], preserving the earlier 1A; taking the right equal key would violate stability. A four-element caller workspace receives one element per transition, and the two input cursors never pass their lengths. For heap sort, reuse PR-T14-05 build/sift-down: max-heap [4,3,2,1] has active length 4. Swap root with the final active element to obtain [1,3,2 | 4], shrink to 3, then sift to [3,1,2 | 4]. Next extraction gives [2,1 | 3,4]; the active root already dominates its child. The last exchange gives [1 | 2,3,4]. Each step preserves the active max-heap and increasing final suffix; heap sort has no stable-tie promise.

## Inputs and expected results

Its `input` and `expected` define an exact synthetic case, not an observation from a real compiler, filesystem, board or concurrent run. ## Contract

Implement an allocator callback contract and aligned bump arena over caller storage. Accept only declared power-of-two alignments, check every arithmetic step, define zero-size behavior and preserve cursor on exhaustion. No malloc/realloc/free/aligned_alloc or external allocator may perform the policy; a hosted backing buffer is merely input storage. Storage legality is part of acceptance. Under the selected C17 baseline, an aligned declared unsigned-char array is still a declared character array; alignment alone does not license arbitrary T* lvalue access. # PR-T16-09 — Adversarial allocator evidence

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T16](#t16).

**Covered topics:** [T16.14](#t16-14).

## Contract

Build an independent abstract live-extent model and generated allocate/free/resize traces with exhaustion and corruption injection. Check alignment, non-overlap, ownership, leaks and metadata after every action. Measure peak payload/charged bytes, fragmentation and latency distributions separately, disclosing instrumentation overhead. Storage legality is part of acceptance. Under the selected C17 baseline, an aligned declared unsigned-char array is still a declared character array; alignment alone does not license arbitrary T* lvalue access. The portable byte arena uses byte APIs and explicit copying into/out of actual typed objects. A typed pool uses a real array of the selected T. A hosted harness may separately supply genuine allocated storage through a backing callback, while the studied allocator/container policy stays local. Firmware casts or mapping-backed typed objects need an explicit, inspected implementation contract and are reported under that contract, not as a blanket ISO C guarantee. Check effective type, alignment, bounds and lifetime independently.
The reusable target is Profile C: implement each studied algorithm/container/allocator/byte operation locally. A hosted test oracle may call mature libraries, but the target may not delegate its mechanism to qsort, bsearch, malloc/realloc/free, strto*, printf-style conversion, external memory primitives or equivalent library substitutes. Allocator callbacks/backing storage and compiler helpers must be explicitly scoped and audited.

## Inputs and expected results

Load [fixtures/systems/PR-T16-09.json](fixtures/systems/PR-T16-09.json). Its `input` and `expected` define an exact synthetic case, not an observation from a real compiler, filesystem, board or concurrent run. Run `python tools/verify_systems_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to recompute all declared fields. Keep input immutable for the reference comparison; store observed outputs separately. The fixture is one anchor, not exhaustive acceptance coverage.

## Steps

1. Write the operation/state/effects contract and predict the fixture result by hand.
2. Establish the smallest supported positive case and record environment/provenance.

- **T16.14:** Generate allocate/free/resize traces with failures and compare against an abstract live-allocation model.

3. Add boundary and deliberate-failure cases before broadening the implementation.
4. Minimize each disagreement and retain the earliest broken invariant.

## Failure cases

- Challenge the mistaken claim: Passing a few throughput runs establishes allocator correctness. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.

Exercise empty/singleton or zero-progress states where the operation admits them, exact capacity, one beyond capacity, repeated completion/cleanup and a deliberately invalid precondition. For storage-owning work, inject acquisition failures and verify unchanged old ownership. For build/binary/source studies, inject a wrong edge, symbol, width, target assumption or unsupported environment and require a visible failure verdict. Never execute malformed pointers or privileged instructions just to demonstrate a negative case. Apply these cases to the declared operation; document any inapplicable case and its reason.

## Acceptance and evidence

- **T16.14:** Minimized corruption traces and separate peak/fragmentation/latency reports support bounded conclusions.

Submit contract, implementation or awareness dossier, reference comparison, independent generated cases, failure traces, effect/resource ledger and environment manifest. The independent oracle checks the synthetic mathematical/abstract case; actual platform behavior needs the separate observations specified above. Complete the linked-objective checklist with distinct evidence items:

- [ ] `T16.14.a`: Generate allocate/free/resize sequences with a reference ownership model. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.
- [ ] `T16.14.b`: Check overlap, alignment, leaks, corruption, and exhaustion invariants. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.
- [ ] `T16.14.c`: Measure peak usage, fragmentation, latency distribution, and instrumentation overhead. Attach a trace, artifact, counterexample or explicit bounded analysis; optional implementation conditions in this project remain in force.

## Hints and recovery

Maintain a separate live-extent model rather than asking allocator metadata to certify itself. Compare ownership and non-overlap after each operation before collecting latency statistics.

Before changing the target, determine whether the disagreement is its semantics, an invalid test precondition, a boundary mismatch or an environment limitation. If the fixture oracle fails, stop and repair the fixture/oracle independently; do not change expected data to fit the target. Return to the named prerequisite module when ownership, width or ordering assumptions are missing.

## Transfer challenge

An extension is accepted only after its new contract and independent evidence are supplied. Derive the recurrence and |1-h| condition, implement the finite-step update, then halve h over a fixed final time and plot/report errors.

Implement one normal path, then add each boundary/failure path. Run the independent fixture oracle and your own implementation checks separately; preserve versions, commands, binary identity and raw observations.

## Acceptance and evidence

Discrete outputs match, stability is classified under this equation only, and step-halving evidence is retained without claiming physical-model validation.

Retain an evidence item for each of the three original objectives of every linked topic, including explanation and a check of its own property. # PR-T18-01 — Transactional bounded-view API

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T18](#t18).

**Covered topics:** [T18.01](#t18-01), [T18.02](#t18-02), [T18.07](#t18-07), [T18.09](#t18-09).

## Contract

Implement a bounded byte-view append API with explicit units, capacity, aliasing and output-state rules. Success appends exactly the supplied bytes; insufficient capacity or forbidden overlap leaves content and logical length unchanged. Return a distinct status and valid length so that zero-length success cannot collide with an error sentinel.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 8 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture has initial bytes [1,2], appended bytes [3,4] and capacities 3 and 4. Expected results are rejected/unchanged [1,2] at capacity 3 and success [1,2,3,4] at capacity 4. The fixture assumes disjoint logical inputs; overlap policy is tested separately by the learner.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T18-01.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Write domain/pre/post/invariant clauses before implementation. Validate capacity with nonoverflowing arithmetic, implement the no-library component and add empty/full/invalid cases. Classify compile-time checks, runtime validation and internal assertions. Build with assertions enabled and disabled; required input rejection must remain.

- **T18.01:** Write a bounded byte-view and timeout domain contract, then list representable but forbidden states. Retain value partitions, unit-aware names and explicit acceptance/rejection tests. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T18.01.a (Specify valid values, ranges, units, and sentinel meanings.); T18.01.b (Distinguish representable states from permitted states.); T18.01.c (Make assumptions about target representation explicit.).

- **T18.02:** Define append pre/postconditions and prove the capacity check before writing. Retain a contract table and state snapshots proving the declared success/failure guarantee. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T18.02.a (Define preconditions, postconditions, and preserved invariants.); T18.02.b (Specify capacity, aliasing, mutation, and failure effects.); T18.02.c (Separate caller obligations from implementation checks.).

- **T18.07:** Design a lookup that permits zero as a valid value and a parse operation with explicit output-state rules. Retain result tables, sentinel-collision cases and output-state checks. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T18.07.a (Compare status returns, tagged results, and output parameters.); T18.07.b (Define success and failure initialization of output values.); T18.07.c (Prevent ambiguous sentinel collisions with valid results.).

- **T18.09:** Build enabled/disabled assertion configurations and compare externally invalid input behavior. Retain checks classified by purpose and identical required validation across build modes. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T18.09.a (Use compile-time checks, runtime validation, assertions, and tests appropriately.); T18.09.b (Define behavior when assertions or diagnostics are disabled.); T18.09.c (Keep contract violations distinguishable from ordinary environmental failures.).

## Failure cases

Reject invalid length/capacity relationships and forbidden overlap before mutation. Do not use a sentinel that collides with a valid zero result. Disabled assertions must not remove validation or argument evaluation required by the API.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit exact state snapshots, output-status rules, boundary tests and a dependency audit. Explain caller versus implementation obligations for overlap and representation. Test a consumer that knows only the public header and contract.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Separate validation and commit. Name capacities in bytes and avoid ambiguous size fields. Use output snapshots to detect a partially mutated failure path.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

Attempt the changed condition after a delay without copying the prior solution. Explain which invariant, lifetime, resource or dependency claims survive and which must be revised.

# PR-T18-02 — Owner, borrowed view and stable handle

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | B |

**Teaching module:** [T18](#t18).

**Covered topics:** [T18.03](#t18-03), [T18.04](#t18-04).

## Contract

Build a fixed-capacity owner/view abstraction with a mutation epoch or generation handle. Caller storage owns the bytes; borrowed views never release them. Define invalidation for mutation, reset and destruction. Add a production-source reading comparison with SQLite result pointers and prepared-statement finalization.

The declared profile **B** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 6 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture owner starts at generation 4. Handles carry generations 4 and 3; only generation 4 is valid. After reset increments the owner generation to 5, both old handles are stale. Generation wrap/exhaustion needs an explicit application policy rather than modulo reuse.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T18-02.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Write a creation/release/transfer ledger for memory and one descriptor/device-like synthetic resource. Implement view validation, reset and stale-handle rejection without allocation. Draw parent/child and callback/context timelines. Compare SQLite conversion/step/reset/finalize invalidation with your simpler policy.

- **T18.03:** Create creation/release/transfer ledgers for a buffer and a non-memory resource, contrasting shared and weak access. Retain resource ledgers with exactly one release obligation or an explicit shared-count protocol. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T18.03.a (Distinguish owned, borrowed, shared, transferred, and weak references.); T18.03.b (Document which operation creates and releases each resource.); T18.03.c (Model ownership consistently for memory, descriptors, locks, and devices.).

- **T18.04:** Design an owner/view/callback timeline and replace one fragile direct pointer with a generation handle. Retain an invalidation table and stale-view tests tied to exact operations. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T18.04.a (Express parent/child, view/owner, and callback/context lifetimes.); T18.04.b (Identify references invalidated by mutation or reset.); T18.04.c (Replace ambiguous lifetime rules with handles or explicit protocols.).

## Failure cases

A borrowed pointer is never freed by the borrower. An alive owner may still invalidate prior views. Reject stale handles before access and prohibit generation wrap from silently making old handles valid. Shared or weak references require a stated separate protocol.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit resource/lifetime ledgers, invalidation cases, independent stale-handle tests and the source-contract comparison. Audit selected callees before claiming component allocation freedom. Identify exactly when ownership transfers, if any transfer operation exists.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Model identity as slot plus generation, not numeric address. Keep owner storage and view metadata visibly separate.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

# PR-T19-03 — Pure state strategies and two traversal styles

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T19](#t19).

**Covered topics:** [T19.06](#t19-06), [T19.07](#t19-07).

## Contract

Implement a small pure state machine with effects returned as data, plus a fixed-capacity collection traversable by cursor and callback. Compare switch/table state dispatch and an injected runtime strategy with a static alternative. Both traversal styles must have explicit order, early-stop and mutation invalidation.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 8 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture values [2,4,6,8] stop before processing values greater than 5. Expected visited values are [2,4], total 6. A traversal epoch 3 becomes stale when mutation changes owner epoch to 4. The stop rule and epoch policy are part of the contract.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T19-03.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

State transition decisions precede effects. Implement equivalent switch/table outputs and compare dispatch visibility/cost. Add pull next and push visit interfaces, early stop and bounded-storage guarantees. Inject mutation during traversal and reject stale cursors according to the epoch policy; define callback reentry separately.

- **T19.06:** Implement one transition model with a pure core and compare switch/table dispatch plus one injected strategy. Retain equivalent transition outputs, effect boundaries and a reasoned dispatch choice. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T19.06.a (Separate transition logic from effectful operations.); T19.06.b (Compare tables, switches, and function-based dispatch.); T19.06.c (Justify dynamic dispatch against simpler static alternatives.).

- **T19.07:** Implement cursor and callback traversal over a fixed-capacity collection with epoch invalidation. Retain order/early-stop cases, stale-iterator checks and bounded temporary storage. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T19.07.a (Specify traversal order, mutation, and invalidation behavior.); T19.07.b (Implement cursor-based and callback-based traversal.); T19.07.c (Compare pull and push iteration under bounded-storage requirements.).

## Failure cases

Unknown events and stale iterators must not index tables or access invalid elements. A callback cannot silently mutate during a traversal that forbids it. End state is distinct from an error, and early stop is not treated as failure.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit transition equivalence, traversal order/stop checks, stale-state tests and a dispatch decision. Record temporary bytes and whether any callbacks retain data. Explain why dynamic strategy is justified or deliberately avoided.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Keep the core transition function deterministic. Use an explicit next-result enum instead of overloading a value sentinel.

# PR-T19-04 — Composable short-write stream and stable handles

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T19](#t19).

**Covered topics:** [T19.08](#t19-08), [T19.09](#t19-09), [T19.10](#t19-10).

## Contract

Compose a bounded framing/checksum layer with a transport that accepts short writes and can apply backpressure. Retain pending bytes in caller storage and expose partial progress. Use generation-counted slots for request identity, with an exhaustion policy, and compare direct versus table-dispatched transport costs under identical contracts.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 12 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture payload [1,2,3] uses an additive modulo-256 checksum and a one-byte length prefix, yielding frame [3,1,2,3,6]. Transport quotas [2,1,2] produce chunks [3,1], [2], [3,6] with no pending bytes. No actual OS transport behavior is assumed.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T19-04.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Define ownership at each layer and progress/error results. Implement a short-write adapter and retry only unconsumed bytes. Add backpressure, terminal failure and stale-generation tests. Analyze a reference-count cycle as an alternative, including count overflow. Inspect object code and measure dispatch/size/resource differences with documented workloads.

- **T19.08:** Compose a bounded frame/checksum writer with a short-write transport adapter. Retain progress traces, exact reconstructed bytes and backpressure/ownership checks. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T19.08.a (Define read/write contracts including partial progress and errors.); T19.08.b (Compose buffering, framing, checksumming, and transport adapters.); T19.08.c (Preserve backpressure and ownership across abstraction boundaries.).

- **T19.09:** Implement generation-counted fixed slots and analyze a reference-counted cycle as an alternative. Retain stale/overflow/reuse tests and separate lifetime versus access-safety claims. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T19.09.a (Implement reference counting or generation-counted handles with explicit limits.); T19.09.b (Analyze cycles, overflow, stale access, and reclamation.); T19.09.c (Separate shared ownership from concurrent access safety.).

- **T19.10:** Compare direct and table-dispatched versions with identical contracts and workloads. Retain size/code/resource ledger, repeated measurements and a bounded decision record. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T19.10.a (Inspect generated code for each dispatch and representation strategy.); T19.10.b (Measure size, allocations, branches, and cache access where relevant.); T19.10.c (Remove abstraction only when evidence and maintainability justify the change.).

## Failure cases

A zero-progress backpressure result must not busy-loop without a policy. Prevent duplicate completion and stale-slot access. Do not treat reference counting as synchronization or allow generation wrap to revive old requests. Failure preserves a valid pending-state invariant.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit reconstructed frame bytes, progress traces, handle invalidation/exhaustion checks and cost evidence. Explain which effects are in the harness, which in the component and which callbacks could invalidate the dependency promise.

Track a consumed offset rather than resending the full frame. Keep checksum computation separate from transport progress.

# PR-T21-01 — Error translation and failure-complete construction

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T21](#t21).

**Covered topics:** [T21.01](#t21-01), [T21.02](#t21-02), [T21.03](#t21-03), [T21.04](#t21-04).

## Contract

Implement a small constructor that acquires three resources through injectable adapters, maps backend failures to stable public errors and rolls back exactly once. Compare early-return/nested cleanup with a narrowly scoped cleanup-label version. Record original cause independently of public classification.

The declared profile **A** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 10 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture resources are memory, channel and registration; acquisition fails at index 2 before registration is acquired. Expected acquired sequence is [memory,channel], release order [channel,memory] and no live resources. Every other failure index and full success become learner tests.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T21-01.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Define error taxonomy/recovery actions. Write acquisition ownership states, implement stage tracking and translation, then inject each failure. Compare two cleanup structures against the same tests. Add repeated init/stop under a documented lifecycle policy and preserve the first cause through cleanup errors.

- **T21.01:** Define an error table for parser, allocator and transport failures with recovery class and context. Retain error/class/action matrix and tests for at least one outcome in each category. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T21.01.a (Separate invalid input, contract violations, resource failures, and hardware faults.); T21.01.b (Define recoverable, retryable, terminal, and degraded outcomes.); T21.01.c (Preserve enough context to identify the original cause.).

- **T21.02:** Implement a bounded error record and backend-to-public mapping with an explicit unknown-error policy. Retain mapping tests, stable public codes and original-cause preservation across propagation. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T21.02.a (Map backend errors into stable component-level results.); T21.02.b (Retain causal context without exposing unstable implementation details.); T21.02.c (Avoid silent information loss and ambiguous success codes.).

- **T21.03:** Inject failure after each of three acquisitions and check remaining ownership after rollback. Retain acquisition/rollback traces and repeated-init/cleanup tests. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T21.03.a (Track resource acquisition order and completed initialization stages.); T21.03.b (Roll back safely after every possible failure point.); T21.03.c (Test repeated initialization and cleanup under injected failures.).

- **T21.04:** Implement the same small acquisition sequence with two cleanup structures and compare reviewability. Retain exactly-once release proof, failure-point tests and a justified style choice. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T21.04.a (Compare early returns, nested cleanup, and narrowly scoped cleanup labels.); T21.04.b (Establish exactly-once release for each acquired resource.); T21.04.c (Choose structure by correctness and readability rather than blanket style rules.).

## Failure cases

A cleanup error must not erase the original construction failure. Release only acquired resources and do not publish an active object on partial construction. Unknown backend codes map deliberately, while internal contract violations remain distinguishable from expected exhaustion.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit all failure-point traces, public/backend mapping, release counts and a cleanup-style decision. Test repeated cleanup and show stable consumer errors without exposing volatile backend details as the public ABI.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Treat the acquisition list as a stack of obligations. Keep constructor success publication after all required acquisitions.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

# PR-T21-02 — Transactional update and cancellation ownership

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T21](#t21).

**Covered topics:** [T21.05](#t21-05), [T21.06](#t21-06).

## Contract

Implement a caller-storage transactional update and a small asynchronous-operation state model with timeout/cancellation. The update promises unchanged observable state on validation/capacity failure. The operation model has explicit request identity, in-flight ownership and exactly one completion result; timeout alone never authorizes context reclamation.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Budget 10 h for implementation and verification together. Start from your own sources and the listed fixtures, with prior modules as prerequisites; no starter repository or solved program is required.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture initial configuration [1,2] proposes [3,4,5] into capacity 2, so update is rejected and state stays [1,2]. Events start, timeout, cancel_ack, late_complete produce one cancelled completion and a stale late event. This synthetic acknowledgment ordering is the declared model.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T21-02.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Steps

Separate validation/staging/commit and compare strong/basic guarantees in the dossier. Implement idempotent request handling where promised. Draw timeout/cancel/completion states and test late, duplicate and reordered events. Keep retained context alive until the ownership protocol ends.

- **T21.05:** Implement a staged configuration update and compare strong/basic failure contracts. Retain before/after snapshots, commit-point proof and repeated-request checks. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T21.05.a (Define strong, basic, and explicitly weaker failure guarantees.); T21.05.b (Stage changes before committing externally visible state.); T21.05.c (Verify rollback and idempotent retries where promised.).

- **T21.06:** Model timeout, cancel request, late callback and cancel acknowledgment, rejecting stale/duplicate completion. Retain ownership/timing traces, exactly-once completion and no stale-context access. For its three original objectives, record separate evidence references: T21.06.a (Distinguish timeout expiry from successful cancellation.); T21.06.b (Specify ownership of operations still in flight.); T21.06.c (Prevent stale callbacks and duplicate completion reporting.).

## Failure cases

Capacity failure must not partially install a configuration. Cancel request can fail or remain pending under a declared policy. Reject stale callback identity and prevent duplicate completion; do not confuse a deadline result with backend cancellation acknowledgment.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit snapshots, commit proof, repeated-update tests and event/ownership traces. Explain which orderings are permitted and how terminal state handles later events. Audit callbacks and compiler helpers for the C boundary.

Record contract, build/dependency evidence, independent cases, minimized failures and the specific evidence file for every linked objective. A passing synthetic oracle does not establish a passing implementation. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for the review gate.

## Hints and recovery

Use a separate proposed state until commit and an explicit in-flight token until acknowledgment/completion. Test every terminal transition twice.

If stuck, separate the violated contract from the observed symptom and reduce the input before changing the implementation. Revisit the linked teaching section and retain the minimized case after repair.

## Contract

Implement a bounded fault-record encoder/decoder with format version, build identity, operation/state fields and a simple declared checksum. Reject corruption and incompatible format/build identity before using diagnostic fields. Define collection storage assumptions separately from a recovery procedure, which must reinitialize and validate state under the selected fault model.

The declared profile **C** applies to the boundary named here; specify harness versus component dependencies in [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). ## Inputs and expected results

The fixture record bytes [1,4,9,2] use additive modulo-256 checksum 16. The supplied checksum 16 is accepted; 17 is rejected. Expected build identity is 4, so a record identity 5 is stale. The checksum detects these specified corruptions, not every possible corruption.

The canonical fixture is `fixtures/language/PR-T21-04.json`. Preserve its supplied fields and add independent cases in your dossier. Run `python tools/verify_language_fixtures.py` from the curriculum root to verify the fixture oracle; then test your C component separately.

## Failure cases

Never treat a checksum as cryptographic integrity or a complete corruption detector. Do not symbolize with mismatched debug artifacts. Persistent-storage atomicity needs actual platform evidence at the later hardware integration, while the current byte model remains synthetic.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit exact codec vectors, corruption/version/build rejection and a recovery test plan/result for the declared environment. Explain what the record can diagnose and what it cannot prove about safe continuation.

# PR-T25-01 — Thread-owned work and join obligations

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T25](#t25).

**Covered topics:** [T25.01](#t25-01), [T25.02](#t25-02).

## Contract

Implement one partitioned worker example with explicit immutable inputs, thread-owned results and transferred work items using the selected POSIX interface. Every joinable thread has one join owner; detached use is an analysis alternative unless its object-lifetime protocol is complete. Forced creation failures release all acquired resources. Add a bounded interface comparison against the inspected C thread clauses: thrd_t versus pthread_t, int-returning versus pointer-returning start functions, creation status, join output and optional C17 thread support versus POSIX environment support. Produce signature/status/lifetime mappings and compile-only availability probes; do not build a second worker implementation or cast handles/start functions between families. Mark an unavailable C thread header/library as unavailable rather than a POSIX or C17 language failure.

Interface mapping for the selected C17 lesson: C thread facilities are optional; record __STDC_NO_THREADS__ and actual header/library support separately from POSIX availability. The inspected N3096 text is a later-draft cross-check, not an exact C17 edition. C uses thrd_t, thrd_create(thrd_t*, int (*)(void*), void*) and thrd_join(thrd_t, int*): the start returns an int, creation returns thrd_success/thrd_nomem/thrd_error and joining reports the integer result. POSIX uses pthread_t, pthread_create(pthread_t*, const pthread_attr_t*, void* (*)(void*), void*) and pthread_join(pthread_t, void**): null attributes request defaults, the start returns a pointer, and creation/join return zero or an error number directly. Keep the result pointee live independently; do not diagnose a nonzero pthread result by assuming errno contains it. Neither family supplies a portable representation cast to the other. Never mix their creation/start/join contracts, and do not join a detached or already-joined thread. PR-T25-01 implements one POSIX worker and supplies this comparison plus availability probes, rather than two worker implementations.

Load [fixtures/systems/PR-T25-01.json](fixtures/systems/PR-T25-01.json). # PR-T26-03 — Kernel ordering and lifetime boundary

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | awareness | C |

**Teaching module:** [T26](#t26).

**Covered topics:** [T26.09](#t26-09), [T26.10](#t26-10).

## Contract

Core awareness: compare portable C graphs with inspected LKMM relations and write an isolated version-matched kernel experiment dossier. Use the inspected Linux 6.12 ordinary-work cancel_work_sync contract to draw references from an external producer and queued/running work to module text and its device object. In the declared narrow model, stop and join all producers so racing enqueues are impossible, invoke synchronous cancellation from a permitted sleepable context without a lock needed by the worker, and release the object only after drain. An smp_mb event alone changes neither pending/running work nor reference ownership. Analyze user-pointer access and nonsleepable-context restrictions separately. No kernel module must be loaded to pass. The fixture certifies only this declared ordinary-work lifetime graph; timers, IRQ handlers, RCU callbacks, delayed work, registrations and other module references are excluded and require newly inspected complete contracts before any actual unload claim.

Worked kernel lifetime graph: external producer -> module_text; queued/running work -> module_text and device_object. With one queued and one running instance in the declared model, smp_mb preserves all these lifetime edges. An unload attempt therefore fails the model gate. Stop and wait for every producer first, then let cancel_work_sync return under its no-racing-enqueue and permitted-context preconditions. Only then are pending/running work zero; release the object and consider code removal eligible within this narrow graph. That eligibility is not a real-module verdict: any IRQ, timer, RCU, delayed work or other registration adds a distinct obligation outside this fixture.

- Challenge the mistaken claim: Adding CAS to an SPSC head creates a complete MPMC design. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.
- Challenge the mistaken claim: Equal pointer bits prove the same live object remained there. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.
- Challenge the mistaken claim: Publishing a pointer once is enough to make arbitrary reclamation safe. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.
- Challenge the mistaken claim: Elapsed wall-clock time alone completes a grace period. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.
- Challenge the mistaken claim: Completing a publication store immediately permits freeing the old object. Preserve a minimal failing trace or explain the valid precondition that excludes it.

Exercise empty/singleton or zero-progress states where the operation admits them, exact capacity, one beyond capacity, repeated completion/cleanup and a deliberately invalid precondition. For storage-owning work, inject acquisition failures and verify unchanged old ownership. For build/binary/source studies, inject a wrong edge, symbol, width, target assumption or unsupported environment and require a visible failure verdict. Never execute malformed pointers or privileged instructions just to demonstrate a negative case. Apply these cases to the declared operation; document any inapplicable case and its reason.

# PR-T35-02 — Descriptor authority and permitted-effect worker

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |

| 8 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T35](#t35).

**Covered topics:** [T35.05](#t35-05), [T35.08](#t35-08).

## Contract

Implement a nonprivileged Linux parent and worker with explicit argument vectors, controlled descriptor inheritance and a private test directory. Pass an O_RDONLY descriptor for a disposable log to the worker; reads must succeed and write through that same descriptor must fail with EBADF. Separately deny write-config in the application capability policy. This is a narrow enforced descriptor property: the worker retains its ordinary user filesystem authority and may be able to reopen a path writable by that user.

Use dependency profile A under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles). Implement the studied mechanism yourself; a mature library may be a separately declared hosted oracle. This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification, with reading/assessment budgeted in the module.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture `fixtures/embedded/PR-T35-02.json` contains concrete inputs and exact expected fields; use the supplied-fixture download below in the local handbook. FDs 0 and 4 lack close-on-exec and are inherited; FD 3 is closed at successful exec. A declared read-log capability allows read-log but denies write-config.

Filter declared close-on-exec flags/capability membership independently. It models policy; actual OS enforcement requires process/descriptor observations.

## Steps

Create disposable files in a private test directory without changing system-wide permissions. Open the log O_RDONLY, arrange only declared descriptors for exec, and report inherited descriptors. In the worker, read the expected log bytes, attempt write on the inherited descriptor and record -1/EBADF plus unchanged file bytes. Run authorized read-log and denied write-config requests and confirm denied requests create no effects. Test exclusive temporary creation and a competing name. Record whether reopening the path is permitted by the current user; explain that CLOEXEC and a private directory do not remove ambient authority. Compare this narrow process boundary with a separately verified MPU design at awareness depth.

First write the public interface, storage/effect limits and expected failure state. Derive at least one supplied value by hand before coding. Implement one normal path, then add each boundary/failure path. Run the independent fixture oracle and your own implementation checks separately; preserve versions, commands, binary identity and raw observations.

## Failure cases

Unexpected inherited descriptors, successful write through the read-only descriptor, denied application requests with effects, stale competing names, partial spawn cleanup and shell interpretation fail the contract.
