# PR-T36-03 — Tagged stable insertion in assembly

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T36](#t36).

**Covered topics:** [T36.05](#t36-05).

## Contract

Write an original bounded insertion kernel in one of the two already exercised assembly ISAs for actual typed records `{uint32_t key; uint32_t tag;}`; n≤32. Sort by unsigned key and preserve initial order of equal tags. Reuse the completed T15 insertion/merge/heap sort artifacts as differential subjects, without reimplementing those full algorithms. Supply prefix-state and comparison/write counters in a separate instrumentation build.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-03.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Tags A..E denote distinct numeric tags in the target harness. Fixture `(3,A),(1,B),(3,C),(2,D),(1,E)` gives B, E, D, A, C, six shift writes, four final placements and nine key comparisons. The merge checkpoint takes left ties before right ties. Sorted/reverse five-key inputs use four/ten comparisons with the declared final-placement convention. Heap-sort evidence is ordering/permutation only, since its prior policy is unstable.

## Steps

Define the pending record, sorted prefix and multiset including the pending value before moving anything. Implement only the bounded kernel, annotate record stride and register pressure, then disassemble/execute it. Emit prefix certificates for the fixture and an equal-key family. Compare each complete result with stable prior C insertion/merge; compare heap sort without requiring tie stability. Count exact moves independently from inversion numbers. Retain build/source provenance so instrumentation and performance versions are distinguishable.

## Failure cases

Test n 0/n 1/32, all equal, largest unsigned keys, capacity 31 for 32 records in the checked API, and a `≥` shift mutation. Whole-record moves must keep key/tag pairs intact. Failure returns before any writes; stable but corrupted multiplicities and sorted but reversed tags both fail acceptance.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .05a submit insertion and merge-prefix reasoning with tag/multiset checks; .05b actual authored assembly, execution and identified prior full-sort reuse; .05c comparison/shift/placement counts for sorted, reverse and duplicate-rich families, with timing in a separate column. Callee-save/sentinel and dependency audits pass as in PR-T36-02. Do not claim a speedup from fewer comparisons alone.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Preserve the pending whole record across shifts. A tie must stop insertion and choose the left head in merge for this policy. Count comparisons at the stopping predecessor, but not a nonexistent predecessor when insertion reaches index 0. If counts differ by one, replay that boundary before altering the algorithm.

## Transfer challenge

Add a descending comparator policy only in a separate interface experiment. Predict which tie rules stay the same and compare observable tag stability.

## Contract

Replace only the sift-down kernel in the completed PR-T14-05 max heap with original assembly in one ISA. Keep its capacity, key multiplicity and API intact; no new heap/container implementation. Kernel precondition: all edges obey heap order except possibly those from the selected p, and both child subtrees are heaps. Equal child keys choose the left child; stop when parent≥selected child. n≤1024 and p<n, with a separate empty-heap no-op wrapper.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-04.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

## Inputs and expected results

Fixture root replacement `[5,7,8,3,6,2]` follows 0→2 and ends `[8,7,5,3,6,2]`, three comparisons and one swap. A two-level violation follows 0→1→3, four comparisons and two swaps. `[5,5,4]` makes two comparisons and no swap. Counts include sibling and parent comparisons; no-child terminal contributes zero.

## Steps

Freeze the prior heap and swap in a single function boundary. Derive child-index arithmetic under the length bound and draw the moving invariant. Implement/execute the kernel with callee-save and sentinels. Emit snapshots only after complete swaps; independently check intact edges, multiplicities and final order. Reuse prior build/insert/extract tests, adding one-child, equal-child and maximum-length cases. Compute the visited-level height bound separately from measured work.

## Failure cases

Reject p outside the live heap, incorrect n/backing capacity and malformed preconditions through the diagnostic wrapper. Include a right-child-out-of-range mutation, reversed child choice, dropped duplicate and integer child-index wrap reasoning. Reject before mutation where validation applies; the trusted internal kernel requires its documented precondition.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .06a give local precondition and state-path derivation; .06b source/disassembly/execution showing only the kernel replacement and preserved API/tie policy; .06c per-swap independent heap/multiplicity certificates and height/work ledger. Prior full heap acceptance remains referenced. The public oracle validates these narrow certificates, not a provided full C heap.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

The violation moves with the displaced old parent. Check child existence before comparing its value; for a leaf there is no comparison. A valid final maximum is not enough: every retained key count must match the original. Repair the smallest one-child case before a large random heap.

Use the same certificate format for a min heap without changing the original max-heap artifact. Identify which predicates reverse and which ownership/bounds facts remain.

Emit stable node IDs, keys, children, parents and cached heights after each complete mutation; null height 0. Build an independent checker that recomputes metadata from reachability rather than trusting the cached heights. Intermediate rotation snapshots are explicitly marked possibly unbalanced.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. ## Inputs and expected results

The LR fixture 30, 10, 20 ends root 20 with inorder 10, 20, 30 and height 2. Deleting 1 from root 2/left 1/right 4(children 3, 5) ends root 4 with inorder 2, 3, 4, 5 and height 3. Duplicate 20 returns reject/unchanged. A balanced 1, 2, 3 search for 3 takes two key comparisons; the right chain takes three.

## Steps

Freeze prior source, add read-only certificate emission, then derive both rotations by partitioning subtrees. Recompute each node height bottom-up and check parent edges and single reachability. Checker rejects duplicate keys, cycles/shared children, unreachable nodes, wrong parent/root, stale heights and unacceptable final balance. The simple supplied deletion does not waive the multiple-ancestor path evidence.

Fix child links first, then heights from the lowest changed node upward. In LR, the middle key becomes the subtree root. Equal inorder output can conceal shared/cyclic links; compare reachable IDs before heights. If deletion fails only near the root, inspect where the recorded ancestor walk stopped.

Explain how a red-black policy certificate would differ using the already inspected CLRS properties; do not build another full balanced tree in this budget.

Reuse the prior full table and T15 prefix matcher/preprocessing. For this milestone capacity 8 uses h(k)=k mod 8 and linear steps; lookup visits at most capacity slots, stops at empty, continues past deleted and never mutates. Matcher reports all overlapping offsets; empty pattern matches all n+1 boundaries.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T36-06.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

## Inputs and expected results

Key 22 visits 6, 7, 0, 1, 2, 3 and is absent; key 16 hits 0; key 2 hits 2. An absent key in a full eight-slot table returns absent after 8 probes. Byte text 0, 97, 0, 97, 0 with patterns 97, 0 and 0, 97, 0 reports 1, 3 and 0, 2 with six/seven naive comparisons. Empty pattern reports 0..5 without comparisons. Numeric zero is data.

## Steps

Annotate slot layout and stop states from the prior representation; do not cast an unrelated byte array into it. Assemble/disassemble/execute lookup and record visits. Define span lengths, output-capacity preflight and overlap policy before writing the bounded matcher. Compare outputs with the reused prefix matcher and independent slice enumeration. Replay tombstones, wraparound, full-table absence and embedded-zero cases; record probe/comparison counts beside correctness.

## Failure cases

Reject invalid slot states/capacity in a checked wrapper. Test all-deleted tables, zero capacity, pattern longer than text, empty text/pattern, output capacity one short and a tombstone-stop mutation. On output-capacity failure return required count/status and preserve the output buffer; preflight by a read-only count pass or a declared transactional strategy. No strlen/strstr/memcmp delegation.

For .08a submit reachability argument, bounded termination and expected-bound assumptions; .08b actual assembly and small original C output API, with prior table/prefix work explicitly reused; .08c independent visit/byte counts and each wrap/full/deleted/zero boundary. # PR-T37-04 — Forwarding, stalls and branch squash schedule

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.06](#t37-06).

## Contract

Build a small original stage-schedule model/checker for declared IF/ID/EX/MEM/WB, single issue, in order. ALU result is available after EX; load after MEM; forwarded values enter next-cycle EX; register-file writes occur before reads in a cycle. A taken branch resolves at EX end, squashes younger IF/ID and refetches target next cycle. Do not label this a physical Cortex-M4/x86 pipeline.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-04.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Fixture I1/I2 dependent ALU, I3 load, I4 load consumer, I5 taken branch, I6 wrong-path work, I7 target retires I1, I2, I3, I4, I5, I7 by cycle 13. I3 MEM 6 requires I4 EX 7. Two younger fetch instances are squashed at 8; target refetch is 9. First four instructions retire by 9 with forwarding/one bubble, versus 14 without forwarding under write-first/read-second register-file order.

## Steps

Draw the stage-by-cycle table and attach a producer availability to every read. Build a bounded scheduler or independent certificate checker, then run the same original stream with/without forwarding. Keep blocked IF/ID slots distinct from empty EX bubbles. On the branch, show which fetched instances are discarded and which instruction identity is later refetched. Count retired instructions separately from fetched/issued instances. Include a parallel explanation of RAW dependence, implementation hazard and C data race.

## Failure cases

Reject a consumer EX before its value is available, duplicate occupancy of a single stage/cycle, advancing a blocked younger instruction, retired squashed work and unsupported branch rules. Include same-cycle MEM 6→EX 6 mutation. Do not count a stalled instruction twice or add a bubble penalty already visible in the schedule.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .06a submit complete RAW/load-use stage table; .06b forwarding/no-forwarding and branch effects with cycle/retirement counts; .06c distinguish dependence/hazard/race with examples and state physical extrapolation limits. The independent oracle validates declared certificates, not an exported commercial CPU simulator. Functional final register equivalence alone does not validate cycle accounting.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

Write the producer’s availability edge first. With no forwarding, a following dependent EX waits until the cycle after producer WB; with load forwarding it still waits after MEM. Label I7’s wrong fetch separately from its eventual correct fetch to avoid accidental double retirement.

## Transfer challenge

Move branch resolution to ID under a separately specified model and predict the flush count. State any new operand-availability rule before rerunning.

# PR-T37-05 — Cache tags, miss mechanisms and dimensional costs

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.07](#t37-07).

## Contract

Implement an original bounded trace model for a four-line direct-mapped cache with 16 byte blocks and byte addresses. Add an independent same-capacity fully associative LRU shadow for three-C classification. Keep valid bits/tag identity explicit; no actual memory loads are needed to model a reference. Compute AMAT and a separate declared in-order stall estimate with consistent units.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-05.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Trace 0, 16, 0, 64, 0, 16, 80, 16, 0 yields six misses: four compulsory, two conflict, zero capacity. Trace 0, 16, 32, 48, 64, 0 ends with a capacity miss. Hit 1 ns/additional penalty 30 ns gives AMAT 21 ns for the first trace. Declared 100 instructions, CPI 1.2, 24 references, rate 0.25, penalty 20 cycles gives 240 cycles total and 120 ns at 2 GHz.

## Steps

Derive offset/index/tag partitions before coding. Emit cache and shadow state after every reference and explain each category using seen blocks and shadow membership. Design two small original layouts/access orders and compare their normalized address traces under exactly the same geometry. Compute dimensional equations independently from trace hit counting. If optionally measuring host behavior, identify CPU/tool/counters and put observations in a separate column; do not tune fixture geometry to claim the host matches it.

## Failure cases

Reject negative/invalid addresses or zero/non-power-of-two geometry in the general wrapper. Include cold start, repeated hits, two conflicting blocks, more than four distinct blocks and an invalid uninitialized-tag mutation. Miss penalty is additional to hit cost under this contract; a total-miss-latency input must be converted explicitly.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .07a submit fields and state/hit trace; .07b AMAT/stall equations and two-layout comparison with units; .07c compulsory/conflict/capacity reasoning and model-versus-measurement boundary. Shadow replacement and capacity are recorded. Correct miss totals with incorrect tags/categories fail acceptance.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

A repeated block can miss by conflict while the equal-capacity shadow still holds it. The three-C category is evaluated against shadow state before servicing that reference. Normalize addresses to declared blocks; do not confuse array element count with byte offset. Check cycles/seconds conversion before interpreting a large time.

## Transfer challenge

Change associativity to two-way with an explicit replacement rule. Predict which conflict cases disappear and which capacity limitation remains.

# PR-T37-08 — Work, cycles and repeated native measurements

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T37](#t37).

**Covered topics:** [T37.10](#t37-10).

## Contract

Build a bounded experiment comparing one reused C kernel and its original T36 assembly counterpart with identical valid outputs and input family. First derive CPU-time/Amdahl equations and process the explicitly synthetic fixture. Then collect at least 31 raw native measurements per condition; this new budget covers the experiment, not kernel construction. Keep the Profile C component separate from a Profile A timing/reporting harness.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. Reading, assessment and delayed consolidation belong to the module budget. The concrete original fixture is `fixtures/algorithms/PR-T37-08.json`; run `tools/verify_algorithms_fixtures.py` for its independent narrow oracle, then run your own component checks separately.

Declare the Profile C component boundary and Profile A hosted harness under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles); audit object and final symbols, generated code and callback effects. Implement the studied mechanism yourself. Existing base work is reused with its original acceptance evidence; this budget covers only the new work described here.

## Inputs and expected results

Original equation inputs 1.2 million instructions, CPI 1.5, 2 GHz give 0.9 ms. Accelerating 60% threefold gives 0.54 ms, speedup 5/3, limit 2.5. Synthetic sample medians 100/95 ns give ratio 20/19; ranges 96..110 and 93..120 include outliers. These samples demonstrate reporting only and must not be presented as measured hardware performance.

## Steps

Verify every timed result/checksum outside the timing region. Record exact source/binary, CPU/ABI/compiler/options, input sizes/order, clock resolution/overhead and warm/cold policy. Alternate condition order, retain all raw samples and record migration/frequency/interrupt controls or their absence. Report median/range and original operation counts; explain whether timer granularity or setup dominates. Compare the same outputs with the declared equations but do not force measured timings to equal an assumed CPI. Thumb emulator runs may provide ISA correctness only; use Linux x86 native execution for required measurements if no physical MCU is available.

## Failure cases

Reject mismatched outputs, optimized-away work, uncontrolled changing inputs, unit confusion, dropped outliers and an unsupported energy/WCET conclusion. A timer interval below its usable resolution is inconclusive; enlarge repetitions within a batch with correctness retained and disclose the normalization. Do not blindly subtract overhead to produce negative times.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .10a submit dimensionally checked equations and Amdahl derivation; .10b reproducible native experiment, identical results and at least 31 samples/condition; .10c raw distribution/confounders, work-versus-time table and explicit limits. No speedup threshold is required; a slower correct assembly kernel can satisfy the project with a sound explanation.

Keep the evidence items separate for each linked topic's three objectives. Retain the actual input/output replay, build identity, dependency/storage ledger, first counterexample and limits. Deterministic synthetic expectations do not substitute for required executable or device observations.

## Hints and recovery

The improved fraction is a fraction of baseline elapsed work, not source lines. Average CPI already aggregates the measured instruction mix. Keep raw timings even if a median is convenient. If measurements wobble, first check order/cache/clock granularity before rewriting assembly.

## Transfer challenge

Repeat one input family at a different size and predict whether algorithmic work or fixed overhead dominates. Treat any trend as conditional evidence rather than a universal performance ranking.

# PR-T38-01 — UART architecture, frame and baud laboratory

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.01](#t38-01), [T38.02](#t38-02).

## Contract

Reuse the T27 reset/linker and T28 UART adapter. Write an allocation-free character/baud analyzer and a bounded 8N1 target exchange, maximum 16 bytes per request and 32 bytes of RX caller storage. Add 7E1/8E1 to the software frame model; do not silently reuse an 8-bit-with-parity configuration. Results separate byte, parity/framing error, overrun, busy and deadline. Draw the CPU/MMIO/peripheral/transceiver/wire path and document which tested component owns each responsibility.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

PR-T38-01 supplies 42 MHz/115200 baud under both oversampling choices, a 3 Mbaud validity contrast,0xA5 and 0x35 frame patterns, parity/stop corruption and TXE-versus-TC completion observations. The exact rational baud/error fields are the arithmetic oracle; approximate decimal printing is supplementary. The 8N1 0xA5 frame has 10 bits. BRR is 0x16D under OVER8=0 and 0x2D5 under OVER8=1 for the declared clock.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-01.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Derive all frame positions and both BRR encodings before programming. Validate divisor and word-length ranges.
2. Implement an explicit byte/error result and bounded wait policy; preserve SR-before-DR status evidence for the chosen F439 receive errors.
3. Replay software fixtures and a synthetic RX-overrun prefix. Keep the older held RDR value distinct from lost later input.
4. Connect only the exact documented board UART routing/logic peer, transmit 16 or fewer known bytes and measure bit/stop timing. Use the existing startup and pin ledger.
5. Audit the profile E image and supply the three architecture receipts: host arithmetic, target operation and physical trace.

## Failure cases

Reject divisor range, unsupported data/parity settings and capacity overflow without publishing partial successful records. A TXE-only release is premature. Record FE/ORE as errors; a baud timeout must not fabricate a received zero byte. A wrong peripheral-clock assumption is a calculation failure even when the peer happens to tolerate it.

## Acceptance and evidence

All fixture bits/encodings/rational values match. Show one actual clock derivation and measured baud discrepancy, final TC after the last stop interval, and exact receive-error handling. Provide separate per-objective evidence for both linked topics. Physical timing is closed only by the captured board/peer route; the software receipt alone is a partial hardware route.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Use unsigned shifts with explicit widths. Compute nearest effective divisor first, then encode its mantissa/fraction for the chosen oversampling. Reduce a parity disagreement to one character; reduce a timeout to clock, pin, status sequence and deadline evidence.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Change the selected peripheral clock while preserving the character contract; recompute BRR and invalidate stale configuration before the next transfer.

## Contract

Implement the eight-data-bit synchronous-master trace model and one bounded matched CK/TX/RX exchange, at most 8 characters, LBCL enabled for the physical baseline. Reuse the asynchronous USART adapter, but add explicit clock/data configuration and TE/RE-off reconfiguration. Reception must include a declared clock-generating transmit value; no autonomous synchronous receive API is permitted.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture supplies 0x96 under all four CPOL/CPHA combinations, LBCL-on/off contrasts, a clockless receive request and an attempted change with TE active. Data bits are LSB-first. With LBCL on there are 16 data-clock edges and no start/stop clock edges; CPHA selects odd/even capture edges. The fixture does not assert that an LBCL-off trace is compatible with an arbitrary peer.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-02.json`. 2. Implement the predictor and a configuration validator rejecting changes while TE or RE is enabled.
3. Extend the bounded adapter with transmit-generated clocks and a maximum transfer count/deadline.
4. Use a matched documented peer or declared logic-level receive loopback; capture CK/TX/RX for the LBCL-on baseline. Compare asynchronous and synchronous timing.
5. Replay clockless and live-change failures synthetically; retain peer setup/hold limitations.

## Failure cases

No TX means no receive clock. Mismatched CPHA/CPOL, incompatible last-clock policy and live configuration changes are explicit errors or unclosed peer compatibility. Do not assume USART character/start/stop conventions satisfy a generic SPI target.

## Acceptance and evidence

Correct edge numbers, idle levels, bit order and last-clock policy; no falsely completed clockless receive; one matched bounded physical transfer with source-verified pins. Demonstrate all configuration preconditions and profile E image dependencies.

# PR-T38-03 — I2C pull-up and wired-AND investigation

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.04](#t38-04).

## Contract

Write a caller-storage calculator and at-most 3-controller wired-AND trace model. Inputs are positive bounded integer mV/mA/ns/pF and up to 32 data bits. Use checked 64-bit intermediates or a proved bounded equivalent, integer ceil/floor resistor limits and explicit infeasible status. The physical baseline is a short Standard/Fast-mode bus with known target voltage/sink limits and measured capacitance assumptions; unsupported high-speed modes are excluded.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture uses 3.3 V, VOL0.4 V,3 mA,300 ns,100 pF with 2.2 kΩ/4.7 kΩ choices, then 400 pF. Expected interval is 967..3540 Ω for 100 pF and infeasible for 400 pF. Two streams 101100/101010 lose participation at their first differing dominant bit; identical streams both survive. Common low/high holds are max(4,7)=7 and min(6,3)=3 ticks.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-03.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Derive Rp bounds with units and rounding direction; state uncertainty and check products/divisors.
2. Implement the calculator, rejecting empty intervals rather than picking an arbitrary resistor.
3. Implement release-high/pull-low participants, loss logging and wired-AND clock periods. Do not force a losing controller STOP.
4. Measure SDA/SCL low level and rise time on the declared prepared setup, compare scope and decoder views, and label any unknown capacitance estimate.
5. Audit the profile C component object and retain target adaptation separately under E.

## Failure cases

Zero or negative denominators, out-of-envelope inputs, arithmetic overflow, empty resistor interval and non-binary traces fail explicitly. A low pulse on SDA while SCL high is not ordinary data. A push-pull SCL design is rejected unless the inspected single-controller/no-stretch exception is actually declared.

## Acceptance and evidence

All resistor/trace results match the independent exact rational oracle. Show simultaneous identical-prefix arbitration, measured analog levels/rise time and a justified chosen resistor. Logic decoding alone leaves the electrical receipt open.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Keep a unit table:0.8473×Ω×pF/1000 gives ns. Never round the minimum downward or maximum upward. Inspect the first lost participant instead of comparing only decoded addresses.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Increase estimated capacitance and identify the threshold where the pull-up interval becomes empty; propose a justified change to rate/load rather than guessing a resistor.

## Steps

3. Add line observation and the conditional bus-clear action; do not generate clocks when SCL is held low.

# PR-T38-05 — SPI four-mode transaction and ownership laboratory

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |

## Contract

Implement a checked full-duplex eight-bit MSB-first transfer service, maximum 16 bytes, caller-owned TX/RX buffers, one active transaction and explicit timeout/cancel-pending outcomes. Reuse the T28 register adapter and prior ring/ownership abstractions. The selected external target contributes a documented mode/clock/select/dummy-byte contract; the fixture is an original scripted peer, not a claimed sensor command specification.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

0xA6 TX/0x3C RX is traced in all four CPOL/CPHA modes with 16 numbered edges per byte. Final cases include correct drained completion, one missing received byte, BSY still set and cancellation before DMA is confirmed stopped. Mode 0/2 sample odd edges and mode 1/3 even edges.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-05.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw MOSI/MISO and capture/change edges independently for all modes.
2. Define transfer parameters, lengths, buffer lifetime, status and callback reentry restrictions; reject invalid requests before touching select.
3. Implement one polling path: TXE write, RXNE consume and final TXE/BSY completion. Reuse prior DMA sequencing only for a declared adapter with stop confirmation.
4. Replay timeout, undrained receive and cancelled-in-flight traces; buffer ownership remains with the adapter until completion/confirmed stop.
5. Capture one bounded matched-target transaction, including select setup/hold and final clock. Audit object and image dependencies under the declared E boundary.

## Failure cases

Null/capacity/length/mode rejection, receive overrun, wrong target select policy, BSY timeout, early deselection and buffer reuse while DMA remains active. A request with no meaningful receive payload still needs receive draining. Never change configuration while the selected peripheral transfer is active.

## Acceptance and evidence

Every fixture edge/bit and release decision matches; no solved sensor driver is required. Submit transaction API, per-byte/final trace, resource ledger, cancellation proof and one external capture. Identify which physical target requirements are outside generic SPI.

## Contract

Reuse the bounded 8N1 UART service to send at most 16 known bytes through a specifically documented 3.3-V MAX3232 circuit and an RS-232 peer or loopback adapter. Use a modest declared rate within guaranteed part/load conditions. Implement a polarity/connection checker, but do not supply an arbitrary generic DB9 pinout: derive the exact selected adapter table with DTE/DCE directions and reference.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture maps logic 1/0 to synthetic−6/+6 V, interprets line samples at/over±3 V and leaves the central region undecided. DTE.TD→DCE.TD and DCE.RD→DTE.RD connections have matching output/input directions; output-to-output and missing-reference examples fail. Synthetic±6 V values are illustrative, not an expected measured MAX3232 amplitude.

# PR-T38-08 — RS-485 direction-safe reusable byte channel

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.09](#t38-09).

## Contract

Implement `rs485_byte_channel_v1`: enqueue up to 16TX bytes with a caller token, accept/copy at most 16RX bytes into fixed storage, and emit byte, framing_error, overrun, tx_done, aborted and unavailable events. Return busy/accepted/consumed counts and explicit backpressure. The channel supplies no record delimiter, address or retry protocol. One transaction/driver at a time; callbacks cannot retain borrowed input, allocate or reenter. Reuse the UART adapter and a short two-node THVD1410-class prepared bus; peer scheduling is explicit.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture has two 8N1 bytes at 100 kbaud, DE assert 0,600 ns enabled-receiver startup,200 ns disable and 2 µs guard. Earliest peer start is 202.8 µs; release at 100.6 µs fails while 200.6 µs succeeds. A third synthetic drive interval overlaps the first two and must be flagged. Sixteen 1/8 unit receivers plus modeled bias 2 sum to 4 unit loads. Capacity 2 accepts 17,34 and reports one overflow for 51.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-08.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Define IDLE→ENABLING→TX→WAIT_TC→DISABLING→RX_READY states and token/abort ownership. Derive delay rounding for the actual timer.
2. Implement event/capacity handling with final-TC completion and confirmed stop before abort returns ownership.
3. Replay early release, overlap and RX overflow; use synthetic traces for forbidden active-driver overlap.
4. Record actual termination, bias/failsafe, load, reference and transceiver enabled/shutdown mode. Capture DE, UART TX and differential waveform for a scheduled two-node exchange.
5. Export the byte/event header, resource bounds and measured physical receipt to T40; keep application framing outside this channel.

## Failure cases

Premature DE release, simultaneous drivers, shutdown wake delay mistaken for ordinary enable delay, capacity overflow, stale token completion and unconfirmed DMA abort. On unknown device-stop state report unavailable and retain ownership until reset/stop is confirmed. A timeout cannot manufacture tx_done.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact timing/load/overlap/capacity oracle values; no byte loss hidden by the API; final stop preserved and measured non-overlap on the physical baseline. Supply both software and physical channel receipts and demonstrate token lifetime/backpressure to the T40 consumer. Profile E ledger includes ISR/shared-state and helper dependencies.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Round 600 ns to the next timer tick; a 1 µs timer cannot wait 0 ticks. Measure DE against final TC/stop, not against the last data-register write. Separate bias loading from receiver-count arithmetic.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

# PR-T38-09 — Classic CAN codec and bounded bxCAN control

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T38](#t38).

**Covered topics:** [T38.10](#t38-10), [T38.11](#t38-11).

## Contract

Implement a bounded standard-data classic CAN codec for 0–8 bytes with strict local DLC0–8, an 11/29-bit arbitration-prefix analyzer, and a small mailbox/filter/FIFO model. Reuse the prepared F439 image and implement only one TX mailbox, one mask rule and FIFO0 for the physical baseline; no full general CAN driver, FD, USB or complete fault-confinement state machine. Fixed codec storage is 128 bits plus at most 24 stuff bits; if a bounded output cannot fit, return capacity before publication.

This 12-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture compares standard remote ID 0x123, extended data sharing base 0x123 and standard data 0x123; standard data wins. Its comparison prefix includes standard IDE0 from the first control-field bit, so standard-remote versus extended is decided by the actual format bit rather than string termination. At 42 MHz, prescaler 6, BS1=11, BS2=2, SJW=1 give 500 kbit/s and sample 6/7. The 0x120/0x7F0 filter accepts 120,123,12F and rejects 130. FIFO10,20,30,40 retains 10,20,30 locked or 10,20,40 unlocked. The original CRC input is the destuffed SOF/header/data for standard ID 0x123 and one byte 0xA5; compare polynomial division with your bounded recurrence.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T38-09.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw arbitration fields including standard/extended and data/remote distinctions; use bit-sequence comparisons and explicitly handle identical contenders.
2. Implement the strict standard-data codec, destuff validation and classic CRC check; preserve separate CRC delimiter, ACK and EOF boundaries.
3. Implement the timing/filter/mailbox/FIFO model and reject illegal segment/register values. Make exactly-once receive release visible.
4. Configure one filter/mailbox/FIFO on the prepared board and exchange one known classic frame with a declared peer/transceiver, capturing timing and controller status. Internal loopback is a controller observation, not a physical peer proof.
5. Diagnose supplied arbitration-loss, transmit-error, error-passive and bus-off traces; state recovery exclusions and leave complete transition enforcement to additional inspected scope.

## Failure cases

Identifier/range/capacity rejection, bad stuff/CRC/fixed-form bits, strict-local DLC9–15 exclusion, illegal timing, filter mismatch, mailbox still pending, FIFO overflow and repeated release. Arbitration loss is a retry/participation event, not an error frame. Do not claim link ACK proves application delivery or that automatic bus-off recovery proves network health.

## Acceptance and evidence

Fixture arbitration/timing/mask/FIFO/CRC values, codec round-trip and independent malformed cases; source-backed classic-only capability. Give separate evidence for all six linked objectives: wire semantics, error-state scope, timing, acceptance and ownership. Close the physical receipt only with the declared two-node classic exchange; source analysis and loopback remain separately identified.

Compare standard RTR and extended SRR/IDE before lower identifier bits. Keep encoded fields distinct from semantic values minus one. For CRC, inspect the first differing destuffed bit rather than including inserted stuff in the classic input.

# PR-T39-02 — Ethernet media and checked frame boundary

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.02](#t39-02), [T39.03](#t39-03).

## Contract

Implement an allocation-free untagged Ethernet frame builder/parser: six-byte source/destination, a checked length/type field, payload≤1500, fixed caller capacity 1518 including optional FCS. Local output uses zero pad to 46 payload bytes; the host oracle computes declared reflected CRC32. VLAN, jumbo and the 1501..1535 gap are excluded. Separate buffers with/without FCS and physical preamble/SFD/gap; never place gap bytes in a DMA buffer. Record the prepared 100BASE-TX board/PHY/media path.

This 8-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

Original fixtures use three payload bytes with EtherType 0x0800 and length 3, requiring 43 pad bytes and 64 frame bytes including FCS. Gap 1520, VLAN 0x8100 and length 2 for a 3-byte payload fail under this local subset. The check string 123456789 has CRC32=0xCBF43926. FCS is calculated over destination through zero pad using declared reflected 0xEDB88320, initial/final complement, then serialized little-endian in this fixture; the target baseline lets MAC generate it.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-02.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Draw MAC/RMII/PHY/magnetics/cable boundaries and document exact board/clock/media identities.
2. Implement checked field/length/capacity parsing without casting unaligned network bytes into C structs.
3. Implement the declared CRC arithmetic and compare independent recurrence/zlib results; keep the RFC appendix’s arithmetic purpose distinct from Ethernet normative status.
4. Exercise minimum/maximum/pad/type/gap/tagged cases and distinguish meaningful length from padding.
5. Observe prepared physical link establishment/loss and a selected captured frame; identify whether its capture point exposes FCS/preamble. PHY management details follow PR-T39-04.

## Failure cases

Short header, oversized/overflowing length, capacity, length mismatch, unsupported tag/gap and bad declared FCS. VLAN is excluded, not universally invalid Ethernet. Unknown capture FCS stripping cannot be guessed. A virtual NIC or QEMU run does not prove cable/media/clock behavior.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact bytes/pad/FCS/length values plus independently reasoned maximum/short-header tests. Submit media/PHY responsibility ledger and actual link/capture observations for the physical route, with FCS visibility explicit. Each of the six linked objectives has its own evidence.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Use 14+payload+pad+4 for frame accounting. Compare CRC input bytes at the first mismatch; avoid the suspicious Rev 21 CRC-complement sentence as a derivation. For a length field, upper data excludes pad.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

## Transfer challenge

Change the MAC stripping policy and update exactly one frame-channel boundary rather than subtracting FCS independently at every layer.

# PR-T39-03 — MAC addressing and bounded learning bridge

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.04](#t39-04).

## Contract

Implement a six-byte MAC classifier and a synthetic three-port, four-entry learning bridge. Table capacity is fixed, expiration is 10 ticks and ingress values are 1..3. Reject group source addresses. Learn/update individual sources, expire before lookup, flood unknown/group destinations to other ports, forward known unicast and filter same-port destinations. This model excludes VLAN, spanning tree, loops and production switch conformance.

This 6-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

Addresses 02:...:01,01:00:5E:00:00:01,FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF and 00:11:22:33:44:55 exercise local/group/broadcast bits. At time 0 A→B floods; B→A at 1 learns B and forwards to 1; A→B at 2 forwards to 2; A→A at 3 filters; time 12 C→B sees B expired and floods to 1,2. Expiry uses age≥10.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-03.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Mark first-octet I/G/U/L and distinguish printed hex order from wire bit order.
2. Implement exact six-byte validation and the fixed table with a declared capacity-failure policy.
3. Replay learning, refresh, same-port filtering and expiration; log table contents and outputs.
4. Add group/broadcast and full-table inputs, rejecting duplicate/conflicting malformed entries without hidden allocation.
5. Compare endpoint filtering and switched capture visibility; explain why promiscuous mode is not a network-wide tap.

## Failure cases

Wrong address length, group source, invalid ingress, nonmonotonic time, table full and stale-entry lookup. Local address does not guarantee uniqueness. Returning an ingress port as a flood destination is a forwarding bug. Bridge forwarding is separate from IP routing.

## Acceptance and evidence

Fixture bit classes and forwarding/expiry outputs plus own group/full-capacity tests. Show first failed invariant, table/resource bound and endpoint filter/capture assumptions. All three topic objectives require evidence.

## Hints and recovery

Expire before refreshing the current source and before looking up destination. Separate “unknown” from “known on the ingress port”; both must not use the same output decision.

# PR-T39-04 — RMII clock and bounded PHY management

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.05](#t39-05).

## Contract

Implement bounded F439 SMI read/reset/status queries for the inspected LAN8742A route using the matching Rev 8 board Ethernet pin/clock table and actual board-revision receipt. One register access at a time, at most 32PHY addresses for an explicit discovery attempt, finite reset/access/link deadlines. Check PHY IDs, two BSR reads and register 31 negotiated result. Only 10/full or 100/full closes the selected mode-ready gate; half duplex remains decoded but unsupported. Do not transmit with a guessed speed/duplex or edit the MII register while busy.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile E under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

At HCLK168 MHz, CR100 divides 102 and PHY0/register 2 read-start is 0x91; busy input forbids writes and 10 MHz HCLK is outside this selected divider scope. PHY IDs are 0007 and C13x. BSR first 20/second 24 distinguishes historic/current link. Register 31=0x1018 indicates 100/full and done;0x1008 indicates 100/half and is excluded. Wrong ID, link-down and incomplete negotiation have distinct fixture results.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-04.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. Add an independently reasoned boundary case of your own.

## Steps

1. Record exact board revision, Ethernet pins/solder bridges, PHY address/ID and 50 MHz reference source. Measure the clock with adequate instrument bandwidth/sampling.
2. Derive PA/MR/CR/MW/MB fields from the actual register scope; require idle before writes, select fields with MB0, then start the read and wait boundedly for completion before consuming data.
3. Implement reset polling and ID masking; unknown/all-ones reads are diagnostic results, not a discovered matching PHY.
4. Read BSR twice, record both values, confirm register 31 done and mode, and configure MAC mode only from a ready result.
5. Capture/record link establishment and removal, MDC rate and timeout prefixes. Export the management result contract for T41.

## Failure cases

Busy no-write, unsupported clock range, absent reference, reset/access timeout, wrong IDs, link down, incomplete negotiation, unknown mode and half-duplex exclusion. A latched-low first read is not alone current link status, and a ready observation is not an everlasting link guarantee. A PHY status fault cannot be inferred solely from a synthetic adapter timeout.

## Acceptance and evidence

Exact fixture command/clock/ID/latch/mode results and explicit timeout tests; actual matching board/PHY status and 50 MHz/MDC observations for physical closure. Record source identities and image audit, and invalidate mode on link change before later sends.

Retain one explicit evidence item for each original objective under every linked topic: explanation, implemented/derived property, observed result and limitation. Submit interface/source, replay, dependency/resource ledger and first-failure analysis. Synthetic, target and physical receipts remain separately identified; equipment acquisition or missing adapter/peer setup is an entry prerequisite, not hidden work inside the hour budget.

## Hints and recovery

Read identity and status before building packets. Reduce an MDIO failure to reference clock, PHY address, divider, busy sequence and source-backed pin path. Preserve first/second latch reads instead of overwriting history.

If a check disagrees, minimize the first failing prefix and compare units, capture point, state and ownership. Use [guide-assessment](#guide-assessment) for targeted remediation; repair only the failed objective group.

Declare SRAM interval[0x20000000,0x20030000), CPU-only CCM excluded, aligned fixed normal descriptors and maximum 1536-byte buffers. The local 4-byte alignment rule is a project policy. Assert reset, select RMII under reset/before clocks, enable clocks, complete reset, prepare descriptors, install bases/accepted PHY mode, then start the separately controlled MAC/DMA engines. No full IP/TCP stack is needed.

The oracle lists each first-order dependency violation, not a claim of every hardware readiness check.

Implement normal-descriptor RX validation and `ethernet_frame_channel_v1` receive handoff. At most 2 descriptors per frame and 1536 combined caller bytes; configured CSTF=APCS=0 retains FCS, accepted FL64..1518, publish FL−4 bytes from DA. Require all OWN clear, first FS, last LS, no ES/DE and capacity before publication. The core target baseline can reject multi-descriptor frames; the model still exercises a declared two-descriptor complete chain. A borrowed span/token may be released exactly once, and recycling waits until the consumer releases it.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture has FL64 complete frames with/without a held consumer, DMA-owned, incomplete FS-only, ES/DE, FL100 in capacity 80 and a complete two-descriptor frame. FL64 publishes 60 bytes; incomplete/error/capacity cases publish none. A held successful consumer forbids recycling; returned/failed CPU-owned storage is recyclable under the declared drop policy.

# PR-T39-07 — Ethernet transmit publication and bounded recovery

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T39](#t39).

**Covered topics:** [T39.08](#t39-08).

## Contract

Implement a fixed two-descriptor TX publication model and bounded transmit side of `ethernet_frame_channel_v1`. Accept a caller frame beginning DA without preamble/FCS,14..1514 bytes and exact declared capacity; MAC supplies pad/FCS under the selected policy. Copy into fixed internal storage or retain an explicit borrow token until confirmed completion/stop. At most 2 queued slots, one publication at a time. Full ring returns backpressure; no hidden allocation or automatic unbounded retry.

This 10-hour milestone includes implementation and verification. The module budgets reading, assessment and delayed consolidation separately. Apply profile C under [guide-profiles](#guide-profiles): fixed caller storage and explicit component/image dependencies. A hosted harness may print/use library oracles; that permission does not extend to the studied component or target image.

## Inputs and expected results

Successful events prepare tail/head, own tail/head, complete then reuse. Early own-head fails partial_publication; reuse while DMA-owned fails premature_reuse. Error completion and confirmed reset-stop return local ownership but not peer-delivery proof. Payload 3,46,100 requires 43,0,0 pad bytes. The fixture’s completion events imply ownership has actually returned, not merely that an IRQ fired.

The original supplied fixture is `fixtures/communications/PR-T39-07.json`. Its `input` and exact `expected` fields are reproducible using `python tools/verify_communications_fixtures.py`; the Python oracle verifies fixture data, not your C or hardware. ## Steps

1. Define CPU-prepared, DMA-owned, complete, failed, abort-pending and stopped-generation states.
2. Prepare metadata/buffers and publish tail before first OWN with declared compiler/hardware order.
3. Implement bounded completion, failure/backpressure and stop/reset ownership handling; prevent late-generation completion from ending a new request.
4. Replay publication/reuse failures and add a full-ring plus unconfirmed-stop case.
5. Bind the mechanism to the prepared E adapter for one captured frame and preserve image/map/status evidence, retaining the C component’s separate undefined-symbol audit.

## Failure cases

Capacity/invalid length, partial descriptor publication, full ring, premature reuse, completion without publication, unconfirmed abort and stale completion. On unknown engine state report unavailable/retain ownership; confirmed error completion is not successful wire delivery. An interrupt by itself is insufficient.

## Acceptance and evidence

All publication/reuse/padding fixture values plus own backpressure/generation/stop-confirmation tests. Exact frame policy and first-OWN ordering are visible; every success/error/abort ownership return is justified. Submit target descriptor and external frame observations for hardware closure.

## Hints and recovery

Make the first descriptor the final publication point. Keep “queued”, “in flight”, “local completion” and “peer application accepted” as distinct outcomes. On timeout preserve the outstanding token until stop is established.

# PR-T40-01 — Seven boundary contracts and encapsulation ledger

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.01](#t40-01).

## Contract

Produce the executable design boundary for EDU7-v1 before implementing packets. Use the fixed [original wire contract](research/enhancement/networking_contracts.json), rather than choosing new addresses or retry policies. A=17, R=34 and B=51 use two independent segments. R terminates L1/L2 and forwards L3 without decoding presentation/session data. Map application, typed representation, dialogue, bounded reliable message, routed datagram, local frame and physical symbols to their actual responsibility.

Define each layer's submit/receive/tick/completion interface, result and ownership. A synchronous receive span is immutable and borrowed until callback return. Waiting layers copy into bounded private storage. An asynchronous accepted transmit span remains immutable until its specified completion; BUSY consumes nothing. The ledger must identify which completions permit buffer reuse and which establish peer delivery.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture starts with a conservative L6 service capacity of 80 octets, L5 header 7, L4 payload 24/header 8, L3 header 6 and L2 header 5/CRC 2. The capacity proof gives session storage 87 and fragment capacities 24, 24, 24, 15. Schema 1 cannot actually encode 80 legal octets: its largest canonical record is 1+5*2+(1+2+2+1+16)=33, giving session SDU 40 and fragments 24, 16. The fixture recomputes both bounds. The largest generated network packet is 38 octets and link body 45; generic allowed link payload 40 separately requires body 47 and worst escaped frame 96. Treat storage capacity and accepted syntax as different bounds.

Output a boundary table, nested worked trace and capacity assertions. The fixture's independent arithmetic verifier derives all sizes; your C tests demonstrate that capacities and checked arithmetic enforce them.

## Steps

1. Draw A→R→B and attach three namespaces: local link 1/2, node 17/34/51, ports 7/8.
2. Write a state/lifetime contract for every interface, including upper-delivery rejection and lower BUSY.
3. Derive lengths outward from the 80-octet capacity envelope and the actual 33-octet canonical maximum, then inward from the 40-octet link limit; reconcile all three bounds.
4. Instrument a host pipeline with layer events without yet solving the protocols. Poison borrowed input after return and attempt a forbidden queued reference.
5. Review the trace against X.200 purposes and Peterson/Davie's encapsulation passage. Mark original protocol decisions separately from reference-model definitions.

## Failure cases

Reject an 81-octet presentation record before publication, arithmetic beyond configured capacity, a retained pointer to a borrowed span, and treating R as an application endpoint. A local CRC success may not be reported as session/application success. A BUSY return may not advance or free the sender's buffer.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the seven service/peer rows, all capacities with units, an exact routed encapsulation trace, and one rejected lifetime trace. Show why Internet protocols do not require one distinct library per OSI layer. For the three topic objectives retain model comparison, nested/address trace and per-boundary ownership/error ledger. This design milestone requires no physical-success claim and does not replace the later implementations.

## Hints and recovery

Start from one record and change one layer at a time. If the length ledger disagrees, label whether a number is SDU, PDU, escaped bytes or physical bit times. If ownership is vague, identify exactly who may write/free each storage slot at one event boundary.

## Transfer challenge

Change only the optional label length. Predict which nested lengths and fragment count change, and which routing/session authority remains unchanged. Do not change the accepted wire contract during the required milestone.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.01.a:** Distinguish OSI reference-model responsibilities from a particular protocol suite and Internet architecture.
- **T40.01.b:** Trace an application record through all seven original layer PDUs and both physical segments.
- **T40.01.c:** Specify ownership, capacities, addressing scope and error publication at every service boundary.

# PR-T40-02 — Two-segment RS-485 grant scheduler and measured adapter

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.02](#t40-02).

## Contract

Reuse the bounded byte-channel work from T38.09 and UART completion from T38.02.c. Adapt it to the declared THVD1400 3.3-V boards and add EDU7-v1's two-segment master-granted schedule. This milestone's new implementation is medium-access scheduling and routed bench integration; do not charge the reused channel implementation again.

Each segment is at most 1 m with termination at both ends and a common reference. RE is low; DE is separately controlled. Assert DE 200 us before data, release only after final TC, then allow a peer after a 200 us guard. Local echo is filtered by transmit ownership. Master link 1 starts a turn each 25 ms: at most one DATA followed by zero-payload POLL; slave link 2 replies once with DATA/EMPTY, starting within 2 ms after complete POLL+guard and completing within 10 ms of its first octet.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture derives ten bits per 8N1 octet, the rounded-up occupancy of 96 octets and legal DE/peer-start events. Its deliberately premature TXE release must fail. Start and completion deadlines are distinct: an on-time reply may legally continue after the start deadline. Host timestamps are injected integer microseconds, never claimed measured waveforms.

Expected outputs include grant state, start/completion timeout counters, echo-filtered peer octets and a waveform index for both actual segments. A missing bench closes software tests only.

## Steps

1. Record board/pins, actual adapter schematic, supply and differential polarity. Check end-to-end termination with power off and explain the approximately 60 ohm parallel result.
2. Reuse the byte/error channel and add per-segment master/slave turn states and finite deadlines. Keep router UARTs independent.
3. Test maximum frame duration, legal EMPTY, no reply, late first byte and legal long reply with virtual time.
4. Measure DE, UART TX and bus differential signal. Correlate TC with the final stop bit; show no driver overlap.
5. Run both segments, then remove/reconnect one cable. Record UART faults/discarded candidates and scheduler recovery without inventing clean bytes.

## Failure cases

An ungranted slave transmission is a counted protocol fault; no overlapping drive is deliberately required to prove rejection. Premature TC assumptions, late start, over 10 ms reply, UART framing/overrun faults and link disconnect produce distinct outcomes. Do not connect an undocumented voltage-domain adapter or substitute RS-232 signals for this differential bus.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain wiring/termination/part table, two DE/TX/bus captures with settings and timing uncertainty, exact host grant logs, and disconnect/reconnect evidence. The timing oracle checks schedule arithmetic; real measurements close voltage/wiring, final-stop-bit and driver-ownership claims. Demonstrate the three objectives through measured topology, scheduler/TC behavior and an explicit software-versus-physical evidence matrix.

## Hints and recovery

If replies disappear, first compare link grant and DE ownership, then UART errors, then framing; application code cannot repair truncated physical bytes. If a long legal reply is cut off, separate its start deadline from completion deadline. Measure polarity rather than inferring it from a decoder's label.

## Transfer challenge

Run an intentionally slower legal baud as a separate experiment: recalculate the entire turn budget before proceeding. Explain which policy deadlines would need a new contract rather than silently retaining them.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.02.a:** Wire and measure the declared 3.3-V transceiver, terminations and two independent half-duplex segments.
- **T40.02.b:** Implement UART transmit-complete, driver-enable guards and master-granted turns without overlapping drivers.
- **T40.02.c:** Separate real physical timing/disconnect evidence from deterministic host octet traces.

{
  "id": "FX-NET-T40-02",
  "description": "Synthetic UART/DE timing arithmetic and deliberate absence of physical evidence.",
  "input": {
    "case_kind": "grant_timing",
    "data_bits": 8,

# PR-T40-03 — Incremental escaped link framer with independent CRC

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.03](#t40-03).

## Contract

Implement only L2's exact delimiter/escape/header/CRC decoder and encoder above the granted byte channel. Body fields are version 1, kind 0/1/2, local source, local destination, payload length 0..40, payload and big-endian CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE. Encode CRC over the unescaped header/payload, then escape 0x7e/0x7d; delimit with 0x7e. Maximum unescaped body 47 and escaped frame 96 are checked capacities, not allocation suggestions.

Decoder publication occurs only after delimiter, escape, CRC, version, kind, actual length, local destination and grant checks all pass. A POLL/EMPTY has zero payload. A DATA received on the wrong ownership turn does not deliver upward.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture contains a body with both escape characters, exact encoded wire hex, CRC and known ASCII check vector 123456789→0x29b1. Its negative inputs are isolated candidates for truncated escape, corrupted CRC, foreign destination, impossible declared length, capacity overflow and missing grant. The oracle classifies each isolated candidate; it does not execute a streaming receiver or count callbacks across consecutive candidates.

Create a mandatory learner stream containing an overlong candidate, a resynchronizing delimiter and then a valid frame. Assert exactly one upper callback with only the valid payload. Repeat with truncated escape and foreign traffic preceding a valid frame, and split each stream at every octet boundary.

Your decoder output is an immutable borrowed local SDU plus metadata, or a counted rejection. Splitting input at every octet boundary must produce the same valid payload/event sequence as coalesced input.

## Steps

1. Derive the CRC vector independently on paper for a small prefix, then compare with the supplied finite verifier's polynomial calculation.
2. Design SEARCH/BODY/ESCAPE/DISCARD state and an explicit reset/resynchronization rule for every delimiter.
3. Implement bounded incremental parsing without publishing a partially decoded header or payload.
4. Enumerate every split of the encoded frame and append noise/truncation followed by the valid frame.
5. Integrate grant metadata; serialize one frame on each measured segment and compare the actual unescaped header/CRC with the host expectation.

## Failure cases

Trailing escape, candidate over 47, incorrect CRC/version/kind, mismatch between actual and declared length, foreign addresses and ungranted DATA publish no upper callback. Empty delimiters publish nothing. After DISCARD, the next delimiter permits a fresh candidate; a broken prefix must not poison an indefinitely long stream.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit exact encoder hex, independent CRC witness, exhaustive split table, rejection/resynchronization counters and actual frame capture if bench is available. Show that a valid local frame can still be lost later and that CRC does not authenticate a sender. The objectives' evidence is the parser/encoder contract, bounded recovery traces and scoped delivery/drop observations. Preserve output sentinels and borrowed-span lifetime on rejected input.

## Hints and recovery

Check whether the CRC was computed before or after escaping. If only split input fails, trace the stored escape state rather than changing wire bytes. If noise grows memory, switch to DISCARD with a bounded counter rather than retaining the entire candidate.

## Transfer challenge

Use a payload composed entirely of delimiter/escape octets and recompute the maximum wire size. Explain why worst-case expansion does not double a physical bit error probability into a reliability guarantee.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.03.a:** Encode and incrementally validate the exact bounded delimiter/escape/header/CRC frame contract.
- **T40.03.b:** Recover framing after truncation, noise, bad escaping, foreign addresses and overlong input.
- **T40.03.c:** Demonstrate local-link delivery and drop counters without attributing end-to-end reliability to CRC.

# PR-T40-04 — Static two-link router with hop and lifetime oracles

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.04](#t40-04).

## Contract

Implement L3 forwarding at R and endpoint delivery at A/B. The six-octet header is version 1, network source, destination, hop limit, next protocol 4 and payload length 0..34. A begins hop 4; R forwards only known nonlocal routes with hop>1, preserving end-to-end source/destination/payload and decrementing hop. B locally consumes positive-hop packets addressed to 51. No dynamic routes, broadcast or L3 fragmentation are part of this contract.

Use the exact table: A→51 left/link 2; R→17 left/link 1; R→51 right/link 2; B→17 right/link 1. R owns a bounded private copy while its egress segment is BUSY; the input span is invalid immediately after return. Rebuild egress link header and CRC.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture routes A 17→B 51 via R 34 with hop 4 and a fixed payload. Expected right output retains source 17/destination 51, hop 3, link source 1/destination 2 and identical upper bytes. Additional unknown-route, hop 1, own-origin-loop and bad length/protocol cases produce distinct counted drops with no forward/local delivery.

Output a route decision and changed/preserved field ledger, plus complete rebuilt link bytes from the already-tested L2 encoder. The fixture arithmetic/route oracle does not implement a target router for you.

## Steps

1. Decode the network header with enclosing link bounds before table lookup. Keep ports opaque.
2. Separate local consumption from forwarding; never decrement a hop solely for delivery at B.
3. Copy one accepted egress packet into private storage before returning input ownership. Reject BUSY enqueue without consuming caller state.
4. Poison input storage and delay the other segment's grant; verify egress bytes remain unchanged.
5. Capture the same end-to-end record on both segments and annotate only local addresses, hop and CRC as changed.

## Failure cases

Unknown destination, hop<=1 at a forwarding router, source claiming R in a looped packet, wrong next protocol, actual length mismatch and full egress slot are independent failures. A foreign link address must already have been rejected by L2. An own-origin loop cannot be repaired by merely decrementing hops until zero.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit positive and negative route tables, output wire record, poisoned-input ownership test and measured two-segment relay if available. Explain three address namespaces and why copying a link destination into a network destination is wrong. Evidence for the objectives covers namespaces, exact static forwarding and hop/route/storage failures; every drop leaves session/transport state untouched.

## Hints and recovery

If only delayed egress fails, inspect who owns the input after callback return. If routing works in one direction only, rewrite the left/right local address table explicitly; R has two different link identities. Do not add a default route to make a failing fixture pass.

## Transfer challenge

Predict a hop 2 forward and hop 1 destination delivery, then contrast hop 1 at R. Explain which behavior belongs to the original forwarding contract, rather than assuming an IP router's entire policy was implemented.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.04.a:** Keep link next-hop addresses distinct from end-to-end node addresses and service ports.
- **T40.04.b:** Forward between the two segments by the exact static route table while preserving end-to-end fields.
- **T40.04.c:** Predict and verify unknown-route, hop-limit and ownership failures at the intermediate router.
