# PR-T40-05 — Stop-and-wait message transport with atomic reassembly

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.05](#t40-05).

## Contract

Implement L4 over the unreliable routed datagram service. DATA/ACK/PROBE headers carry type, source/destination port, transfer ID, fragment index/count and credit. DATA has 1–24 octets; non-final fragments are exactly 24 and the message is at most 120. Ports 7↔8 select the endpoint service. Keep one outstanding fragment and one bounded reassembly per direction; no partial message reaches L5.

Transfer IDs start at 1 and increase within the session without reuse/wrap. Keep highest-completed ID and one last-completed receipt including final fragment bytes. Re-ACK an identical duplicate final fragment without redelivery; older completed IDs drop. Keep a complete message pending upper consumption with credit zero. Reopen the session before ID wrap.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture has a 25-octet message, repeated first fragment after a lost ACK, a credit-zero pause/probe, credit reopening, final fragment and repeated final fragment. Expected upper bytes appear once only after completion; ACK indices and probe time are exact. Separate failure traces reach retransmissions at 100, 200, 300 ms then fail at 400 ms; blocked credit reaches its independent 500-ms deadline.

Report transfer result, complete delivery bytes/count, matching ACKs, retransmitted bytes/indices, retained/free state and timeout counters. Both failure traces retain unchanged upper output. The supplied oracle derives fragment sizes and abstract event outcomes, not a solved transport stack.

## Steps

1. Spend the first 4 h defining sender/receiver tuple and states, checked fragment arithmetic and matching ACK rules; run a normal 25-octet transfer.
2. Add duplicate receipt and atomic upper publication. A completion callback may refuse consumption, so keep the SDU and advertise no credit.
3. Start clocks only after lower submit accepts transmission; BUSY/grant waiting alone must not consume a retry.
4. In the remaining 6 h, inject lost ACK, wrong ID/index/count, credit pause, reset and final-ACK loss. Advance virtual time exactly through boundaries.
5. Relay on both measured segments and compare application delivery count with frame/retry count. Record which delays come from grants and which from transport timers.

## Failure cases

A mismatched ACK frees nothing. Duplicate accepted data appends nothing. Wrong non-final length, unexpected index/count, total over 120, old completed ID, unsupported port and no capacity are distinct rejects. Credit probes do not restart the blocked deadline. At retry or blocked failure, clear partial state and publish a failure event, never a partial SDU. Session reopen clears old receipts and separates ID incarnations.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain the sender/receiver state diagram, exact fragment/ACK ledger, injected-clock log, complete upper bytes and failure cleanup witnesses. For all three objectives show checked segmentation/reassembly, match/retry/credit transitions and absence of partial publication/leaks. Capture one dropped-ACK retry on the bench if available. An eventual successful transfer alone cannot replace the timeout/duplicate evidence.

## Hints and recovery

If a repeated byte appears upward, distinguish duplicate fragment append from repeated complete-message publication. If retries fire during BUSY, move the timer origin to accepted transmission. If credit probes prolong blocking forever, retain a separate resource-deadline origin.

## Transfer challenge

Change the message from 25 to 120 octets and predict all five fragment sizes, retained storage and final-ACK behavior. Explain why adopting a byte-stream API would require a different service contract.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.05.a:** Segment and atomically reassemble bounded messages using the exact transfer/fragment contract.
- **T40.05.b:** Trace matching acknowledgments, retransmission, duplicates and credit probes with an injected clock.
- **T40.05.c:** Prove that failed or blocked transfers publish no partial message and free their bounded state.

# PR-T40-06 — Negotiated session, dialogue token and retained-state resume

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.06](#t40-06).

## Contract

Implement L5 independent of L4's transfer IDs. Session headers carry type, nonzero session ID, nonzero epoch and checkpoint. OPEN/OPEN_ACK negotiate schema 1, unit 1 and initial holder A; control records use checkpoint 0. DATA uses the next positive checkpoint per direction. Only the current holder sends DATA. A request transfers the token to B, B responds and transfers it back.

On sending TOKEN, enter TOKEN_PENDING and block new DATA until matching transport completion. Receiver changes holder once on complete TOKEN; repeats are idempotent. A lost ACK can pause progress but cannot permit both endpoints to send. Retained RAM stores committed checkpoint, bytes and response; close/reopen precedes wrap.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture uses a session/epoch, a SET at checkpoint 1, the same DATA again, altered bytes at checkpoint 1, token pending/lost completion, compatible retained resume and peer reboot. Expected effects count is one, the changed duplicate is ERROR, DATA during pending is blocked, retained state resumes and absent state refuses.

Output state/events, token holder, pending flag, per-direction committed checkpoint and application effect count. A successful transport ACK is not by itself compatible negotiation or application authorization.

## Steps

1. Draw negotiation, READY, TOKEN_PENDING, retained-reset, resume-refused and CLOSED transitions.
2. Encode exact OPEN control fields and reject mismatched schema/unit/epoch before DATA delivery.
3. Commit a DATA checkpoint only after accepted upper handling; retain identical bytes and recorded response for duplicate suppression.
4. Lose the token-transfer ACK and attempt DATA at both nodes. Complete/repeat the transfer and prove at most one permission exists.
5. Reset only transport while keeping session RAM, then separately reboot the peer without RAM. Compare RESUME results and cleanup. Correlate session checkpoints with different L4 retry IDs in the log.

## Failure cases

Nonholder DATA, checkpoint skip/wrap, changed payload at the same checkpoint, stale epoch, incompatible unit/schema and rebooted peer state publish no new effect. CLOSE clears session authority; a new epoch cannot inherit an old receipt. An ERROR event may not silently restore token ownership. Neither checkpoint matching nor an epoch field supplies authentication or durable recovery.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the state diagram and exact OPEN/DATA/TOKEN/RESUME wire fields, lost-ACK token trace, duplicate effect count and retained-versus-reboot evidence. The three objectives require distinct negotiation/dialogue, checkpoint/effect and resumption-limit witnesses. Show where RAM state disappears and explicitly state that an effect surviving a reboot would need a different durable protocol.

## Hints and recovery

If both nodes appear permitted, inspect sender TOKEN_PENDING rather than inventing an extra timeout transfer. If a duplicate changes state, compare checkpoint plus payload and response before applying. If a reboot resumes, identify where the claimed retained state actually came from.

## Transfer challenge

Consider a power loss immediately after applying SET but before any durable record. Explain why this RAM-only design cannot promise durable exactly-once processing; propose requirements without adding an unverified persistence implementation.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.06.a:** Negotiate schema/units and enforce explicit dialogue-token ownership independently of transport state.
- **T40.06.b:** Use per-direction checkpoints to suppress repeated application effects after a retained-state resume.
- **T40.06.c:** Distinguish successful RAM-state resume from stale epoch, incompatible negotiation and reboot refusal.

# PR-T40-07 — Canonical TLV presentation with strict UTF-8

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T40](#t40).

**Covered topics:** [T40.07](#t40-07).

## Contract

Implement L6 schema 1, ascending unique tag/length/value fields and at most 80 octets. Tags 1–5 encode verb u8, request ID big-endian u16, signed big-endian two's-complement centidegrees value, unit u8 and optional UTF-8 label of at most 16 octets. Every record needs verb/request ID; SET and REPLY need value/unit 1. GET need not carry them. ERROR may report retained setpoint/unit 1. Unknown tags are rejected.

Validate all syntax/required fields, exact lengths, integer representation, unit and canonical UTF-8 before publishing a typed record. Use staged output so failure preserves sentinels. Label is display data and never a format string or routing authority.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture encodes SET request 42, value -4000 and unit 1. Its exact presentation wire hex is independently reconstructed; signed bytes are f0 60. Invalid cases include duplicate/out-of-order tag, wrong field length, missing unit, truncated TLV, overlong UTF-8, surrogate encoding and schema mismatch.

Output exact wire bytes or a typed staged value plus deterministic error category. Distinguish representable 12501 from application's disallowed setpoint: L6 can represent it, while L7 rejects its effect.

## Steps

1. Derive the canonical 15-octet SET record by hand; do not copy a native struct.
2. Implement checked encoder capacity and staged decoder with all required-field checks.
3. Decode negative values with unsigned intermediates and explicit representable conversion. Test -32768, 32767 and the application boundaries separately.
4. Validate UTF-8 across each split of a multibyte label; reject overlong, surrogate and >U+10FFFF sequences before publication.
5. Compare outputs with the independent fixture and integrate one encoded record through session/transport without giving presentation access to route/token state.

## Failure cases

Truncation, duplicate/out-of-order or unknown tag, wrong known-field length, missing required tag, invalid unit/schema, label over 16 octets and malformed UTF-8 leave output unchanged. Encoder insufficient capacity writes no partial record under the selected staging contract. A decoded out-of-application-range integer is not silently clamped or applied.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain exact encode/decode round trips, negative-value derivation, invalid-case sentinels and UTF-8 byte-count/split evidence. For the objectives show representation portability, validated publication and separation of presentation from routing/session/application authority. Measure serialized bytes, not sizeof a host struct. Integrate on the bench only after finite representation tests pass.

## Hints and recovery

If a negative value differs by 65536, inspect signed conversion and byte order. If labels work only unsplit, keep bounded incremental state or decode after complete L6 SDU rather than treating callback boundaries as code points. Do not repair malformed input by replacing characters under a canonical-wire contract.

## Transfer challenge

Replace ASCII label with a legal multibyte label near 16 octets. Predict packet/fragment lengths and explain why the numeric unit remains unchanged even if the display language changes.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T40.07.a:** Convert between local typed values and canonical bounded TLVs without copying native struct layout.
- **T40.07.b:** Validate ordering, uniqueness, signed range, units and UTF-8 before publishing a decoded record.
- **T40.07.c:** Show that presentation encoding changes no routing, transport or application semantic authority.

GET returns plant value; successful SET within [-4000, 12500] changes/replies with setpoint. Invalid SET produces ERROR containing retained setpoint/unit 1 and changes nothing. ## Inputs and expected results

The fixture applies SET request 42 value -4000, duplicate checkpoint/payload, invalid SET 12501, then GET. Expected setpoint is -4000, plant remains 1800, accepted effects count 1 and response values correlate exactly. 5. Publish the evidence index and measured uncertainty, then reconstruct one unseen fault and one byte split during review.

Repair the first failed boundary, then repeat one adjacent interaction.

## Transfer challenge

# PR-T41-01 — Controlled Ethernet endpoint and ownership ledger

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 h | core | E |

## Contract

Specify the exact F439-LAN8742 same-link profile before implementing its stack. Board IP is 192.0.2.2/24, fixture MAC 02:00:00:00:00:02, peer 192.0.2.1/24, passive TCP 8080. The actual peer MAC is recorded during the cable lab. There is no default route, DHCP, DNS, bridge to the Internet, VLAN or fragmentation/options support. State explicitly that a cooperative-client exchange is not full RFC/IEEE conformance.

Define frame/datagram/segment/stream boundaries and ownership for receive, submit, tick, link change, DMA completion and TCP ACK. Reuse T39's frame-channel design; the new work is the upper packet/stream handoff and finite stack resource plan. A borrowed receive span expires on callback return; queued data needs private owned storage.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture gives an application TCP payload length 3, fixed headers 20/20, Ethernet header 14, minimum pre-FCS frame 60 and FCS 4. Expected IP 43, unpadded frame 57, pad 3 and MAC frame 64 exclude preamble/SFD/interpacket gap. It also budgets six 2048-byte DMA buffers and six 16-byte descriptors.

Output interface/result/lifetime table, nested length diagram, static resource inventory and omitted-requirements matrix. The independent fixture derives arithmetic; actual build map and capacity tests validate placement/bounds.

## Steps

1. Draw MAC/PHY/magnetics/cable and Internet layer ownership without forcing seven one-to-one protocol labels.
2. Define immutable packet spans, complete validation before publication and BUSY without consuming caller bytes.
3. Separate TX DMA buffer reuse from retention of unacknowledged TCP bytes. Design a bounded retransmission copy and 512-byte receive storage.
4. Derive padding and nested length trimming independently, including ARP which has no IP wrapper.
5. Prepare isolated host adapter settings and select independent capture/client tools. Attach actual source revision and board identity to the ledger.

## Failure cases

Do not count Ethernet padding as IP/TCP payload, cast an incomplete header, free retransmission bytes at DMA completion, or call an emulator physical evidence. A second simultaneous connection is refused by the one-connection resource contract. Queue-full/BUSY preserves ownership, and protocol omissions remain visible even after successful HTTP.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit subset/exclusion table, exact boundary lengths and API/resource/ownership ledger. For the objectives demonstrate declared interoperability limits, nested bytes/lifetimes and packet-to-stream semantics. Show at least one rejected borrowed-reference test and a build-map storage plan. No physical claim closes in this design milestone.

## Hints and recovery

Name every length by its starting byte and excluded trailer. If ownership is unclear, compare DMA complete and TCP ACK as two separate events. If an excluded requirement seems optional, consult the actual host/RFC scope before labeling it that way.

## Transfer challenge

Increase HTTP response length beyond MSS 256 and predict segmentation, retained output and padding per packet while preserving the exact response byte stream.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.01.b:** Trace nested Ethernet/ARP or Ethernet/IPv4/TCP/HTTP lengths and buffer ownership.

# PR-T41-03 — Original normal-ring MAC/DMA driver with reuse recovery

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.03](#t41-03).

## Contract

Implement the selected polled F439 Ethernet driver, reusing T39's descriptor/lifetime models as design evidence. Four RX/two TX normal 16-byte descriptors use contiguous, word-aligned DMA SRAM and one 2048-byte buffer each; no CCM, enhanced format, chained mode, skip words or timestamping. RBS1=2048/RBS2=0; RER marks final RX. TBS1 is actual transmit bytes/TBS2=0; TER marks final TX.

Use store-and-forward, software checksums, CSTF=APCS=IPCO=0, no error/undersized forwarding. Normal TDES0 controls are rebuilt on every reuse; OWN is published last after required ordering. RX exposes FL-4 bytes only with OWN clear, FS+LS, no ES/DE and FL 64..1518. MAC pads and appends TX CRC; preamble/SFD are not user packet bytes.

## Inputs and expected results

Fixture statuses cover DMA-owned, valid 64/1518, partial, error, descriptor-error and overrange frames. Valid64 exposes 60 bytes, valid 1518 exposes 1514. The ring/buffer cost is 12384 bytes. Independent bit arithmetic derives last TX control mask and validates configured normal-ring size; snapshots deliberately show writeback-cleared control bits.

Outputs are frame spans, completion/error events, ring indices, counters and register/ownership logs. A synthetic descriptor oracle does not establish a functioning target driver.

## Steps

1. First 4 h: prove map-file addresses are reachable, initialize reset/clocks/filter/MAC mode, stopped list bases and normal ring metadata. Use exact inspected register descriptions, including address 0 octet ordering.
2. Build a host side-effect model for OWN/control writeback, W1C status and poll demand. Reject premature reuse.
3. Remaining 6 h: implement target RX/TX and wrap both rings repeatedly. Keep retransmission copy ownership separate from DMA-buffer reuse.
4. Rebuild FS/LS/IC/TER on reused TDES0, then publish OWN with target ordering. Refill suspended RX before poll demand; transmit demand follows new ownership.
5. Exercise ring-full, consumer delay, unavailable-buffer status, failed completion and bounded reset/stop. Fatal bus error stops service and reports its snapshot.

## Failure cases

Wrong SRAM/unaligned descriptor, CPU payload read with OWN set, absent FS/LS, ES/DE, invalid FL, double CRC subtraction, reused control bits lost, ring-full and unknown W1C bits all fail deterministically. Configure list bases only stopped. Fatal error cannot be recovered by merely acknowledging status while continuing corrupted queues.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit build-map memory proof, exact initialization/register table, all ownership traces and real repeated ring wrap/reuse plus external frame capture. For the objectives show initialization/reachability, publication/reclaim/error checks and exact length/recovery. Root's source ledger identifies the generic IC reference conflict; use the actual normal TDES0 detail, not a guessed TDES1 bit. Host-only results leave hardware evidence open.

## Hints and recovery

If the first TX works but reuse fails, inspect writeback reset of TDES0 controls. If payload is four bytes short, audit both hardware strip bits and software subtraction. If RX stalls, restore ownership before issuing poll demand; do not write every status bit as a blind reset.

## Transfer challenge

Temporarily hold one RX consumer span and predict remaining ring capacity. Explain why switching to timestamps, enhanced descriptors or a cached MCU requires a different memory/descriptor contract and inspected source scope.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.03.a:** Initialize bounded RX/TX rings in DMA-accessible memory using the selected actual controller contract.
- **T41.03.b:** Publish/reclaim descriptor and frame ownership with ordering, first/last and error checks.
- **T41.03.c:** Calculate the exposed frame length with padding and CRC handled exactly once and recover from unavailable buffers.

# PR-T41-04 — Untagged Ethernet and one-peer ARP state

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.04](#t41-04).

## Contract

Implement checked Ethernet II demultiplexing and the exact one-peer Ethernet/IPv4 ARP service. DA/SA are six octets, type is big-endian; allow local unicast and ARP broadcast, types 0x0800/0x0806. VLAN, foreign destination and unsupported type drop/counter. Hardware filtering does not remove software validation obligations.

ARP payload is 28 octets with htype 1, ptype 0x0800, hlen 6, plen 4, opcode 1/2. Require sender hardware address equals enclosing Ethernet SA and learn only configured peer 192.0.2.1. Cache expires after 30 s, holds one peer and at most one queued datagram. Requests occur at 0, 1000, 2000 ms; unresolved failure releases the pending datagram at 3000 ms.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture reconstructs exact ARP request/reply wire bytes, checks a sender-MAC mismatch, and derives cache validity at 29999 ms versus expiry at 30000 ms, request times and bounded failure cleanup. Its fixed peer/local MACs are 02:00:00:00:00:01 and 02:00:00:00:00:02. This finite serialization/cache oracle is not an Ethernet/ARP receive parser.

Create mandatory learner receive cases for wrong configured peer IP, htype/ptype/hlen/plen/opcode, truncated or inconsistent enclosing length, VLAN and foreign destination. Recompute each nested span before accessing it and assert no cache mutation or upper delivery on rejection.

Output parsed frame kind, cache publication/expiry, queued datagram outcome and exact reply bytes. Ethernet padding is ignored using ARP's declared fixed payload length; it is not extra ARP data.

## Steps

1. Parse enclosing 14-byte header before demultiplexing, then validate ARP field lengths before addresses.
2. Build exact broadcast request and local reply from field serialization, never native struct layout.
3. Implement one-entry cache, monotonic expiry and one queued datagram with BUSY on an additional submit.
4. Inject forged SA/sha, delayed reply, expiry and unresolved retry trace; check no invalid learn or silent queue overwrite.
5. Observe actual peer MAC on the isolated cable and capture request/reply; replace fixture-only peer identity in the lab record, not the supplied fixture.

## Failure cases

Foreign destination, unsupported type/VLAN, short frame, invalid ARP types/lengths/opcode, sender mismatch and nonpeer source cannot update cache. Expired association cannot send a queued packet without renewed resolution. A second queued datagram returns BUSY and remains caller-owned. ARP is unauthenticated; a valid association does not prove peer application identity.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit exact request/reply wire bytes, validation/drop matrix, timed cache/retry/queue logs and independent actual ARP capture. The objectives require field validation, bounded neighbor state and spoof/foreign/stale/unresolved outcomes. Show queue release on failure and distinguish Ethernet DA from IPv4 destination. Keep the original controlled-subset limits visible.

## Hints and recovery

If a reply parses but the next TCP frame goes elsewhere, compare Ethernet SA with ARP sender before cache write. If expiry depends on traffic count, use the injected monotonic clock. Do not solve unresolved peer by adding a broadcast TCP send.

## Transfer challenge

After a delay, predict the effect of a legitimate peer MAC change at cache expiry. Explain why a multi-peer table or address-conflict defense adds source and state obligations beyond this one-peer contract.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.04.a:** Validate the exact untagged Ethernet II and Ethernet/IPv4 ARP fields before dispatch or cache updates.
- **T41.04.b:** Resolve only the declared peer with bounded cache, queued datagram, retry and expiry state.
- **T41.04.c:** Explain and verify foreign-destination, spoofed-field, VLAN, stale-cache and unresolved-peer outcomes.

# PR-T41-05 — Fixed IPv4, odd-span checksums and exact Echo replies

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.05](#t41-05).

## Contract

Implement the selected IPv4 receive/emit and ICMP Echo subset above checked Ethernet. Receive version 4/IHL 5, bounded total 20..1500, positive TTL, correct header checksum, local destination/configured peer source and protocol 1/6. Reject options, MF or nonzero fragment offset and unknown protocol. Emit DF 1, MF 0, offset 0, ID 0, TTL 64. This intentionally omits full-host reassembly/options requirements; keep that limitation explicit.

ICMP Echo accepts type 8/code 0, valid checksum and 0..64 data octets; reply type 0 preserves id, sequence and payload. Implement reusable one's-complement checksum over byte spans, including odd final byte and TCP's IPv4 pseudo-header. Fold carries without overflowing the selected accumulator.

## Inputs and expected results

The supplied fixture uses five bytes hex 6162636465, Echo id 0x1234/seq 1 and peer/local 192.0.2.1/.2. Reply IP total is 33; Ethernet header+IP is 47, requiring 13 pad bytes before FCS for 64 minimum MAC frame. It recomputes exact emitted request/reply IP/ICMP bytes, checksums and padding, plus the odd final-byte checksum example. It does not execute the receive parser or establish fragment/options rejection.

Create mandatory learner receive cases with an invalid IP checksum, IHL other than 5, MF set and nonzero fragment offset, as well as the length/TTL/address/ICMP cases below. Assert the specific drop category and unchanged output sentinels. Include one valid packet with Ethernet padding and ensure only IPv4 total-length bytes reach ICMP.

Output verified/trimmed datagram spans, exact Echo reply bytes and drop categories. Do not checksum Ethernet padding as ICMP data; IPv4 total length bounds the nested message.

## Steps

1. Independently derive odd-span and end-around carry examples, then implement bounded checksum over one and split spans.
2. Parse fixed IPv4 fields and reject all length/flag/header mismatches before reading ICMP/TCP data.
3. Build the Echo reply from preserved fields and recomputed checksums; derive IP length/padding separately.
4. Inject each corruption, odd-length split, MF/nonzero offset and IHL 6. Keep all failed output sentinels unchanged.
5. Run actual default 56-byte ping on the isolated link and compare peer capture bytes with your target output; record host offload/capture settings.

## Failure cases

Truncated or inconsistent length, TTL 0, wrong destination/source, invalid checksum, fragmented/options packet, nonzero Echo code and payload over 64 drop without reply/publication. Receiving a checksummed IPv4 header never bypasses ICMP/TCP checksum validation. A checksum result from a host RAM fixture cannot establish hardware CRC or electrical integrity.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit the independent checksum/length worksheet, exact reply wire bytes, odd/split-span tests, invalid-case counters and actual Echo capture. The three objectives require fixed-header validation, one's-complement/pseudo-header arithmetic and exact Echo plus omitted-requirement evidence. Show the same data is returned unchanged and that receive padding is trimmed exactly once. Successful ping remains lower-layer evidence, not TCP/HTTP acceptance.

## Hints and recovery

If only odd-length messages fail, inspect whether the final byte became 0xXX00 and whether carries were repeatedly folded. If ICMP checksum differs by the padding amount, audit nested total length. If a packet with options seems parseable, still enforce the declared IHL 5 subset and record the omitted host requirement.

## Transfer challenge

Change Echo payload to the maximum 64 octets and compare padding/checksum behavior. Then identify what a general-host fragmentation extension would need to store, time out and validate before accepting it.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.05.a:** Parse bounded fixed IPv4 headers and verify total length, flags, destination and header checksum.
- **T41.05.b:** Compute one’s-complement checksums across odd spans and the TCP pseudo-header without undefined arithmetic.
- **T41.05.c:** Reply to the exact ICMP echo subset and expose fragment/option omissions as restricted-profile limitations.

# PR-T41-06 — Passive TCP with wrap, overlap, reset and close traces

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.06](#t41-06).

## Contract

Implement one passive connection on 8080 with MSS 256 and checked options. Use exact tuple/header/checksum/window validation, modulo 2^32 predicates with live spans<2^31 and SYN/FIN consumption of one sequence number. A pure ACK consumes none. Reject ACK beyond SND.NXT before releasing any output; guard accepted window updates with SND.WL1/WL2.

Accept only admissible in-order bytes, trim old prefixes, ACK duplicates and drop gaps with duplicate ACK. Validate FIN's position before consuming it. Exact-RCV.NXT RST aborts; unequal in-window RST produces a challenge ACK, outside-window drops. Trace all declared passive/close states and 240 s TIME-WAIT, including repeated FIN timer restart. No active/simultaneous open, arbitrary reordering queue, urgent processing or general-host conformance is claimed.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture starts peer SYN 0xfffffff0/localISN 1000. Sixteen bytes at 0xfffffff1 advance RCV.NXT to 1; identical repeat adds none. Twelve bytes at 0xfffffff9 contain an eight-byte old prefix and four new bytes, advancing to 5. A gap is dropped, unsent ACK 1002 when SND.NXT 1001 is rejected, and FIN at 5 advances to 6/CLOSE-WAIT. Local FIN 1001 and matching ACK 1002 complete LAST-ACK.

Expected accepted stream is the 20 octets abcdefghijklmnopqrst, with exact ACK/state list. Additional close/reset table covers simultaneous close, TIME-WAIT/repeated FIN and reset categories. Window guards use the same modular ordering: with WL1=WL2=0xfffffff0, updates (seq=0x10, ack=0xfffffff0) and (seq=0xfffffff0, ack=0x10) are both newer and accepted under the declared half-range assumption.

## Steps

1. First 4 h: implement header/checksum/options bounds, MSS negotiation and LISTEN/SYN-RECEIVED/ESTABLISHED with one retained SYN-ACK.
2. Next 4 h: derive circular intervals and run duplicate/overlap/gap/unsent-ACK traces, including stale window update guards and 512-byte capacity.
3. Final 4 h: implement half-close, active/passive/simultaneous close, RST and virtual 240 s TIME-WAIT. A peer FIN never completes an unfinished HTTP body.
4. Collect actual handshake/data/close packets from an independent client. Test a split/coalesced stream that crosses the sequence wrap in host fixtures; physical ISNs use recorded isolated-lab incarnation policy.
5. Inspect the state ledger against the selected RFC9293 branches and maintain an omitted-event matrix.

## Failure cases

Malformed option length, bad checksum/tuple/header, urgent/SYN-data subset exclusions, ACK of unsent bytes, out-of-window content and stale window updates have no unauthorized publication/free. Trimming duplicates cannot trim new tail bytes or count FIN twice. An RST is abort, not EOF; a local reset must flush owned queues without falsely acknowledging application delivery.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit option/handshake and modular arithmetic witnesses, exact accepted stream/ACK states, reset/half-close/simultaneous-close/TIME-WAIT logs and actual capture. For the objectives show passive setup, duplicate-safe stream and every declared close/reset distinction. The supplied finite oracle checks the worked trace; your C transition tests must cover all listed states, including scenarios not contained in that one trace.

## Hints and recovery

If wrap breaks comparison, draw a small ring and state interval length before using 32 bits. If duplicate data reappears, log original sequence and trimmed prefix. If half-close seems like an empty HTTP body, inspect the parser's independently required framing completion.

## Transfer challenge

Repeat with local active close and peer FIN before local FIN ACK. Predict CLOSING→TIME-WAIT and when its timer restarts; explain why shortening physical TIME-WAIT to speed a host test would change the contract.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.06.a:** Implement passive handshake, MSS parsing and modular sequence/ACK validation for the declared one-connection profile.
- **T41.06.b:** Preserve exactly the accepted in-order byte stream under duplicates, prefix overlap and packet segmentation.
- **T41.06.c:** Trace FIN, peer half-close, simultaneous close, reset and TIME-WAIT without treating them as HTTP framing.

# PR-T41-07 — RTO estimation, one-flight pressure and zero-window probes

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.07](#t41-07).

## Contract

Implement timers and bounded sending around the established TCP state. Initial/minimum RTO is 1000 ms, maximum cap 60000 ms, estimates follow RFC6298 update order and ambiguous retransmitted RTT samples are ignored. Retransmit earliest unacknowledged segment, double RTO after timeout and abort after three retransmissions under the original resource policy. SYN timeout makes post-handshake initial data RTO at least 3000 ms.

Keep one unacknowledged segment no larger than effective MSS and usable peer window, with conservative fixed cwnd 1 MSS. Retain immutable TCP bytes after DMA completes. Local RX window follows actual storage and reopens only as parser consumption frees space. Zero-window probes begin at current RTO and back off without duplicating or consuming another application byte.

## Inputs and expected results

The fixture samples RTT 80 then 120 ms: SRTT 80/85, RTTVAR 40/40 and clamped RTO 1000 both. A marked retransmitted sample is ignored. Timeout trace sends again at 1000, 3000, 7000 ms then aborts at 15000 ms; RTO cap and SYN-loss floor are separately checked. Flow input distinguishes peer window zero, outstanding flight and opening 256 window. A wrapped flight with SND.UNA 0xfffffff0, SND.NXT 0x10 and window 40 has 32 outstanding octets and 8 usable; it permits no new data under this one-outstanding-segment policy.

Outputs include estimator values, timer origins/deadlines, emitted/retransmitted byte intervals, probe events, ACK-freed storage, usable window and abort cleanup. The oracle checks finite mathematics and events, not production network behavior.

## Steps

1. First 4 h: derive first/second RTT calculations and implement estimator with checked clock/duration arithmetic. Update RTTVAR using the old SRTT.
2. Next 4 h: implement timer start/stop/restart and three-retransmission cleanup. Inject ACK just before/at deadline and never accept a retransmitted RTT sample.
3. Final 4 h: hold peer window zero and local parser consumption, verify probes, reopen update and exact pending bytes. Exercise stale window update guard from the previous milestone.
4. On the isolated cable, use a declared independent peer tool to withhold ACKs/advertise zero then reopen; record captures and actual elapsed times.
5. Compare your policy against the selected congestion passage and list absent growth/fast-recovery/general-event behavior.

## Failure cases

Queueing BUSY without actual send does not start RTO. Invalid ACK frees nothing. Duplicate/old window update cannot release a blocked sender. No new data exceeds peer window/cwnd or becomes a second outstanding flight. Ambiguous RTT and clock wrap/overflow are rejected/handled by the declared clock interface. Abort releases owned buffers and reports failure, not graceful delivery.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain independent weighted-mean/backoff calculations, every timer transition, zero-window/probe/reopen bytes and actual peer capture if available. The objectives require admissible samples/backoff, capacity/window/no-loss behavior and explicit conservative/full-host comparison. Show DMA completion precedes but does not substitute for valid ACK. A throughput benchmark alone cannot establish these invariants.

## Hints and recovery

If RTO differs on the second sample, update variance before SRTT and apply the 1 s minimum afterward. If probes advance application offset, separate probe sequence handling from new-data consumption. If retransmission data changes, audit immutable retained bytes and their owner.

## Transfer challenge

Use a 600 ms first sample then a longer second sample and independently recompute estimates; test a backed-off value beyond 60000. Explain which conditions would require general congestion algorithms rather than increasing this profile's flight count ad hoc.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.07.a:** Update retransmission estimates and backoff using only admissible RTT samples and an injected monotonic clock.
- **T41.07.b:** Enforce peer usable window, local capacity, zero-window probes and one outstanding segment without byte loss.
- **T41.07.c:** Compare conservative lab behavior with unimplemented general-host congestion/event requirements and record its limits.

# PR-T41-08 — Shared HTTP core over custom TCP and measured cable closure

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | E |

**Teaching module:** [T41](#t41).

**Covered topics:** [T41.08](#t41-08).

## Contract

Reuse the original portable T42.02–T42.05 parser/framing/chunk/serializer core, without charging those projects here again. This milestone owns the embedded stream adapter, custom-stack interoperability and physical/fault closure. Configure one connection, queue depth 1, one request, Connection: close. Preserve T42's grammar, body/chunk/trailer limits, target/Host and rejection policies. GET/HEAD /health use representation hex 6f6b0a; POST /echo returns identical bounded binary bytes.

Feed only accepted ordered TCP prefixes; retain unconsumed bytes and output offsets. ACK transport bytes retained safely independently of complete HTTP parsing. Keep response immutable for segmentation/retry, send FIN only after all response bytes are acknowledged and stop interpreting trailing optimistic requests after close/error. Configure authority 192.0.2.2:8080 for this adapter; use the hosted profile's declared loopback authority there. Change only configuration/callbacks, never disable Host or absolute-target authority validation.

## Inputs and expected results

Use this milestone's adapter fixture and shared [fixed-order wire fixture](fixtures/network_http/09_wire.json). Shared epoch 1672531200 gives Sun, 01 Jan 2023 00:00:00 GMT Date in the exact supplied format; field order is an original fixture policy. Expected GET body length 3, HEAD metadata length 3/body 0 and binary echo match T42. Segment/rejoin the exact response at effective MSS/window without changing a byte.

The adapter fixture deliberately provides host traces without measured hardware closure and therefore expects pending physical. Fixed epoch 1672531200 is fixture-only. Actual Date uses a recorded reasonable UTC callback/initialized clock separate from monotonic TCP time; if unavailable, omit Date under RFC9110's inspected rule and disclose that response variant. Compare actual response semantics and its declared Date variant rather than calling the historical golden date current. Output stream/response bytes, packet/ACK/state trace and separate genuine hardware evidence index.

## Steps

1. Spend first 4 h attaching consume/produce/capacity callbacks and injected clocks to the existing portable core. Test arbitrary TCP segmentation and coalescing of header/body/chunks.
2. Compare exact response with the shared wire oracle and test short output, retained retry bytes, malformedTE+CL and premature peer FIN.
3. Remaining 6 h: collect independent ARP,ping,handshake,GET/HEAD/POST,response and close captures from the actual board/link.
4. Inject loss, zero window/reopen, cable removal/recovery and board reset. Identify the first failed boundary and old/new incarnation; preserve declaredTIME-WAIT behavior.
5. Publish original-code ownership, resource/exclusion matrix and all 24topic evidence items for this family. Link reused T42 evidence rather than copying its hours.

## Failure cases

TE+CL/ambiguous framing, incomplete body/chunk/trailer and parser limit violations cannot publish partial application success. Peer half-close does not complete body framing. Unsent or invalidly ACKed response bytes cannot be freed. After error/close, trailing requests are never dispatched. Link down aborts the old incarnation; a new cable link does not magically finish an old request.

## Acceptance and evidence

Retain exact shared response/adapter tests, independent real packet captures, measured PHY/RMII/driver evidence from earlier milestones and cable/reset/fault records. For the objectives show unchanged portable HTTP semantics, independent selected-protocol interoperability and actual physical/incarnation closure. A TAP/canned pcap/emulator can supply useful host evidence but cannot replace any physical gate. State full-host omissions even after the cooperative client succeeds.

## Hints and recovery

If the body loses bytes at packet edges, inspect consume counts and leftover spans before altering HTTP grammar. If final response disappears on close, wait for valid ACKs before FIN and preserve output ownership. If a host capture shows unusual checksums, record offload/capture position before blaming the wire.

## Transfer challenge

After a delay, replay a legal chunked binary echo and an incomplete half-close with different packet splits. Explain why TLS or a second concurrent connection would require new security/resource/state contracts rather than merely a changed port.

For this milestone, retain three separately labeled evidence items:

- **T41.08.a:** Attach the previously verified T42 HTTP core through an adapter that preserves stream bytes and bounded ownership.
- **T41.08.b:** Verify ARP, echo, handshake, HTTP response, loss, zero-window and close traces with an independent peer.
- **T41.08.c:** Close actual cable-loss/recovery and board reset-incarnation evidence without counting simulated packets as L1 success.

# PR-T42-01 — Owned socket lifecycle

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T42](#t42).

**Covered topics:** [T42.01](#t42-01).

## Contract

Reuse the prior listener/event code; implement bounded records and their acquisition/release transitions. This is milestone1 of the hosted HTTP family. The shared contract is the supplied contract fixture; preserve its capacities, routes, body bytes and close behavior. The application owns the studied mechanism. The operating system supplies TCP/IP and the physical network. Reuse earlier C/ownership/Linux components and accepted evidence; this budget charges the new HTTP boundary work. No equivalent HTTP parser/server library may implement the target.

## Inputs and expected results

Use the accompanying finite fixture and shared contract. Its expected object is an oracle for the declared examples, not proof of every runtime path. The /health representation is exactly hex `6f6b0a`. Record consumed, retained, published and discarded octets separately. Match every listed status, length, ownership and timing result, and explain any environment-dependent evidence separately.

## Steps

1. Read the corresponding T42 topic and its assigned source locators; predict the fixture before coding.
2. State input preconditions, live storage, output ownership, error results and progress measure.
3. Reuse the prior listener/event code; implement bounded records and their acquisition/release transitions.
4. Observe listener flags and accepted flags; inject readiness races and the fifth concurrent connection.
5. Compare the smallest observed trace with the independent fixture calculation and preserve the first disagreement.
6. Audit component dependencies, record actual commands/versions and retain separate evidence for objectives a,b,c.

Trace accepted descriptors 11,12,13,14 into four slots. Descriptor 15 cannot acquire a slot and is closed. Releasing 12 allows 16 to enter; no reference to 12 may survive in a queued event. Add a generation number to distinguish a recycled descriptor number from the old connection. Record this invariant: every live descriptor has one owner and every published record has a valid descriptor. A readable listener does not guarantee a successful accept, and an open socket does not establish an HTTP session. Evidence includes flag inspection, an accept-race trace, injected exhaustion, resource counters and an explicit layer-ownership map.

## Failure cases

Include empty input, every relevant incomplete prefix, malformed syntax, exact capacity and one beyond capacity. Exercise error then retry/cleanup, pending output and a later event referring to a recycled descriptor. For a portable parser, no failure may publish a partial request or retain a span after its owner releases storage. For an adapter, no failure may leak a descriptor, advance an unsent offset or claim peer consumption from local send success.

## Acceptance and evidence

Observe listener flags and accepted flags; inject readiness races and the fifth concurrent connection. Run the saved Python fixture verifier, then execute the learner's original C against these and independently added counterexamples. Retain a per-objective checklist, dependency/symbol audit, byte/state trace and memory/descriptor ledger. A successful static oracle does not establish actual parser, socket, hardware or full HTTP conformance. Explain the selected RFC requirement, any stricter project policy and every omitted capability independently.

## Hints and recovery

Reduce a failing exchange to one request, one state and one split point. Compare the promised consumed offset and ownership before adding logging. Keep the raw input immutable for diagnosis. If the oracle disagrees, recompute byte lengths or deadline arithmetic independently before changing expected data. Return to the corresponding entry foundation when the defect is a pointer lifetime, integer overflow, partial-I/O or event-ownership mistake.

## Transfer challenge

After a delay, change one split, capacity, connection-generation or time boundary and predict the outcome from the contract. Demonstrate which evidence survives and which must be regenerated. Carry the portable HTTP core into T41 only after parser/serializer gates pass; its original implementation hours remain here, while T41 pays for its different transport adapter and physical closure.

For a GET header ending at offset 46, feed prefixes of lengths 0 through 46. Every proper prefix reports NEED_MORE with no complete request; the final LF completes the header once. Feeding two headers in one span completes only the first and returns its consumed length, leaving the second unchanged. Absolute-form http://localhost:8080/health selects authority localhost:8080, even if the syntactically valid single Host says other.example. Origin-form uses the single Host. Validate bounded configured host/port authorities; do not implement filesystem normalization. Missing/duplicate/malformed HTTP/1.1 Host returns 400 and close. A complete header is not yet a complete body. Retain split/coalescing, target-authority and smallest malformed-octet evidence.

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |

**Teaching module:** [T42](#t42).

## Contract

Add occurrence-counted normalized fields and checked framing selection, then consume the exact selected body. This is milestone3 of the hosted HTTP family. The shared contract is the supplied contract fixture; preserve its capacities, routes, body bytes and close behavior. The application owns the studied mechanism. The operating system supplies TCP/IP and the physical network. Reuse earlier C/ownership/Linux components and accepted evidence; this budget charges the new HTTP boundary work. ## Inputs and expected results

Use the accompanying finite fixture and shared contract. Its expected object is an oracle for the declared examples, not proof of every runtime path. The /health representation is exactly hex `6f6b0a`. Record consumed, retained, published and discarded octets separately. Match every listed status, length, ownership and timing result, and explain any environment-dependent evidence separately.

## Steps

1. Read the corresponding T42 topic and its assigned source locators; predict the fixture before coding.
2. State input preconditions, live storage, output ownership, error results and progress measure.
3. Add occurrence-counted normalized fields and checked framing selection, then consume the exact selected body.
4. Inject every framing-table case and EOF at each Content-Length prefix; preserve the following message unchanged.
5. Compare the smallest observed trace with the independent fixture calculation and preserve the first disagreement.
6. Audit component dependencies, record actual commands/versions and retain separate evidence for objectives a,b,c.

Derive a checked decimal accumulation condition before each multiply/add using the declared maximum 4294967295. Then apply the 1024-byte body cap. An overflowing numeral is 400; a representable declared body above the cap is 413. Identical duplicate Content-Length is conservatively400+close. TE+CL is always400+close, rather than choosing whichever parser seems convenient. Check syntax and framing before unsupported decoding: a request whose final coding is not chunked is 400+close. Thus gzip alone and chunked,gzip are 400. Repeated chunked, malformed token lists and chunked parameters are 400. A valid gzip,chunked list is framed but requires an unsupported decoder, so it is 501+close. The declared strict profile rejects other parameterized coding lists with 400; this is a syntax-subset policy. For LENGTH 5 and input abcdeGET..., consume exactly five body octets; GET belongs to the next message. Premature EOF after four bytes is incomplete and cannot dispatch a successful echo. Produce the framing-decision table, byte-conservation ledger and overflow counterexamples.

# PR-T42-04 — Chunk decoder with separate trailers

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T42](#t42).

**Covered topics:** [T42.04](#t42-04).

## Contract

Implement chunk-size, extension, data-CRLF and trailer states with independent caps. This is milestone4 of the hosted HTTP family. The shared contract is the supplied contract fixture; preserve its capacities, routes, body bytes and close behavior. The application owns the studied mechanism. The operating system supplies TCP/IP and the physical network. Reuse earlier C/ownership/Linux components and accepted evidence; this budget charges the new HTTP boundary work. No equivalent HTTP parser/server library may implement the target.

## Inputs and expected results

Use the accompanying finite fixture and shared contract. Its expected object is an oracle for the declared examples, not proof of every runtime path. The /health representation is exactly hex `6f6b0a`. Record consumed, retained, published and discarded octets separately. Match every listed status, length, ownership and timing result, and explain any environment-dependent evidence separately.

## Steps

1. Read the corresponding T42 topic and its assigned source locators; predict the fixture before coding.
2. State input preconditions, live storage, output ownership, error results and progress measure.
3. Implement chunk-size, extension, data-CRLF and trailer states with independent caps.
4. Split at every byte, corrupt each delimiter, exceed each cap and verify no partial body publication.
5. Compare the smallest observed trace with the independent fixture calculation and preserve the first disagreement.
6. Audit component dependencies, record actual commands/versions and retain separate evidence for objectives a,b,c.

Trace 3;x=y CRLF abc CRLF 2 CRLF de CRLF 0 CRLF X-Debug: ignored CRLF CRLF. The representation is the five octets abcde. The zero-size chunk ends data but does not finish the message until the trailer section's final empty line. A CR split across reads is still pending state, not an optional delimiter. The supplied invalid trace puts X where the data-ending CR belongs and returns 400+close; the incomplete trace has no terminal empty line and publishes no body. Check every byte split, extension/trailer capacities and EOF in every state. Keep decoded content separate from wire byte counts; the wire overhead is not echoed.

## Failure cases

Include empty input, every relevant incomplete prefix, malformed syntax, exact capacity and one beyond capacity. Exercise error then retry/cleanup, pending output and a later event referring to a recycled descriptor. For a portable parser, no failure may publish a partial request or retain a span after its owner releases storage. For an adapter, no failure may leak a descriptor, advance an unsent offset or claim peer consumption from local send success.

## Acceptance and evidence

Split at every byte, corrupt each delimiter, exceed each cap and verify no partial body publication. Run the saved Python fixture verifier, then execute the learner's original C against these and independently added counterexamples. Retain a per-objective checklist, dependency/symbol audit, byte/state trace and memory/descriptor ledger. A successful static oracle does not establish actual parser, socket, hardware or full HTTP conformance. Explain the selected RFC requirement, any stricter project policy and every omitted capability independently.

## Hints and recovery

Reduce a failing exchange to one request, one state and one split point. Compare the promised consumed offset and ownership before adding logging. Keep the raw input immutable for diagnosis. If the oracle disagrees, recompute byte lengths or deadline arithmetic independently before changing expected data. Return to the corresponding entry foundation when the defect is a pointer lifetime, integer overflow, partial-I/O or event-ownership mistake.

## Transfer challenge

After a delay, change one split, capacity, connection-generation or time boundary and predict the outcome from the contract. Demonstrate which evidence survives and which must be regenerated. Carry the portable HTTP core into T41 only after parser/serializer gates pass; its original implementation hours remain here, while T41 pays for its different transport adapter and physical closure.

# PR-T42-06 — Persistent output and close state

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 h | core | A |

**Teaching module:** [T42](#t42).

**Covered topics:** [T42.06](#t42-06).

## Contract

Attach immutable output and FIFO request records to the socket adapter, then stage closure. This is milestone6 of the hosted HTTP family. The shared contract is the supplied contract fixture; preserve its capacities, routes, body bytes and close behavior. The application owns the studied mechanism. The operating system supplies TCP/IP and the physical network. Reuse earlier C/ownership/Linux components and accepted evidence; this budget charges the new HTTP boundary work. No equivalent HTTP parser/server library may implement the target.

## Inputs and expected results

Use the accompanying finite fixture and shared contract. Its expected object is an oracle for the declared examples, not proof of every runtime path. The /health representation is exactly hex `6f6b0a`. Record consumed, retained, published and discarded octets separately. Match every listed status, length, ownership and timing result, and explain any environment-dependent evidence separately.

## Steps

1. Read the corresponding T42 topic and its assigned source locators; predict the fixture before coding.
2. State input preconditions, live storage, output ownership, error results and progress measure.
3. Attach immutable output and FIFO request records to the socket adapter, then stage closure.
4. Force the short-send script, two-entry queue pressure and close followed by apparent pipeline bytes.
5. Compare the smallest observed trace with the independent fixture calculation and preserve the first disagreement.
6. Audit component dependencies, record actual commands/versions and retain separate evidence for objectives a,b,c.

Persistent responses remain FIFO even if their computation costs differ. Root owns this family authorship."

# PR-T43-01 — A cost contract before a stopwatch

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T43](#t43).

**Covered topics:** [T43.01](#t43-01), [T43.02](#t43-02).

## Contract

Extend the accepted [T15 sorting milestone](#pr-t15-01) with a counter adapter and an analysis sheet. Reuse its insertion kernel; do not rebuild the sort family. Count only key comparisons, shifts of existing records and final placements in this contract. Loop predicates, loading the key, allocation and harness setup are separate work. Preserve the original stable ordering and error contracts. No qsort, bsearch or library routine may perform the educational mechanism.

Spend 5 hours implementing the adapter and 3 verifying traces/proofs. Define n as the number of valid records, state the represented key width, and distinguish an exact cost on a particular input from the maximum over inputs of size n. The adapter's counters must have a checked range; silent wrapping invalidates the experiment.

## Inputs and expected results

[The fixture](fixtures/performance/PR-T43-01.json) includes [4,2,5,2,1,4]. There are 8 inverted pairs, so exactly 8 shifts; 11 key comparisons and 5 final placements give 13 destination writes. The six reverse keys give 15 comparisons and 15 shifts, while equal keys give 5 comparisons and no shifts. Empty input performs neither placements nor reads.

For the separate exact function 3n²+5n+7, prove 3n²≤f(n)≤15n² for every integer n≥1. Finite anchors check the arithmetic; they do not prove the quantifier. A separate output-sensitive work contract is 3V+2E+Z with V=4,E=5,Z=3, giving 25 units.

## Steps

1. Record the accepted prior revision and label each counted event at its semantic point; show one handwritten record-by-record trace before running C.
2. Compare C counts with the independent inversion-pair certificate. Add one input with duplicates in a different order and one maximum permitted size.
3. Write the bound with constants c₁=3,c₂=15,n₀=1 and the inequalities that justify the upper bound. Give the multi-parameter O(V+E+Z) statement and account for output production.
4. Use f(n)=n for n≤128 and n² afterwards to defeat a linear slope claim from samples 2,4,8,16. Test 130; 16900 is outside the apparent linear trend.

## Failure cases

Reject invalid spans before touching records. Preserve the prior failure result and counter status. An overflowed counter is unavailable, not a plausible small measurement. A deliberately weakened shift predicate must fail the stability/count evidence. Do not call every O(n²) upper bound a tight bound on sorted input; the chosen kernel's best case is linear.

## Acceptance and evidence

Submit six separate items: .01.a input/case contract; .01.b independently traced count vector; .01.c a three-column work/instruction/static-CFG distinction; .02.a the quantified algebraic proof; .02.b the V/E/Z input-output bound; .02.c the finite-slope counterexample. Include the prior accepted binary/source identity and actual C count results. The Python oracle certifies the original finite counts only. It supplies neither an asymptotic proof nor timing evidence.

## Hints and recovery

A key comparison that stops the scan counts even though it causes no shift. Compare shifts with inverted pairs to find an off-by-one counter. If the count adapter changes output, restore the accepted kernel and isolate the instrumentation. For the upper inequality use n≤n² and 1≤n² once n≥1; no regression fit is needed.

## Transfer challenge

Apply the same contract discipline to an already accepted graph traversal: name V, stored edges and emitted output Z separately. Supply a tiny work ledger rather than writing a second graph implementation. Predict which counts would change if parallel edges were retained.

# PR-T43-02 — Prefix credits for a reused growing table

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T43](#t43).

**Covered topics:** [T43.03](#t43-03).

## Contract

Reuse the failure-preserving [dynamic array](#pr-t14-02). Add a ledger for twelve successful appends starting empty and doubling capacity when full; unit costs are one insertion plus one copy per existing element. This milestone implements the certificate and observes the existing callbacks, not a new allocator or container. The supplied hosted harness may provide genuine allocated storage; a declared unsigned-char array is not typeless storage for arbitrary typed lvalue access in C17. Alignment alone does not settle effective type.

Use 4 hours implementation and 2 verification. Keep failed acquisition outside the successful-sequence bound and retain the existing unchanged-state acceptance check for failure.

## Inputs and expected results

[The fixture](fixtures/performance/PR-T43-02.json) costs 1,2,3,1,5,1,1,1,9,1,1,1: 27 total units, 15 copies and 12 insertions. Charge 3 per append; the final credit is 36−27=9 and every prefix credit is nonnegative. With Φ=2·live−capacity, Φ₀=0 and Φ₁₂=8, the sum of amortized costs is 27+8=35≤36. The first amortized charge is 2; subsequent ones are 3.

At growth from capacity 8 to 16, coexistence requires 24 four-byte slots, or 96 bytes. Final capacity is 64 bytes and live payload 48 bytes. This transient space is separate from a claim about allocator internals.

## Steps

1. Annotate each accepted append with before/after live count, capacity, copies and acquisition outcome. Compare with the twelve literal fixture rows.
2. Compute running actual cost, credit 3k−Σcᵢ and potential after every prefix. Check Σĉᵢ=Σcᵢ+Φₖ−Φ₀, not merely the final total.
3. Inject the prior allocation-failure case; show unchanged pointer/count/capacity and distinguish it from the successful trace.
4. Repeat the worksheet from a declared nonempty initial state. Retain Φ₀ in the telescoping equation; an arbitrary initial state cannot silently borrow the empty-table proof.

## Failure cases

Reject inconsistent count/capacity snapshots and arithmetic overflow. Negative credit disproves the proposed charging scheme under that initial state. A long single growth operation remains expensive even when the sequence average is bounded. Shrink, concurrent mutation, allocator latency and destruction are outside this expansion-only model and must not inherit its guarantee.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .a provide the exact sequence, largest actual cost 9 and total 27. For .b submit all prefix credit/potential rows and the initial-state variant. For .c state that this is a deterministic worst-case sequence guarantee under unit-copy assumptions, not an expectation over random arrivals. Attach actual prior-table callback/count traces and the preserved failure case. The independent oracle verifies these finite rows and transient payload capacity, not the implementation's allocator time or total process memory.

## Hints and recovery

When a doubling append changes live m to m+1 and capacity m to 2m, the potential change pays for copying m elements. Treat the very first allocation separately. If your potential row differs from the fixture, inspect whether you recorded the state before rather than after insertion. Count old and new capacity concurrently during acquisition.

## Transfer challenge

Compare the same accepted table with a fixed-increment growth policy on paper. Derive a sequence-cost counterexample before considering a policy change. Do not charge the container implementation a second time in this module.

# PR-T43-03 — Instructions, graph cycles and a constrained decision

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T43](#t43).

**Covered topics:** [T43.04](#t43-04), [T43.14](#t43-14).

## Contract

Reuse the callable x86-64/Thumb [lower-bound kernels](#pr-t36-02) and the existing [architecture measurement ledger](#pr-t37-08). Add an executed-instruction count/cost worksheet for one bounded path, two tiny control-flow graphs and a multi-measure acceptance decision. Do not rebuild the paired assembly implementation or equate an emulator's instruction execution with silicon time.

Spend 5 hours extending the adapters and 3 verifying the ledger. Code-size and retained-storage limits are hard constraints; the fastest candidate is acceptable only if it meets them. Complete the final decision dossier after the later measurement projects, within this milestone's reserved verification work.

## Inputs and expected results

[The synthetic fixture](fixtures/performance/PR-T43-03.json) executes 100 instructions at model CPI 1, 40 at 2 and 20 at 4. Thus IC=160, cycles=260, weighted CPI=1.625. At 100 MHz, one cycle is 10 ns and modeled time is 2600 ns.

Both connected function graphs have six nodes and seven edges, so v=e−n+2=3. Their declared sequential versus nested bodies execute 2n versus n² times: 16 versus 64 at n=8. Graph cycles are a static test/design metric. They are neither processor cycles nor an asymptotic bound. Variant B's 240 model cycles beat A's 260, but B's 256 code bytes/96 retained bytes exceed limits 200/80. A's 128/64 fit.

## Steps

1. Take one accepted assembly path and count actual executed instructions from a trace. Record ISA, ABI, input, build and taken branches; a disassembly listing alone is not an executed count.
2. Recompute the fixture's weighted model with units. Contrast it with the accepted native or silicon measurement, including an observed residual and possible working-set effect. Calculate a bounded Amdahl estimate with a declared affected fraction; label it a model.
3. Draw the two original CFGs, retain the connected-entry/exit convention, and explain their equal static v despite different loop work. Do not claim every algebraic basis path is executable.
4. Build a decision table containing model/work counts, observed time or unavailability, code bytes, retained storage, traffic and jitter evidence from later projects. Declare why energy or an event was omitted.

## Failure cases

Reject an unknown edge endpoint, disconnected node or duplicate edge in this scoped graph certificate. Unit errors such as treating 100 MHz as 100 ns per cycle fail the gate. Do not substitute an assumed one-cycle cost for a missing measurement. Mark a unsupported measurement unavailable rather than assigning zero. Static branch predicates may have infeasible combinations.

## Acceptance and evidence

Supply separate .04.a instruction-mix evidence, .04.b dimensional model/speedup/residual evidence and .04.c code/branch/CFG vector. For .14.a give the requirement and justified chosen/omitted observables; for .14.b resolve the faster-but-too-large case and one actual reused-kernel tradeoff; for .14.c freeze an evidence ledger labeling algebraic proof, finite oracle, actual runtime and conditional hardware evidence. Reuse prior measurements without claiming this synthetic 260-cycle model matches either target.

## Hints and recovery

Start with the time identity IC×CPI/f and cancel units before inserting numbers. Draw the CFG before counting edges. A same-v pair is an effective counterexample to using cyclomatic complexity as a speed predictor. If no faster variant meets the constraints, keeping the baseline is a valid decision with evidence.

## Transfer challenge

Change one constraint and predict the selected candidate. Then ask whether a bus-byte or observed jitter limit overturns it. An energy comparison requires a named meter/model and boundary; time×an invented constant power is not evidence.

# PR-T43-04 — Simultaneous storage and a conditional stack certificate

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T43](#t43).

**Covered topics:** [T43.05](#t43-05).

## Contract

Instrument the ownership boundaries of the accepted [span component](#pr-t18-01) and reuse the [stack-budget dossier](#pr-t13-02). Produce a timestamped allocation/liveness ledger and parse one actual GCC -fstack-usage build. This is an adapter and accounting task; do not write another allocator or move a typed object into a byte arena to simplify the report. Keep caller-owned, allocated and borrowed objects distinct.

Use 5 hours implementation and 3 verification. Each owned object appears once. Lifetimes are half-open intervals, so a release at time t removes the object before the state at t is counted.

## Inputs and expected results

[The fixture](fixtures/performance/PR-T43-04.json) has work capacity 128/live 64, scratch 80/80 and result 96/24. Live peak is 144 at time 3, whereas allocated capacity peaks at 224 at time 7. At time 10, work is retained with no live payload: retained peak 128. Active slack peaks at 136 at time 7. These maxima occur in different states and must not be added into a fabricated simultaneous footprint.

Declared sections are text 512, rodata 64, data 32, bss 256 bytes: the stated Flash layout uses 608 bytes, and RAM sections use 288. A main/work/leaf path sums to 96 bytes; main/other is 112. With a stipulated nonnested 24-byte interrupt allowance, the known-path bound is 136. Unknown calls and recurrence have no finite certified bound here.

## Steps

1. Record ownership identity, capacity, currently meaningful payload, acquisition/release and live interval. Recompute every event boundary, then maximum each category separately.
2. Generate actual .su records from the reused component with build flags/ABI identity. Interpret static, dynamic,bounded and dynamic qualifiers. Trace feasible simultaneous call paths rather than summing all function maxima.
3. Record actual section sizes and a sampled watermark if available. State which RAM sections, stack, heap/resident pages and allocator metadata overlap or remain unobserved.
4. Add one indirect unknown call or unbounded dynamic frame to the certificate and preserve the unknown result. A successful shallow test does not resolve it.

## Failure cases

Duplicate ownership, inverted intervals and live bytes beyond capacity fail the ledger. Unknown recursion depth cannot be bounded by the maximum observed depth. An interrupt allowance is valid only under its declared nesting/preemption contract. .bss size is static storage, not runtime retained heap. Process RSS/cgroup memory contain additional charged pages and cannot substitute for the object ledger.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .a submit the event table, distinct four peaks and a rejected double-counted example. For .b submit actual .su lines, a known path, an unresolved path and the watermark/section/accounting distinction. For .c report a symbolic space bound with separate target byte observations and unresolved allocator/callback/interrupt boundaries. The fixture oracle checks declared intervals and simple paths; it does not infer whole-program stack safety from compiler output.

## Hints and recovery

Sort the union of acquisition, liveness and release endpoints. At an endpoint count the state after events according to the half-open convention. Distinguish inactive retained capacity from unused slots in a still-live object. If .su changes under inlining/LTO, retain both build identities rather than merging incompatible frame numbers.

## Transfer challenge

Move scratch use so it overlaps result lifetime and predict the changed simultaneous peak. Demonstrate that a lower retained heap count can coexist with a larger stack frame; select the boundary relevant to the requirement.

# PR-T43-05 — Block traffic rather than a cache-time guess

| Budget | Disposition | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 h | core | C |

**Teaching module:** [T43](#t43).

**Covered topics:** [T43.06](#t43-06).

## Contract

Extend the accepted [cache reference worksheet](#pr-t37-05) with a separate single-disk external-memory certificate. Implement only a tiny bounded two-block LRU/write-back traffic adapter in original C, keeping its results separate from the prior direct-mapped CPU cache. No library cache/container routine may perform the educational policy. The harness may parse JSON and compare output externally.

Use 5 hours implementation and 3 verification. Fixed four-byte items, B=2 items and M=4 items give two eight-byte buffer blocks; D=P=1. This is a declared model with write allocation, dirty eviction and a final dirty flush. It makes no prediction of actual disk service time.

## Inputs and expected results

[The fixture](fixtures/performance/PR-T43-05.json) sequentially reads items 0..7: four block reads, 32 bytes transferred/useful and amplification 1. The mixed references read 0, write 1, read 4, write 0, read 2, write 4, read 5 read four blocks and write two: 32+16=48 transferred bytes for 28 useful bytes, amplification 12/7. The dirty block 0 is evicted; dirty block 2 remains for final flush.

For no references, useful and transferred bytes are both zero. Amplification is undefined, represented by null; 0/0 is not zero or one. A cyclic three-block read stream thrashes the two-block buffer: six reads/48 bytes for 24 useful bytes.

## Steps

1. Declare N as the backing sequence length in items, M and B in the same item units. Name the buffer layer and show each block number, resident order and dirty flag.
2. Extend the C adapter with counts of fetched/flushed blocks; verify final-flush handling and exact byte conversion against all original fixture cases.
3. Observe a bounded file read through the existing file adapter, preserving syscall accepted-byte counts and any permitted device-byte evidence. Compare a repeat/warm run without claiming a system cache flush.
4. Explain a discrepancy between useful bytes, userspace requests and device accounting. Buffering, readahead, writeback or a different layer are hypotheses to test, not invisible zero-cost transfers.

## Failure cases

Reject invalid indices, unknown read/write modes and geometry that violates the stated buffer contract. The empty stream must not divide by zero. A dirty hit does not write back immediately in this policy. A bus transaction, disk I/O and CPU cache fill can have different sizes; replacing one with another invalidates the unit label.

## Acceptance and evidence

For .a submit an original hand-traced stream and the N/M/B/D/P model contract. For .b submit all read/write/useful byte totals, ratios and null denominator case. For .c supply actual existing-adapter observations or a clearly labeled denied device-accounting boundary, plus a warm-state explanation and follow-up. The independent Python model checks the bounded policy, not C correctness on every stream or a physical device model.

## Hints and recovery

Use an ordered resident list oldest first; on a hit update recency without incrementing fetch count. Keep dirty identity independent of recency. Count final dirty writes exactly once. If your sequential ratio is below one, inspect whether useful-byte totals are counting repeated bytes while transfer counts refer to an already warm cache.

## Transfer challenge

Increase M to six items and predict the cyclic-stream counts before running. Compare the gain in traffic with additional retained storage; do not infer the same speedup for every device or asynchronous backend.
